## UA-P-4d — a foreign login at the gate: the second-account witness runs headless on a guest key (2026-09-20; `b4a61f23`, the lane's `25df8f9e` rebased over UA-P-0g; lane guestprobe)

**Why now.** The roadmap has owed "the two-account tailnet witness" since UA-4 — a colleague's login on the same tailnet seeing nothing of yours — and since UA-P-4 it has had something concrete to falsify (a colleague's desktop must never appear in the roster, never receive a slice, and be refused at the hello with 4004), but only a human on a second device could stand it up. UA-P-4's live row (`mesh_login_gate_probe.rs`) stands three ephemeral nodes on ONE auth key, so every node carries the same login and the only refusal it can show is a gate that matches nobody. This slice adds the node that key cannot buy: an auth key names its minter, so a fourth node built from a key the SECOND USER of the tailnet generated puts a genuinely foreign login on the tailnet from one machine.

**As built.** `common::GUEST_AUTHKEY_ENV = "TRUFFLE_TEST_AUTHKEY_GUEST"` beside the primary key; `build_node`/`build_gated_node` take their key as a parameter. The new `#[ignore]`d row `a_foreign_login_is_refused_at_the_gate_and_never_enters_it` SKIPS LOUDLY when the guest key is absent — one line naming the env var and what the key must be — and pins its preconditions before measuring anything: the guest login differs from the account's and is not `tagged-devices` (a tagged key would exercise the "caller has no login" row instead of "caller is someone else", and fieldd's own capture refuses such a node, `link-service.ts` `login_unavailable`); neither login is printed, only a verdict and a length. Then, each absence read in the same beat as the control that explains it: **roster** (RFC 025 §3.3) — the gated node never lists the guest within 4× the measured guest discovery (floor 30 s) while its ungated twin lists it, and the gated node still lists the twin; **the guest's own view** (§3.3) — the guest SEES the gated node, because the gate is admission and not invisibility, and the login it reports for that peer is asserted against what §3.3 promises (the owner's login from the netmap's user map, or absent, never fabricated); **slice** (§3.3 + §3.5) — neither direction crosses while three controls converge (guest→open, open→guest, gated→open); **hello** (§3.4) — the guest's dial is refused with close code 4004, asserted only after both positive controls (the account's own node admitted by that same gated listener; the guest admitted by an ungated one). The dial goes through the node's own session-plane listener, NOT a sidecar `serve` route: RFC 023 §9.7's `allow` list guards a serve and RFC 025 §3.7 says that is not the login gate, so a serve would have witnessed the wrong gate. A process-wide turn mutex makes the two live rows take turns (six sidecars and four discovery measurements at once would make every window a statement about load), taken after the skip checks so a keyless machine never queues. `.env.example` documents the guest key (name only). Errata corrected at their sources: the probe header and `build_gated_node`'s doc said the vendored npm sidecar was pre-RFC-025 and told the reader to set `FIELD_NATIVE_SIDECAR_PATH` — false since UA-P-X (the live run resolved this worktree's own vendored 0.7.14 with the override unset); `vendored_sidecar()`'s doc named `0.7.12` in prose — the number is deleted, the manifest is the authority.

**Witness.** `cargo fmt --check` · clippy `-D warnings` · `cargo test -p field-native` 263 passed / 9 ignored / 0 failed across 21 targets (the only count change: the probe binary's ignored rows 1 → 2) · the ignored run on the real tailnet with the guest key ABSENT: exit 0, 2 passed — the skip loud and named, the three-node row green as the regression control (ungated discovery 25 µs; the walled node holds 0 peers while the ungated node holds 2). **The live guest-key run is owed** to James's second tailnet user. Re-run by the orchestrator before landing: fmt, clippy, the probe compile and the key-absent ignored run — quoted in the docs commit.

**Findings.** (1) The typed refusal RFC 025 §4 promises the dialer does not reach `truffle_core::Node`'s public surface: `TransportError::HelloRefused { code, reason }` is typed at the transport boundary, then `PeerRegistry::ensure_ws_connected` folds every transport failure into `SessionError::ConnectFailed(String)` via `to_string()`, so a consumer who wants to tell "not my app" from "not my login" reads prose — the probe parses the code back out and fails closed; a petition row the day the floor needs to branch on the code. (2) Eager identity re-dials a refused peer with a per-peer backoff doubling to a 30 s cap, so a single `send_bytes` would often report truffle's own rate limiter, not the gate — the probe waits the window out and accepts only an admission or a code the remote sent. (3) A synced store subscribes inside the task it spawns and a lost broadcast is never retried — every store is created and given a beat before a write. (4) `Node` publishes no sidecar protocol version; the gated node's successful `build()` is the assertion (below 5 it refuses to start). (5) The main checkout's `.env` sets `FIELD_NATIVE_SIDECAR_PATH`, which outranks everything in `common::sidecar()`; byte-identical to the vendored 0.7.14 today (sha256 `9f10e84b…`), but a stale override there would silently decide which sidecar every tailnet probe exercises.

## UA-P-4d witness — the foreign login refused on the real tailnet, two human logins (2026-09-21; run by the orchestrator from the lane's worktree at `b4a61f23`)

James invited a second account to the tailnet (a plain Member cannot generate a key — Tailscale gates the Keys page to Owner/Admin/IT admin/Network admin, so the second account holds Admin for the duration) and minted its key into `.env` as `TRUFFLE_TEST_AUTHKEY_GUEST`. The ignored run, both rows, `cargo test -p field-native --test mesh_login_gate_probe -- --ignored --nocapture` against the vendored 0.7.14 sidecar: **`test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed`, 81 s.** The foreign-login row, in its own words: two distinct human logins, neither `tagged-devices`; the ungated node found the guest in 1.7 ms and its gated twin in 20 µs; the allowed login completed the hello with the gated listener and the guest completed one with an ungated node (both controls); **THE ROW: the gated node refused the guest — 4004 (login refused)**; slices converged guest→open, open→guest and gated→open (three controls); after the 30 s settle, in one beat: the gated node holds 1 peer and none of them is the guest while the ungated twin and the guest each hold 2; the ungated node holds the guest's AND the gated node's slice, the gated node holds no guest slice, the guest holds no gated slice. The three-node row ran after it as the regression control (walled node 0 peers against 2). **The two-account tailnet witness owed since UA-4 is PAID on the desktop plane**: a real other identity is refused at the hello, never enters the roster, and exchanges no slice, while the same gate admits the account's own login. Still owed on the phone plane: the phone signed in as the second login drawing no desktop (Phase 0's guest half, James's hands).

## AR-5-1 — the puppeteer pin moves to `2f5ce002`, and the gate is green again (2026-09-21; `d4e60d8d`, lane pin)

**Why.** James landed seven commits on puppeteer over 09-17…09-19 (99 files) while the lock still pinned `73b2d646`, so `pnpm preflight` failed at step one and nobody could run THE gate; field-app's typecheck had been red on three TS2353 since, attributed to the drift. This is the EL8 event, run at James's word ("run it"), and the same hour he had me push puppeteer main (`807904c..2f5ce00`, 122 commits) so the pinned revision is fetchable by CI's clone step.

**What moved upstream.** Live usage accounting is isolated from transcripts — `liveUsageOrigin` admits usage only from `native-telemetry`, `native-protocol` or `native-hook`, and a replayed envelope's usage updates are filtered out of the monitor batch — then native usage is priced into `costUsd`, `costCoverage` and a `costHistory` of buckets, and the UI's ledger record turns from a token series into a list of independently observed USD RUNS (`{currency: 'USD', providerId, nativeSessionId, savedAt, runs}`); the swarm's ONE-INK revision collapses seven state colours to a surface and an ink, deletes `burn-bars`, and brings a STATE GLOW parameter group with defaults (the desktop side of IOS-7's revision).

**Three breaks here, only one of them obvious.** (1) The fixture's three TS2353 — rewritten around a `run()` helper over the new shape. (2) The silent one typecheck could not see, the `clean-merge-hides-a-mirrored-rule` class exactly: `exportUsage` now hands the store only the conversation's LIVE run, and upstream's own host store (`apps/godview/src/main/usage-history-store.ts`) answers that with a per-run merge that preserves corrections by revision — while our renderer-local cache (`packages/field-app/src/godview/monitor/usage-history-cache.ts`) still replaced the whole record, so every earlier run's observed spend would have been discarded and a resumed bubble would open holding only its latest leg. The cache now merges by run id with revision precedence (a newer save breaks ties when neither side carries a revision), bounds a conversation to 50 runs, and writes a version 2 document so a version 1 record (token series, not dollars) is dropped on read rather than shown as USD; three new rows, each proved to bite (reverting the merge reds exactly those three; accepting version 1 again reds exactly the legacy-document row). (3) A stale expectation that was NOT this move's: the opt-in real-claude row in `packages/fieldd/test/agent-session.test.ts` asserted `schemaVersion === 2` while `AGENT_MONITOR_SCHEMA_VERSION` had been 3 at the OLD pin already — a row the ordinary gate cannot see had been red since AR-3; it now asserts the contract's constant.

Re-witnessed at the new pin on the prebuilt rosettad: `agent-session` 20/20 including both REAL claude rows (the native session id observed from the vendor's hooks at schemaVersion 3; re-attached across a fieldd restart at runtime epoch 2, same PTY, hooks flowing, ordinary exit 143), `agent-runtime` 11, `rosettad-daemon` 18, `rosettad-supervisor` 14, `agent-index-sessions` 13, `agent-monitor-pin` 1, `agent-usage` 13 — 70/70; `pnpm smoke:godview` ok (usage column mounted, cold open 1894 ms / 78 ms warm, 60 frames p50 16.6 / p95 17.4 ms; `swarmRenderer: unavailable` is this host's GL bind flap). The orchestrator re-ran preflight, field-app's typecheck and the usage cache file (10/10) before the fast-forward.

**Findings.** The desktop already carries the USD fields: `AgentMonitorMirror.usage` is `.passthrough()` and upstream added the three cost fields at the same schema version 3 with no generation bump (`agent-monitor-pin` stays green); the only thing holding a USD readout back on the desktop is `coreUsage`'s explicit key list in `useMonitorAgents.ts`, which copies the token aggregates and drops the rest — the phone's `field.agents.v1` is a separate content-free projection and is the real D-i18. ## AR-S1 — Settings → Agents: the shelf of installed agents, updates with the updater's own output, each agent's page (2026-09-22; `19b35b1b`, puppeteer `ea90c34` pinned)

**James:** "…implement the settings ui inside vibefield properly following its coding conventions, and at the same time, any api and underline features needs should be implemented or refactored properly inside puppetear side … plan and implement the agent setting first, focus on that, let's do it proper and solid, features in puppetear should also have proper abstractions so actual per agent logics are implemented properly under each adapters." The design is the record's R1 at pass 16 (artifact `MqjwWoxdxFZ87Vt2uduNT1`); AR-S1 is its shared half — the plan names the series (S2 Agent Profiles, S3 install from Settings, S4 extensions, S5 usage windows) in `draft/thinking-ar-agents-settings.md`.

**What moved upstream (puppeteer `ea90c34`, pinned here — on no remote branch until James pushes).** Four answers a host needs and the runtime could not give, every vendor fact inside its adapter: `runtime.planUpdate({providerId, executable?})` → `UpdatePlan` (the adapter's `recipeFor` resolved by the runner's own `recipeArgv`, so the command a host shows is the command run); `InstalledAgent.releaseChannel` (the release line the install's own updater follows — Claude maps `autoUpdatesChannel`, whose default "latest" is `preview`, and npm-global or an `@latest` cask to `preview`; Grok maps `alpha` to `preview`); `ReleaseCheckResult.available` with an exported `availableUpdate()`; `updateInstallation({onOutput})`, an opaque observer beside the 0600 transcript. The read-only live proof now plans every install; on James's Mac it read 11 installs across 10 agents, every one planned, and Grok's oracle offered 1.0.41 on stable. Codex's npm install plans `codex update` by the adapter's documented rule (it resolves npm, bun, pnpm, brew and standalone installs itself).

**The doors.** `agents.installs` names each install's update plan and says whether this daemon holds the machine scope. `agents.releases` KEEPS a check that consulted anything in `distribution.json` (`lastCheckedAt` + the rows) and answers `{cached: true}` from the record alone, re-judged against today's installs — so the page opens on "Checked 09:41:20" and never checks on its own (AR-D22); a check that asked nothing (no oracle, the network off) is not kept, because it learned nothing. `agents.operations.subscribe` carries an update's own output while it runs: ANSI-stripped, a carriage-return redraw settled to its last draw, the last 16 KiB, whole snapshots at the 16 ms tick, memory only, never parsed — the receipt is the outcome; a second update of the same provider is `CONFLICT`. `agents.reveal` shows an install in Finder only when fieldd's own inventory holds the path, through the shell provider's new internal `shell.revealPath` (→ `shell.showItemInFolder`); with no desktop shell attached it refuses `UNAVAILABLE {service: shell}`. The window token holds `agents.manage`. fieldd's distribution service moved out of `agent-runtime.ts` into `agent-distribution.ts` — the first cut of the refactor slate system.html records.

**The section.** `SettingsDialog` gains Agents (Workspace, first) and a subpage header — the record's round back button beside the title; a press on the Agents item returns to the shelf. `panels/agents/` is the UI_SYSTEM.md shape: `agents-model.ts` the pure join of the doors' answers and every word, `AgentsView.tsx` the controller-free shelf and agent page, `AgentsSection.tsx` the controller, `agents-settings.css` beside them. The shelf: one row per installed agent (puppeteer's mark, "2.2.0 → 2.3.0" + Update when behind, else "version · installed by"), Check for updates as the section's act, "Checked HH:MM:SS · N updates"; loading, empty ("No coding agents on this Mac yet" + Look again), unavailable (a refused scope offers no retry) and no-machine-scope states. The agent's page: hero with Update to X / Updating… / Up to date; the updater's output card (the command, Running… or Finished HH:MM:SS, the output open while it runs and folded under its outcome after); Version (installed, latest — "Same as installed", "No release feed" or a failed check in the provider's words — Release notes ↗ in the browser, https only); Install (installed by, location + Show in Finder, automatic updates, what Update runs and who runs it); Signed in under. An update ends when its version has been read back: this window's own request re-reads once before it settles, the feed re-reads for an update another window ran. Focus moves to the page's title on the way in and back to the row on the way out. The catalog mounts the shipping views on fixture doors in six states.

**Record fidelity.** Two corrections back to the record before landing: an other install is SHOWN, never offered as a choice ("not used, new sessions use the one above" + Show in Finder, as in every pass) — so `agents.setActive` keeps its door (AR-D16) and has no UI — and the offered version is neutral ink (pass 16 took the orange out).

**Witness.** In a clean detached worktree of `19b35b1b` with every sibling at its pin and clean (rosetta through a worktree at `e8d907a`, because its checkout carries in-flight protocol-21 edits): preflight OK · `gen:check` clean — the generated Rust and schemas byte-identical, so the cargo steps (fmt, clippy, `test:rust`) were not run, no Rust input having changed · check:deps · iOS fixtures · icons · typecheck 25 projects · biome 9 errors, all main's own `docs/agent-plane` `aria-label` rows, unchanged by this slice · bundle:assert 573.5 KB raw / 154.8 KB gz (from 567.8 / 153.8 at UA-7) · `pnpm test` green in 24 projects (field-app 96 files / 870, electron-shell 718 + 2 skipped, contracts 508, dev-runner among them) and fieldd, re-run with a private `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (finding 4): 87 files, 914 passed + 14 skipped. puppeteer `ea90c34`: `pnpm test` green (typecheck, structural gates, every suite); `format:check` red only on `scripts/capture-swarm-states.mjs`, as at its HEAD. The read-only live proof as above. The catalog over CDP (headless Chrome against a private Vite): every state in light and dark, a 1000 px window, keyboard focus on the rows.

**Findings.** (1) The first full `pnpm test` timed two distribution rows out at 5 s (350–490 ms alone): each boots a daemon and spawns the scripted agent, so the block now carries the 20 s budget the other daemon-spawning rows carry. (2) Mid-session the rosetta sibling's `PROTOCOL_VERSION` moved 20 → 21 in its working tree (19:55) while the built rosettad is still 20; every rosettad-dependent fieldd file (index-search, rosettad-daemon, -supervisor, agent-session, agent-runtime) fails against that pairing until `pnpm siblings:build` — not this slice's, and the distribution rows passed before it. (3) The catalog's "Update runs" row broke a command inside a word (`word-break: break-all`); paths wrap at their spaces first now (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`). (4) A clean worktree needs fieldd's `<root>/target`: its global setup builds field-native and looks there, and `~/.cargo/config.toml` sends every build to the shared SSD target — so the first clean run rebuilt the shared `target/debug/field-native` (identical sources, 20:19) before the witness moved to a private `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` with `target` linked to it, the escape hatch the cargo config documents.

**Owed.** Agent Profiles (AR-S2) waits on one ruling: whether a cross-agent profile groups the per-provider personas in fieldd (A) or in puppeteer's registry (B, the lean). A live pass in the product window (James's dev-runner was running; nothing was driven in it). The puppeteer push, so CI can fetch the pin.

## UA-7c — a user switch is one transition: the window defocuses into the next user's face, and the reload happens under a frame both windows share (2026-09-22; `0361e6cf`)

**Why now.** James: "when clicked switch to another user, entire window should first enter blur, and the user icon appear large at the center, and there will be visual indicators indicating that we are switching to another user, the whole transition should feel seamless, buttery smooth, intuitive". A switch reloads the window (UA-D15); until now the reload was the only feedback.

**As built.** DESIGN.md §8 "The switch" first. The window being left converges on the boot splash wearing the next user's face — the pressed face travels from its row to the centre at 128px (held, 560ms island), the field defocuses (40px backdrop blur), recedes to 0.98 and freezes (M5), the splash's ground rises over it, and "Switching to", the name and the splash's real bar and stage line settle in — and only then asks main. The reloaded window paints that frame first, runs its real boot stages on the bar, and at the reveal flies the face home to the Me corner (to Setup pane 2's face for a user not set up yet) while the new field comes into focus. A refusal plays it backwards; New user… leaves to the plain splash; reduced motion fades in place. `boot/switch.ts` conducts (every switch and New user… door goes through `leaveFor`; a validated, read-once `sessionStorage` handoff carries the face across the reload); `SwitchSceneView` + `SwitchLayer` draw it; the catalog stages it (`SwitchPreview`). The product entry is render-blocking with a synchronous, theme-stamped first render, kept through the build by `render-blocking-entry.ts` and asserted by `verify-production-renderer`. The spec's UA-D15 is amended on dev-local. Not covered: the tray's Switch User (main reloads unannounced; it boots on the plain splash).

**Witness.** Gated on the exact tree (`b3d838c2`), `pnpm verify` then the rest of its chain in a clean worktree: preflight, fmt, clippy, bundle:assert, test:rust (263) and gen:check green; field-app 893 and electron-shell 721 green; typecheck red only at fieldd's agent-distribution.ts and fieldd's rosettad/index rows red, both from UNCOMMITTED edits in the puppeteer and rosetta siblings (at their pins the types and the protocol agree); lint red only on main's agent-plane pages; logging's seed-fuzz green alone. The catalog specimen was recorded frame by frame in headless Chrome, both themes, both frames, a refusal and reduced motion; the leaving window's held frame and the arriving window's first frame are pinned equal in markup, and photographed identical in dark (0 differing pixels). No real user switch was run in Electron before landing — James's dev run is the live witness.

**Findings.** (1) Chromium keeps the old frame on screen through a reload of an `http:` page until the new page paints content, but not through a reload of a `vibefield-app:` page: an offscreen Electron 43 probe saw the new page's stylesheet ground presented ~22ms after the reload — a packaged reload flashed bare ground for as long as the boot script ran, invisible in dev. `blocking="render"` on the head entry holds the first frame until the entry has run (no intermediate frame at 150ms or 900ms of script). (2) Vite's build drops `blocking` when it re-emits the bundled entry tag; the dev server keeps it. (3) The boot splash painted in the light theme for a dark-mode user until the workspace mounted under it: the theme was stamped by `useTheme`, not before the first render. (4) The first catalog photographs showed the scene's ground transparent: `.vf-splash` lives in `boot.css`, which only BootRoot imported — the product loaded it by accident of order, the catalog did not. The scene owns that import now.

## AR-S1b — the update fixes from live use: output as a terminal shows it, a Stop, and receipts that never claim a currency they did not see (2026-09-22; `a3a68b08`, puppeteer `497de8e` + `ddb6e34` + `2cba428`, pinned at `2cba428`)

**James** ran every update from Settings → Agents the evening AR-S1 landed, and sent three screenshots: "kimi update is not working", "opencode update output looks messy", "hermes agent just stuck at update". Codex, Grok, OpenCode, Copilot, Pi and Hermes all updated (the kept receipts read 0.155.1 → 0.156.1, 1.0.30 → 1.0.41, 1.18.23 → 1.18.32, 1.0.80 → 1.0.88, 0.84.3 → 0.87.1, 0.20.5 → 0.21.4). Each of the three was a different layer's fault, read from the kept 0600 transcripts and the live processes, never guessed.

**Kimi — the adapter planned the wrong command, and the runner claimed what it had not seen.** The adapter called `~/.kimi-code/bin/kimi` a standalone binary and planned `kimi upgrade`; Kimi 0.37.1 calls that layout its native installer, and its upgrade answers with "To update manually, run: curl -fsSL https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.sh | bash" and exits 0 — so nothing moved and the receipt said "already current" beside a page offering 2.0.2. Upstream: a new recipe kind, `installer-script` (the vendor's documented `curl | bash`, run as argv with the URL a positional parameter, https only, `pipefail`, with the variables the script documents); the Kimi adapter classifies `native-installer` and declares the script Kimi names (`code.kimi.com` serves it via `cdn.kimi.com`; `kimi.ai` redirects to a web page — read, never executed, before declaring it), with `KIMI_INSTALL_DIR` = the install and `KIMI_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1`. The runner's exit-0-no-change receipt is now `unchanged` — current, or an updater that declined; `already-current` stays readable for older receipts. Here: the receipt carries the versions re-inspection read, and the page weighs `unchanged` against the release still on offer ("The updater finished without updating — 2.0.2 is still available. Its output says why."), saying "Already up to date" only when a check backs it.

**OpenCode — fieldd stripped the redraws out of the output.** Its spinner redraws with `ESC[999D` + `ESC[J`; AR-S1 stripped escapes as chunks arrived, so every frame stayed. fieldd now keeps the raw bytes (bounded, cut on a line so a cut never lands inside an escape) and renders them at projection with a small line terminal, `terminal-text.ts`: CR, BS and TAB; cursor up, down, forward, back, next and previous line, column and position; erase in line and in display; colours, modes, OSC and DCS dropped; cursor MOTION clamped (text is not), so `ESC[999999999C` cannot pad a line to a billion cells on every 16 ms projection. James's own transcript renders as the logo, "Upgrade · Using method: curl · From 1.18.23 → 1.18.32 · Upgrade complete · Done".

**Hermes — not stuck, silent.** The live process tree: `hermes update --yes` → `git fetch origin main` → `ssh … git-upload-pack`, git in `fetch_pack → index_pack`, a `tmp_pack` of 645 MB and growing — the checkout is SHALLOW, so the fetch negotiated poorly and pulled ~712 MiB; then migrations; then "Stopping gateway — draining in-flight runs (up to 1815s)". Nothing reached the page because git prints progress only to a terminal and Python buffered its own lines into the pipe. Upstream, the runner is unattended — `spawn` with no stdin (a prompt reads end of file), a session of its own (nothing can prompt on the host's terminal), `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`, streaming instead of `execFile`'s 8 MB `maxBuffer` (which would have killed a chatty updater) — and a timeout or a stop ends the updater's whole process GROUP, SIGTERM then SIGKILL, so the git, ssh or curl it started goes too. Recipes may carry a budget: Hermes declares 45 minutes, since the 15-minute default would end it mid-drain. Here: `agents.update.stop` (agents.manage, local, audited), the hero's Stop while the updater runs, and "Running · m:ss" in the output's head.

**Witness.** In a clean detached worktree of `a3a68b08` with the siblings at their pins (rosetta through a worktree at `e8d907a`, its checkout carrying in-flight protocol-21 edits): preflight OK · `gen:check` clean · typecheck 25 projects · biome 9 errors, all main's own `docs/agent-plane` `aria-label` rows · contracts 508 · field-app 98 files / 895 · fieldd 87 files, 920 passed + 14 skipped (on a private `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`). puppeteer at `2cba428`: core 144, runtime 189 (the runner's real-process rows among them — stdin reads end of file, no controlling terminal, a stop and a timeout take the grandchildren), Kimi 69, Hermes 57, and a typecheck of every package; the full `pnpm test` under load failed three rows outside this slice that pass alone (runtime 90/90, the imposter's conformance 11/11). The renderer against James's own OpenCode and Grok transcripts; the catalog's updating and updated pages over CDP (Stop and "Running · 2:55"; "Updated to 2.3.0.").

**Findings.** (1) A killed orphan outlives its signal by a reap: the runner's grandchild test asserted death at the instant the run settled and failed once under load — it now waits for the reap. (2) Under the parallel gates three puppeteer rows and fieldd's rosettad-dependent files failed for reasons outside this slice (a loaded host; rosetta's in-flight protocol 21 against a protocol-20 rosettad) and passed alone, or at the pins. (3) The dev-runner watches vibe-field only: a change in the puppeteer sibling reaches a running `pnpm dev` only on its restart.

**Owed.** The puppeteer push (the pin is on no remote branch); Agent Profiles (AR-S2) on the grouping ruling; a live pass of Stop and Kimi's script on James's Mac, his to run.

## AR-S1c — Settings → Agents opens at once: the installs read at boot, answered from that inventory, read again on a check (2026-09-22; `88fad3bf`)

**James:** "currently everytime i clicked to agents page in settings, it runs a check for agents which takes a long time, can you make it run this check during app launch instead so when i open this setting page everything just show instantly, and we can also add a refresh/check button for manual check run?"

**Why it was slow.** `agents.installs` asked puppeteer for a FRESH inspection on every call — every agent's version command, eleven installs on James's Mac, seconds each time the page opened. Puppeteer's inventory already caches per provider (one in-flight read shared by concurrent callers) and an update already re-reads its own provider, so the cache was sound; fieldd simply bypassed it.

**What changed.** `agents.installs` answers the inventory by default and `{ refresh: true }` reads the Mac again. fieldd warms the inventory in the background once boot has committed (`fieldd.agents.inventory_warm`, with the count and the milliseconds), so Settings → Agents and the deck's launcher answer at once; a page opened before the warm read finishes waits on that same read rather than starting another. Check for updates is the manual check James asked for: it reads the Mac again first — a version an agent's own updater moved since launch — then asks the release feeds about that inventory, and both land together (a read begun before them cannot undo them). Look again reads the Mac again too.

**Witness.** In a clean detached worktree of the tree this commit carries (byte-identical, `9a5d02e9`) with the siblings at their pins (rosetta through a worktree at `e8d907a`): fieldd 87 files, 923 passed + 14 skipped, among them a row proving the product's daemon warms at boot (the scripted agent counted in the log) while an embedded one logs nothing; the distribution unit rows (the default read never refreshes, `refresh` does, a warm that fails degrades nothing); contracts 508; field-app's agents rows 18 (the page's first read asks nothing of the Mac; Check for updates reads it, then the feeds; Look again reads it); fieldd and field-app typechecks.

**Finding.** A first cut warmed EVERY daemon — and most test daemons do not set `agentSearchPath`, so they search the real PATH: dozens of parallel test boots ran the developer's own agents' version commands, and 24 rows across unrelated suites (service host, doc service, peer link, the rosettad pair) timed out. Machine-touching boot work is now an explicit product opt-in, `agentInventoryWarm`, set by bin.ts alone — the same shape as `vibefieldRoot`: an embedded or unit daemon never runs a machine's agents unasked.

**Owed.** An agent that updates itself in the background after launch shows its launch-time version until Check for updates or the next launch; the next step, if it matters, is noticing a changed install on disk (its launcher's mtime) and re-reading that provider alone.

## AR-S2 — Agent Profiles: each profile one folder under its user, a default for new sessions, and a sign-out that waits for its sessions (2026-09-23; `41d79b64`, puppeteer `50ac021` pinned)

**James:** "plan and start implement second phase, the agent profile, same convention as before, ui in the vibefield, bottom api and logic stay in puppetear, and also design carefully in vibefield agent plane so that agent profiles are properly managed under vibefield's user account architecture, each profile's data are managed properly under its user account folders". Before it he ruled the open question B: the cross-agent grouping lives in puppeteer's registry (AR-D23). The design is the record's R1 at pass 16 (artifact `MqjwWoxdxFZ87Vt2uduNT1`); the plan and its as-built are in `draft/thinking-ar-agents-settings.md`.

**puppeteer `50ac021` (pinned here).** Profile SETS: a named place holding at most one account per agent, exactly one set the default, This Mac the synthetic native set (the providers' own roots). Registry v2 (`{version: 2, defaultSet?, sets, profiles}`; a v1 file adopted by grouping its managed profiles by label). A managed set owns `<rootsDirectory>/<slug>/`, named once from its first name and never moved by a rename; each member's root is `<set dir>/<provider>-<8 hex>/`, allocated exclusively and never reused (Claude's Keychain item and Codex's keyring entry are keyed on the path). A spawn that names no account runs under the default set's member for its agent, else the agent's own root; resume and attach never consult the default. `retireProfile` and the adapters' `signOut` (Claude: `claude auth logout` under the root's binding); `ProfileGlyph` in the views.

**The agent plane.** `LAYOUT.AGENT_PROFILE_SETS_DIR` puts every profile's folder at `users/<fuid>/agents/profiles/<set>/` (AR-D24): a profile's whole data — each agent's config, history, plugins and sign-in — is one folder under the user it belongs to, and This Mac stays the OS user's own folders (UA-D6). Six doors on `agent.spawn`, local: `agents.profileSets.{list, subscribe, create, update, delete, reveal}`; the mutations audited under the new target kind `agent-profile`. `agents.profiles.create` takes `{ set, provider }`; `agents.profiles.delete` became SIGN OUT (AR-D25): out of its profile and new spawns at once, FINISHED when no session runs under it (the vendor's sign-out, the index runtime retired with its rows kept, unregistered, the root deleted), answering `waiting` meanwhile. Deleting a profile stops its sessions first — the terminate asked again until the floor has placed each one, because a terminate for a session not yet placed was answered `terminated: false` — then signs out every sign-in and deletes the folder. fieldd's `agent-profiles.ts` holds all of it and reaches the fold only through `PersonaSessions`. Folders ride the feed home-abbreviated, for a person to read; no door takes a path back. This Mac's sign-ins are read in the product daemon's boot warm, on a refresh, and after a login pane or a sign-out — never in a test daemon.

**The window.** Settings gained the sidebar group "Agent Profiles" (each profile's glyph and name, This Mac first, New profile…), a profile's page (the C1 timeline for each sign-in — its % steps off the now line, a reach of 12 % where the record's 8 still touched on a narrow track; Add agent…; name, glyph, Use for new sessions, folder; Delete with the P7 confirm), one agent inside a profile (Switch account…, its folder, Sign out), New agent profile, and the sign-in terminal on the page — the terminal pool's third consumer. The catalog carries the "Agent profiles" specimen (six states), checked in both themes over CDP.

**Witness.** In a clean detached worktree of this commit with rosetta at its pin (`e8d907a`) and puppeteer at `50ac021`: preflight, `gen:check`, typecheck 25/25, contracts 509/509. The same code tree, verified an hour earlier (docs and the pin aside): `pnpm test` 25/25 — fieldd 931 passed + 14 skipped, field-app 910/910. At the commit, under a load average near 300 (the dev window and other apps running), five timing rows in unrelated suites timed out once and passed alone (3/3). puppeteer `pnpm test`: every stage green except a pre-existing flake — imposter's Grok conformance, where `adapter-grok`'s `dispose()` deletes its temp home right after signalling the leader (`ENOTEMPTY`, 1 in 8 at the previous HEAD).

**Finding.** Committing into a live worktree: James's in-progress `screenshotResult` channel had landed in `registries.ts`, the file that carries `AGENT_PROFILE_SETS_DIR`, between the verification tree and the commit; the clean worktree's contracts suite caught it (sixteen IPC channels where the shell test pins fifteen), and the commit carries the mine-only blob.

**Owed.** James, on first use: only Claude and Codex can be added — the six other adapters run a login in a bound root but report no identity, and "Add agent…" and This Mac required one (the record's This Mac lists every installed agent). The review round that follows this commit (AR-S2b) — its first reports: a delete does not yet wait for the stopped sessions to leave the floor, login panes are not counted as sessions under a sign-in, and a plain spawn now reads the registry and fails hard when it cannot. Where Copilot, Kimi and Hermes keep a credential is unprobed, so their sign-out is the folder alone. AR-D24/D25 as worded await ratification.

## SNAP-3 — the clipboard tray: a still flies into the notch on the left edge, and the shell serves it through `vibefield-still://` (2026-09-23; `b46c0f05`)

**James:** "plan and implement this notch and side tray design properly in VibeField; the clipboard tray should work nicely with the screenshot feature already ported — once a snapshot is done, the screenshot image chip flies into the side tray." Earlier that day, on the design page (`draft/composer/compact.html` §15–19; `compact.md` Parts III–IV), he ruled the notch — **N1** of four, a matte tab that grows out of the edge: a concave fillet of 12 into the wall, a convex face of 14, 26 × 116 — and for the drawer combined P3's shape with P2's opacity and asked for a white notch in the light theme: **P4**, the same path at 152 wide (fillet 18, face 22), opaque, the notch in the drawer's material, its hairline gapped under the notch so the two outlines are one line. The plan is `draft/composer/build-edge-trays.md`.

**What existed.** The capture door (SNAP-D3) with no product consumer; the View menu's capture invisible to the page; a renderer that could not show a still from its path (the CSP admits no file access); no image card type; the Artifact Hub as the browser plugin's surface. SNAP-D4 had named two ways for bytes to reach the canvas — an artifact, or a shell-owned scheme — and left the choice to this slice.

**The scheme.** `vibefield-still://stills/<basename>` (`electron-shell/src/main/still-protocol.ts`): the request names a basename; the answer is the path the ScreenshotTool retains under that name, realpath-checked on its final component (a planted symlink is refused; the directory chain may resolve, `/var` → `/private/var` does); 404 for every other shape — a wrong scheme or host, a query, a second segment, a traversal, a NUL, a non-PNG, a name the ring no longer holds. `image/png`, `no-store`, CORP `cross-origin` because the app origin is cross-origin to the scheme by construction and is the one reader the bytes exist for. The third row of the ONE `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` call; `standard` + `secure` + `stream`, no fetch, no CORS, no CSP bypass; `img-src` admits it; installed in every mode. The spelling is wire truth in `contracts/src/screenshot.ts` (`SCREENSHOT_STILL_SCHEME`, `screenshotStillUrl`).

**The result reaches the page.** `IPC_CHANNELS.screenshotResult` (`vibefield:screenshot:result`, the closed table's sixteenth): the menu's `takeScreenshot` sends its result to the focused or primary window; the preload validates it and keeps the latest until the renderer subscribes (`window.vibefield.screenshot.onResult`); `FieldHost.onScreenshotResult?` and `screenshotStillUrl?` — both optional, so a harness without the shell renders a tile without its image and says so.

**The tray.** `field-app/src/hud/edge-tray/`: `notch-path.ts` (the pure builders; the suite pins the strings), `clipboard-store.ts` (session-only, newest first, capped at the ring's twelve), `EdgeTrayView.tsx` (controller-free; the drawer's silhouette an SVG measured from the rendered panel), `EdgeTray.tsx` (`ClipboardTray`: hover opens after 120ms, a 320ms grace closes; click pins; ⌘⇧V pins from the keyboard; Escape unpins; typing while pinned filters; the Snap tile calls the door and says why when refused — `helper-missing`, `permission-denied` with the setting named, `busy`), `tray-flight.ts` (the ghost from the capture's bounds mapped into the window, else the centre, to the notch on `--vf-ease-island` 560ms, shrinking along its travel; the store takes the item ON arrival so the count ticks with the bump; reduced motion fades it at the notch; one element, CSS transitions, a 640ms settle timer as the worst case). Mounted in `ChromeLayer` beside the side-panel stage, non-modal and self-governing; `hud-flight` gained `left` and `right`. Tokens: `--vf-shadow-edge`, `--vf-drop-island`, `--vf-drop-edge` (DESIGN.md §5's new row; the island and edge recipes as `drop-shadow()` where the silhouette is a path). DESIGN.md §5 records the one exception to "chrome is glass", §8 the edge-tray canon, §10 the left edge.

**Catalog and tests.** The Field-chrome section mounts the shipping `EdgeTrayView` with self-drawn SVG fixture stills — at rest, open, pinned, empty, no shell — and a bump button; the inventory lists the notch and the tray; the boundaries test lists the prefix, the view and the files. Tests: `still-protocol.test.ts` (22: every hostile URL, the ring moving under a request, the planted symlink, the registration), `preload-screenshot-result.test.ts` (3), `edge-tray.test.tsx` (12: the geometry strings, the flight's start, the store's cap, the Snap words, the view on both edges, the hover/pin/Escape/⌘⇧V grammar with fake timers, a menu-driven landing — the ghost, then the store, then the bump — the door from the Snap tile and its refusal, the no-shell tile); the scheme-rows, CSP and closed-channel-table tests updated.

**Witness.** contracts 509/509 · electron-shell 746/746 · field-app: the three named files green, `pnpm typecheck` 25/25, `bundle:assert` OK, biome clean on every file touched. `pnpm verify` could not run end to end in this tree: preflight stops on the rosetta checkout being off its pin (`8cce7832` vs `e8d907ab`); `pnpm lint`'s 36 errors are all in the untracked `work/` and `docs/design` JSON and HTML; `gen:check` was red on the then-unregenerated `AGENT_PROFILE_SETS_DIR` row; `design-system.test.tsx`'s rows time out under the full suite's load and pass alone. The catalog was photographed over CDP in both themes (`build:design`, served, the specimen in five states).

A transparent 1px border left on the panel put the drawer's silhouette a pixel inside the notch's wall and its face hairline showed as a seam (James: "remove this split line"); the border is gone and the line is gapped under the notch instead. `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` refuses both `{ key: undefined }` and an optional read assigned to an optional prop — destructure to omit. ## SNAP-3a — ⌃⌘A above the page, and a fly-in that needs no frame: what James's first live press found (2026-09-23; `14c97bf7`)

**James:** "⌃⌘A is not working, why? and i'm not seeing the snapshot fly transition." Main's log had two captures `ok` through the IPC door (the tray's Snap tile) at 02:46 and none through the menu, the helper present and spawning, the new main and preload in the running app.

**The chord.** The canvas engine's keymap binds ⌘A to select-all, tests its modifier as `metaKey || ctrlKey` and calls `preventDefault`; on macOS Electron offers a key to the page BEFORE the menu, so ⌃⌘A selected every card and the View item's accelerator never fired — a SNAP-0 latent bug, since the menu path had never been pressed live. `electron-shell/src/main/screenshot-chord.ts` takes ⌃⌘A (Alt+A elsewhere) on `before-input-event`, the door ⇧⇧ already uses, and swallows it there: per Electron, `preventDefault` in that event also suppresses the menu shortcut, so the capture runs exactly once. Installed per window beside the double-shift detector, only where a helper resolves; the menu item keeps the chord in its accelerator column. `screenshot-chord.test.ts` (5) pins the chord, the release, and that ⌘A stays the canvas's.

**The flight.** The ghost's end state was set on a double `requestAnimationFrame`; right after the helper's overlay leaves the screen the window can be occluded or unpainted, no frames come, and the 640ms settle timer removed the ghost before it moved — the tile still landed, so the tray filled with no flight. `tray-flight.ts` now waits for the document to be visible (bounded at 1.5 s) and commits the end state after a forced reflow, no frame needed; the tray test asserts the end state is set synchronously.

**Witness.** electron-shell screenshot-chord 5/5 and godview-state 21/21; field-app edge-tray 12/12; biome clean on the files touched. The dev runner rebuilt main and restarted the app with the interceptor before the commit. Typecheck was red in the tree on fieldd's agent-profiles and its settings test — James's in-progress `contracts/src/agent-index.ts` edit, not these files.

**Owed.** The retry: the fly-in on a real still has still not been seen by anyone.

## SNAP-1 + SNAP-3b — a global screenshot shortcut, display coordinates and native preview (2026-09-24)

**James:** the shortcut fails on his other screen; it should work globally, as in the original prototype, whenever VibeField is running. This amends SNAP-D3's application-only first port.

**The shortcut.** Electron `globalShortcut` owns ⌃⌘A on macOS (Alt+A on Windows) for the app's lifetime. The persisted `desktop.screenshotHotkey` preference defaults on; Settings → Desktop can turn global delivery off and displays a conflict or missing helper. Disabling or quitting unregisters only this chord. The system tray has Take Screenshot; the View item and local interceptor remain. A busy helper prevents duplicate captures. Main chooses the result recipient before the native overlay takes focus, without bringing VibeField in front before the freeze; a capture with no product window keeps its latest result for the next window.

**The two consumer bugs.** The tray treated macOS display-local, bottom-left points as global top-left coordinates. Main now adds optional `screenBounds` to the shell result, preserving the native v1 `bounds`: display origin plus flipped local Y on macOS, Electron's physical-pixel-to-DIP conversion on Windows. Retina points are not scaled twice; a disconnected display uses the tray's centre fallback. Windows overlay results also now include the monitor's virtual-screen offset, as the v1 contract already required. Quick Look previously used `window.open` on the still scheme, which the shell's navigation policy refused. A new `vibefield:screenshot:preview` door accepts a retained PNG basename from a registered renderer, reuses the scheme's realpath check, then opens native Quick Look on macOS or the image viewer on Windows. Evicted stills, symlinks and preview failures produce a visible message.

**Verification.** 209 focused tests pass: electron-shell 130, contracts 52, field-app 20, fieldd 7 (including the persisted preference and subscription round trip). Shell, field-app and fieldd typechecks pass. `pnpm bundle:assert` passes both production boundary checks and the bundle budget (initial graph 617.3 KB raw / 164.4 KB gzip). Windows `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo check --offline --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` pass. The running dev app restarted and logged `screenshot.shortcut.changed` with `status: registered`, `accelerator: Control+Command+A`, `message: null` from the real macOS registration. That receipt establishes OS registration, not an end-to-end capture.

**Full gate and live work remaining.** `pnpm verify` was run verbatim and stopped at preflight: sibling rosetta is dirty/ahead of its pinned `e8d907ab2899` (observed `b85866d51dcc`, binary freshness warning), and the tracked `VibeField Mock.xcscheme` filename contains whitespace disallowed by the Nx watch protocol. Those unrelated files were left as found. An actual global press while another app is active on the secondary display, the completed fly-in, and native Quick Look still need a live witness with James at the display. Canvas image widgets/drag-in, the scoped plugin/agent provider (SNAP-2), and the Windows box/signing round (SNAP-4) remain later work.

## AR-S2b — Agent Profiles after review: a delete that waits for its sessions to be gone, sign-ins that keep their folder when the vendor's sign-out fails, and every agent that signs in can be added (2026-09-23; `c383dc62`, puppeteer `4240196` pinned)

**James:** "commit and do a review", then, on first use, "why it only shows claude and codex? how can i sign in other agents?" Five reviewers read AR-S2 in parallel, one per layer (puppeteer's registry and folders, its runtime and adapters, fieldd's profile service and doors, fieldd's sessions, the page); every finding was checked against the code before it was fixed.

**What they found that mattered most.** A plain spawn now read the registry and THREW on a file it could not read, leaving the run preparing. Registry writes were unserialized and applied before they were saved. A profile delete removed its folder while the sessions it had "stopped" were still exiting — `terminateLive` returned as soon as the ladder started. A login pane was not a session under its persona, so a sign-out could delete the root under a live `claude auth login`. Before the floor's first inventory `liveUnder` read zero. A vendor sign-out that failed was logged and the root deleted anyway, leaving the Keychain credential nothing could reach. A fire-and-forget read of This Mac's sign-ins could reject unhandled and end fieldd. Idle-resume would replace a pending run under a signed-out persona. On the page: a sign-in left running with no way back, a second one over the first, Create profile bouncing to Agents, the sign-out notice cleared by its own route change, an armed Delete carried to the next profile, and a terminal that trapped the keyboard.

**puppeteer `4240196`.** Registry writes one at a time, each to a copy committed only after the save; duplicate ids a corrupt file; onboarding's check-then-act under one lock; adopted folders named after their set. The default a preference: an unreadable registry leaves a plain spawn in the provider's own root, a named profile or set fails typed with its run terminal. `ProfileSupport.credential` (`root` | `external`, absent = not established) behind `signOutProfile`'s new answer `{ ran: false, credential }`, which also requires retire first and refuses while a run uses the account; Claude's logout strict and confirmed by a status read. Retired accounts bind no terminal and start no prewarm. Every profile service built with its launch's executable.

**The host's half.** `stopUnder` waits until what it stopped is GONE (12 s) and a delete is refused, retryable, with nothing deleted otherwise; login panes, creations in flight and — until the floor has answered and the re-attach has run — un-exited records count as live; a sign-out ends an open login pane first; `finish` keeps the folder when a vendor sign-out fails, deletes the root before unregistering, and is audited as the system actor from the sweep; folder deletion checks the exact allocated shapes on resolved paths. The feed gained `identity`; the sign-out answer `credential`. The page was rewritten around the review (one sign-in at a time, a sign-in that outlives its page and is cancelled from its row, keyed pages, act guards, focus, Shift-Tab out of the terminal, re-adoption when the pool's runtime is replaced).

**James's question.** Only Claude Code and Codex read back WHO signed in, and Add agent… had required that. Every agent that runs a login in a folder is offered now; the others' rows say "Doesn't say who is signed in"; This Mac lists every installed agent; a sign-out says what it did to the credential in the adapter's own terms.

**Witness.** In a clean worktree on `741afe5a` with rosetta at its pin: gen:check, typecheck 25/25, `pnpm test` with the files that timed out under a load average near 750 each passing alone — fieldd's new `agent-profiles.test.ts` (what it deletes and keeps, a failed vendor sign-out, a delete while sessions run, the credential claim, the sweep past a failing sign-in, the read that never rejects), the real-floor row where a sign-out ends an open login pane, and the page's review rows. puppeteer `pnpm test` green but for imposter's Grok conformance flake, which fails the same way at a clean HEAD.

**Finding.** The fieldd suite's global setup runs `cargo build -p field-native` with the inherited environment, so a verification worktree that only symlinks `target` still builds into the machine's shared target; a verification run needs `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set as well. The shared target was rebuilt from James's own tree afterwards.

**Owed.** Where Grok, Kimi and Copilot keep a credential (their sign-out is the folder alone, and the page says only that). The Agents page's "Signed in under" has no usage, so it cannot say "expired". adapter-grok's `dispose()` deletes its temp home without waiting (imposter's flake). A sign-in in a real window.

James asked for a performance review because the tool takes time to appear after the
shortcut. Existing real presses took 573–626 ms from helper spawn to `ready`, while global
shortcut dispatch to spawn took 3–10 ms. The capture started a new AppKit process every time.

The shell now prepares a macOS `--service` process at app startup and sends one versioned
capture command at a time. Idle startup reads no screen pixels, creates no overlay and
requests no Screen Recording permission. Every capture still freezes fresh displays before
showing the overlays; cleanup releases snapshots and windows, hides the helper, then
acknowledges `idle`. EOF and shell disposal end the helper; bounded boot/capture/cleanup
failures kill it, and a later request can restart it. The staged plist must advertise service
version 1, because older binaries treat an unknown flag as an immediate capture. Windows
keeps its existing `--once` path. The native command reader uses a bounded POSIX read: a real
pipe probe caught Foundation's buffered read waiting for more bytes on a short command.

Two smaller costs are removed: hovering within the same snapped window no longer requests
another full-overlay repaint, and an unmarked crop returns its CGImage without allocating
and redrawing a second bitmap. The overlay under the pointer receives keyboard focus.
`ready` logs native permission/window-list/capture/overlay timings plus host elapsed time.

**Evidence.** A hidden, single-display probe measured 250.8 ms for the first native capture
and overlay construction, then 82.3 and 81.5 ms when repeated in the same process. Those
exclude permission checks, process launch and visible presentation: they are NOT new global
shortcut-to-visible measurements. The rebuilt real service emitted idle without a capture,
exited on stdin EOF, and promptly refused a short invalid command while the pipe remained
open. Initial idle RSS was about 31 MiB. The running dev app logged `persistent: true` and
initial `idle` for helper PID 27362, followed by global shortcut registration.

**Checks.** Focused TS suites covering the host/protocol/service, contracts, shell screenshot
paths, settings and tray passed; screenshot/shell typechecks, the Swift harness, the native
build, targeted Biome and `pnpm bundle:assert` passed. `pnpm verify` was run verbatim and
stopped at unrelated preflight issues: sibling worktrees/pinned rosetta revision and the
tracked iOS scheme filename containing whitespace. Those files were left as found.

**Remaining evidence and review.** Updated shortcut-to-visible timings and repeated capture
on a secondary display still need the user's live press. Mosaic per-block pixel sampling,
synchronous PNG/TIFF export, and Windows serial capture/fallbacks are the next measured-work
candidates, not changes in this slice. Full review and phase table:
`draft/reviews/screenshot-performance-2026-09-24.md`.

## P0 — the pre-Phase-0 fixes: the posture a restarted floor forgot, the door a restarted fieldd left behind, a client new after every fieldd boot, and a phone that renews its grant (2026-09-24; main `499504cd`…`c6a8a39a`, rebased onto `c6f7d0cb`)

**Why now.** James: "onboard and do a thorough check on our terminal and mesh track of work", then "go ahead" on the fixes the check named as standing between the tree and Phase 0. The check (two read-only audit lanes, every load-bearing claim re-verified at source) found both tracks built to the hardware line and Phase 0 never run — no `tailnet` principal in the dev audit ledger since 09-13 — and four defects no record carried; building the fixes found a fifth (P0-S). Four of the five sit on Phase 0's own path and are fixed here; the fifth, the terminal doors' env-only switch (`FIELD_NATIVE_TERMINAL_MESH` is set by nothing in product code), is James's ruling.

**UA-P-0j `499504cd` — a floor that restarts under a live fieldd is asked for its posture again.** `link-service.ts` declared `native.mesh.start {linked}` once, at boot; the floor boots OFFLINE and holds no posture until asked; so a floor respawn under a resident fieldd (TC-S1's crash respawn, the wedge restart) left a linked desktop off its tailnet until fieldd itself restarted. Measured in the dev logs of 09-24: a wedge restart at 12:05:59, `mesh node not up` on every replay, the node back only at 14:46:19 with the next fieldd. The comment "the next probe … re-declares" was never true. As built: a re-dial of the mgmt link brings the probe forward (`floorReconnected`, wired in daemon.ts on `native.on("connected")`); the probe restores the posture ONLY on the floor's own `disabled` (its word for "no posture held": boot default, stop, retire, nothing else) — never on `starting`, where a second `native.mesh.start` before the node installs aborts the bring-up, never on `degraded`/`crashed`; the in-flight ask is tracked so the boot's own ask is never doubled. The mock floor models a posture on opt-in (`meshPosture`, `meshStarts`).

> **Correction (2026-09-24, §UA-P-0k):** "the in-flight ask is tracked so the boot's own ask is
> never doubled" held only against a probe racing the ask. The landed fieldd's first boot on the
> dev stack logged `fieldd.link.posture_restored` 8 ms after its first dial: the floor answers
> `native.mesh.self` from aggregated health that catches up after `start`, so the probe read the
> boot default once the ask had landed and asked again, and the floor tore down the bring-up the
> first ask began. UA-P-0k `22a666f2` restores only while no ask has landed since the link last
> dialed.

**P0-S `1a44b141` — a fieldd restarted under a surviving floor re-places its tailnet door.** Found building TP-R21's two-boot row, which hung dialing the phone's door: `MeshClient` ADOPTED any desired serve the floor already listed, and `serve.list` carries no target, secret or allow to compare — so a restarted fieldd kept its predecessor's `product` serve, aimed at the dead fieldd's ephemeral control port and gated by the dead boot's path secret, until the floor restarted. Measured before the fix: the target stayed on the first fieldd's port six seconds after the second bound its own; a graceful stop does not withdraw it either. On the product path that is the phone's door on 9423 forwarding to nothing after any fieldd-only restart. As built: `placed` records the serves THIS client added; a desired serve the node lists that is not in it is a predecessor's and first sight REPLACES it (remove, then add); AH-1's `artifact-` serves are adopted as before (their durable queue owns them); F-M5's failed-removal rule holds. This is the restart half of the C3 debt UA-4 recorded as latent (§UA-4 carries a dated note); its in-boot half stands.

**TP-R21 `a00b0329` — a restarted fieldd mints every client new.** fieldd's generation ledgers are memory-only and restart at 1; the cells outlive fieldd and keep each connection set's high-water for `maxGrantLifetimeMs` + skew. Safe for windows (Electron main's `FielddDaemonBootFence` replaces every renderer document), not for a tailnet caller: `tailnet:<login>#<node>` is the phone's identity before and after, so its first grant after a restart sat below the old high-water — `GRANT_GENERATION_ROLLBACK`, retryable false, a lockout up to ten minutes (found by reading; not observed). As built: `mintedClientId(principal, epoch)` = the identity + `~` + a fresh epoch per minter (one per TerminalService, one per fieldd boot), on every grant, windows included; `clientIdFor` stays the pure identity. The TPv3 spec's §Generation ownership rested the reset on the fence; it carries a dated delta (`draft/`).

**P0-F `fdc69df2` — the board's two carriers are asked the same question.** TM-2 F-M4's rows asserted the slice carrier published nothing, "because boot() leaves the product serve as it finds it" — false since TM-r4's first refresh always declares, so they held only while the row beat the publisher's 250 ms flush (red at 1654 ms under a 23-file run, green at 463 ms alone). They now wait for the slice and ask it what they ask the door.

**P0-C `e5c68d54` — the phone renews its write grant, and a lapsed grant re-attaches.** `RoutedTerminalClient.renew` had no caller: every phone attach lost input at 540 s, and at 600 s the cell's tick revoked the whole activation (`right-revoked`), which the client mapped to `.ended` and the card to "this session ended" over a running PTY. As built: `Options.renewalProvider`; a per-session renewal scheduled on every `ControlLegAttached`, due 30 s before the cell's 60 s margin, one `requestId` per scheduled renewal reused across retries; a lapse (`right-revoked`, `attach-deadline`) re-attaches with a fresh ticket — over the live legs when the fresh mint names the same connection set, dialing its own otherwise — and reads `.attaching`, never `.ended`; every other revoke still ends. A latent stall fixed on the way: an attach refused `GRANT_INVALID`/`GRANT_GENERATION_ROLLBACK` went through `requestFreshTicket`, whose `.reconnecting` left `open` no branch that attaches over live legs — the card said "connecting…" for good. `TerminalAttachment.RenewalDoor`, `FieldLink.renewTerminalGrant`, `HomeScreen` wiring.

**P0-E `c6a8a39a` — the note TM-r7 read carries its correction.** TM-r7's "renewal itself is NOT built, a product-wide follow-up shared with the renderer's `session-grants.ts`" was wrong about the renderer when it was written: since TP-S3-production (`67c043d9`, 2026-08-23) ghosttea-react's routed runtime schedules `renewAttach` through the door `routed/host.ts` gives it. The line it was read from — `session-grants.ts`'s "Nothing schedules anything today", true only of its own field — carries a dated correction, and so does §TM-r. Comment only.

**Witnesses.** fieldd: link-service 22 · link-posture-daemon 1 · mesh-client 17 · product-serve-restart 1 · terminal-grants 18 · terminal-remote-ticket 8 · agent-field-daemon 3 (×3 alone) · the 25-file terminal/mesh subset 322 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed; real cells accept epoch-scoped grants (terminal-seam 6, terminal-remote-door e2e, terminal-kill-matrix 11). Every new row mutation-probed and restored byte-identical: no daemon wiring reds only the daemon row, no restore the four restore rows and the daemon row, no in-flight guard the "never doubled" row (UA-P-0j); adopting again exactly the replace row and the daemon row (P0-S); no epoch six rows, the control green (TP-R21); a publisher that ignores the doors reading the withholding row (P0-F); dropping the renewal scheduling exactly the two renewal rows, disabling the lapse branch exactly the lapse row, a grant-refused attach routed back through `requestFreshTicket` exactly the refusal row — the stall was real (P0-C). The kit, on a simulator created for the run: 868 tests in 158 suites (862 + 6), no crash restarts; 10 of 11 bundles green, FieldMeshTests red only on its two documented real-time re-ask rows (red alone on main's untouched tree too) and a 40 ms-window row green alone, at a host load average of 600–800; the iOS tree at the tip is byte-identical to the one it ran. The gate ran at the lane's P0-C tip over `bc15f28f`, every `pnpm verify` step one by one (preflight stops on the tracked `VibeField Mock.xcscheme` filename before anything runs): check:deps, check:ios-fixtures, icons:check, typecheck (25 projects), cargo fmt, clippy, bundle:assert, test:rust (263 passed, 9 ignored) and gen:check green; lint red only on main's nine `useAriaPropsSupportedByRole` errors in `docs/agent-plane/*.html`; `pnpm test` 22 of 25 projects green — contracts red on main's own `screenshot-service.*.json` fixtures, which `a3ebbb83`/`bc15f28f` added with no schema mapped (the package was byte-identical to main's), and three timing rows at a load average of 284–413, each green alone three times: fieldd's UA-P-4 board row (untouched here — it polls for ANY write and reads the last, the race P0-F took out of the F-M4 rows), PRC-2's drain deadline (199 ms against 175) and field-app's DocManager first run (5.3 s); fieldd 954 passed / 14 skipped, field-app 941. ## UA-P-0k — a `disabled` read just after the posture ask landed is the floor's lag, not a forgotten posture (2026-09-24; `22a666f2`)

**Found live, minutes after §P0 landed.** The dev runner rebuilt fieldd and bounced the pair; the new fieldd's first boot logged `fieldd.link.posture_restored {mode: linked}` at 04:07:41.704Z, 8 ms after `fieldd.native_link.connected`, and the floor brought its tailnet node up at 04:07:45 (`field_native.mesh.node_ready`, on James's tailnet) — UA-P-0j's first live run, and a double ask: the boot's `native.mesh.start` had landed before the probe read `disabled`. Cause, read at source: the floor answers `native.mesh.self` from its AGGREGATED health (`mgmt/mesh.rs` `unavailable()` reads `health_tx`), which its own task refreshes after `start` has set the unit (`services/mesh.rs` `Shared::set` → `lib.rs` `health_refresh`), so the boot default can outlive the ask that ended it; and a second `start` with no node installed tears down the bring-up the first began and builds another. Here it cost milliseconds (one sidecar start in the floor log); nothing bounds it under load, and `begin()` — the Link Tailscale account click — awaits its probe right after its ask, so every link click was exposed the same way.

**As built.** `postureLanded`: set when a `native.mesh.start` answers; cleared by a new ask, a re-dial (a respawned floor holds nothing), `stopNode` and unlink. The probe restores only on `disabled` with nothing in flight and nothing landed since the link last dialed; a refused ask never counts as landed, so the next probe that finds `disabled` still asks again with no re-dial. The mock floor models the lag on opt-in (`meshHealthLag`, `meshStaleAnswers`), answering the stale read in its own write after the `start` answer, as the floor's writer task does.

**Witnesses.** link-service 24 (the stale read after landing — two probes, one ask — and only a re-dial makes `disabled` evidence again; a link click asked once over a stale read; an ask that never landed asked again with no re-dial) · link-posture-daemon 2 (a cold linked boot over a lagging floor asked once, the stale read pinned as having happened). Mutation probes, each restored byte-identical: no landed guard reds exactly the three stale-read rows, the daemon row among them, so it is not vacuous; a refused ask counted as landed reds exactly the never-landed row; a re-dial that does not clear it reds the five restore rows. Rebased over main's `a9a0f739` before landing (range-diff identical); the fieldd suite at `22a666f2` (rosetta at its pin): tsc clean, 960 passed / 14 skipped and two rows red at a load average near 120 — doc-service's restart row and a rosettad index-doors row — both files green alone, then red alone on three other rows at load 238 (9 s timeouts): the host's load, in files this commit does not touch. §P0's UA-P-0j paragraph carries the dated correction.

**Not witnessed.** The fix on the live stack; it takes effect at the first fieldd boot after it lands.

## GT-7 — Settings → Terminal, rebuilt: one page over two owners, the loader's dry run on every draft, the viewer's glass v2, and the chords VibeField keeps (2026-09-24; d1952af6 gate · 0f97948b GT-7a · 451941e0 GT-7b · 21168bf3 GT-7c · a3d277b1 GT-7d · 12d6c2b4 GT-7e, branch `gt/terminal-settings`)

`terminal.config.validate` (the dry run), `.import`, `.export`, `.reveal` — `settings.manage`, local; the includes rule as a pure contract function; the write refusal (`includes-changed` | `blocking-errors`) and the conflict (`{current}`) as schemas; two internal shell-provider methods (`shell.dialog.pickFile` / `saveFile`, purpose-literal) — ESR §6.2's provider, no preload growth. *fieldd and main (GT-7b, builder `gt7-daemon`):* the snapshot projected field by field; validate = byte bound → saved document → includes rule judged ALONE (no load) → the dry run, whose BLOCKING set is ghosttea desktop's `blockingConfigDiagnostics` ported whole against a baseline that is a fresh dry run of the SAVED text (the cell's snapshot is as old as its last reload — a deliberate deviation from the brief, pinned by a row); write re-checks revision → includes → blocking before the disk moves; import opens non-blocking, regular files only, 64 KiB + 1, fatal UTF-8; export temp + fsync + durable rename, audited by bytes; reveal the file or its folder; scope and timing facts on every section (DESIGN.md §8); THIS WINDOW's look applies as it changes, THIS MAC's edits collect in one save bar; the controls write only ghosttea's managed block and only what the floor applies (palette, scrollback, keybinds — GT-D20); the Keyboard tab lays the loader's effective list over Ghostty's 86 macOS chords with who decided each row and what it does in the deck (ghosttea's router, the binding's own `performable:` flag); the editor places the loader's diagnostics on their lines; ## AR-S4a–b — Extensions: every agent's plugins, marketplaces, MCP servers and skills read per profile from its own stores, and each Agent Profile's servers and skills on its page (2026-09-25; `fb582770`, puppeteer `63bf175` pinned)

**James:** "managing the 3 for each agent under each agent page can be quite inconvinient … maybe under agent profile page, there can also be 2 new sections, for global skills and MCPs that can be easily toggled for each agent?" — the design record's pass 24 answered it (Version 9); "good, go with recommand, plan and start implementation"; "go ahead"; "commit".

**puppeteer `f5c3b5f` + `63bf175`.** The eight research reports (`draft/*-PLUGINS-SKILLS-MCP.md`, probed 2026-09-24) committed as the evidence. RFC 006 C1: Core's extensions contract — four kinds, where each item comes from (own, project, plugin, bundled, managed, agent, borrowed), items every profile shares, each agent's support per kind, inventories that name what a read could not cover — and never a secret: a server's environment and headers are names, and `describeMcpUrl` / `describeMcpCommand` mask userinfo, query and credential-shaped arguments. The runtime's `extensionInventory(provider, profile?)`. Eight adapters, each from what the agent itself reads: Claude Code's store files (never `claude mcp list`, which connects); Codex's app-server and `codex mcp list --json`, whose environment and header values are dropped; Grok (with what it borrows from Claude Code and Cursor), Kimi, OpenCode (one config for every profile), Pi, Hermes and Antigravity from their own files. Copilot has none yet (no report). The built-in providers take a `home` that every native-default root and reader hangs off.

**The host's half.** contracts `agent-extensions.ts`: the lens, `AgentsExtensionsListResult`, and the doors `agents.extensions.list {set, refresh?}` and `.subscribe {set}` on `agents.manage`. fieldd `agent-extensions.ts`: `buildExtensionLens` (pure — rows by name in the profile's agent order; a server's versions told apart by its masked target and the names it reads, a skill's by its folder) and `AgentExtensionService` (read when asked, one read per profile at a time, the last kept, a frame when a read finishes, read again on a registry change only while watched; never polled); the built-in providers get a home only when fieldd was given one, so production reads where each agent would. field-app: the profile page's MCP servers and Skills — pass 24's L2 grid, read-only: a row per name some agent holds as its own, its cells in pass 24's states and words, a row opening in place to each agent's own holding, the rest counted beneath, "Built from what …'s agents already have", "Read again"; `ProfilePageView`'s `extensions` slot; the catalog's profile states show it, and a "reading extensions" state. api.html gains the two doors.

**Witness.** puppeteer: every touched package's suite (core 173, runtime 232, Claude 256, Codex 160, Grok 117, Kimi 114, OpenCode 99, Pi 53, Hermes 94, Antigravity 62, builtin-providers 23 — one reading through the real runtime on a temp home), typecheck, `packages:check`, `groundtruth:mapping:check` (Codex's map re-locked for the four methods it calls), Prettier; `format:check` flags only the committed `scripts/capture-swarm-states.mjs`. ## GT-8 — terminal links: ghosttea 0.12.0 pinned, a ⌘-clicked web link opens through fieldd, and a race TC-S3 carried is closed (2026-09-25; `14ac43fc` GT-8a · `b76644a0` GT-8b · `811329ca` GT-8c · `0db71c10` GT-8d, branch `gt/8-links`)

**James:** GT-7 left one thing owed: a ghosttea release carrying `link-url` and ⌘-click links, which was a public publish and his call. He chose the full release (push, PR, merge, a signed tag, the CI publish), once he knew the eight link commits were his own unpushed local work, and chose GT-8 to follow it: the pin, the Links switch, the opener. During the publish his words were "publish failed", then "can we fix this tedious CI once and for all", then "do them for me" (merge the fix once green; finish the GitHub release if it took another rerun), and "continue". Every `release` environment approval was his own.

**What is real.**

*Upstream (ghosttea, James's repo).* 0.12.0 was a 0.x minor, not 0.11.2, by ghosttea's own CHANGELOG 0.10.0 rule, because `2660c4a` adds public fields to two published structs.
- PR #63 merged as `a0d657d`, and the Apple artifact `ghosttea-apple-native-a5fa7ef2afc2` was published and pinned (`caa4a56`).
- The tag `v0.12.0` is signed with James's key, and publish run 36117528614 shipped 7 crates, 10 npm packages and the GitHub release, each checked on its registry.
- The run needed five attempts, each behind his approval. Every failure was npm recording a version 56 s to 4m 09s after accepting it (the registry's `time[version]` against each job log's `+` line), against the helper's ~2.5 min.
- PR #64 (`52bde2d`) fixes that for the next release. The publisher waits once per dependency layer, which the manifests decide, and gives each package 20 minutes (`REGISTRY_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`, set in the workflow so a retry can raise it). A rerun waits out an accepted-but-unrecorded version instead of failing. 11 tests replay the measured delays, and each of 8 mutations fails at least one.

*GT-8a (phase 1, builder `gt8-links`).* The wire and the door:
- `terminal.link.open`, under the scope `terminal.link` that only the window's token holds, and main's internal `shell.openLink`.
- fieldd's policy (`terminal-links.ts`). http(s) goes to the browser, and main re-checks it against its own contract. A `file:` path on this device is shown in Finder, never opened. Anything else is refused before main is asked. The audit records the opener and the scheme, never the URL.
- `TerminalConfigSnapshot.linkUrl` and the page's `ManagedValues.linkUrl`.

*GT-8b.*
- EL8, one event, 0.11.1 → 0.12.0: the cargo pin, the four npm overrides, the six age-gate rows and preflight's five rows. Both lockfiles moved only the ghosttea closure (six crates, six packages). The iOS kit stays at 0.10.1 (GM-D7).
- `pnpm gen`: `link-url` reads as applied.
- The opener is the runtime platform's `openExternal`, one per window (terminal-pool `ensureRuntime`), and asks fieldd for web links only.
- Behavior → Links is a This Mac switch over the managed block's `link-url`, and the 0.11.1 fallback is deleted.

*GT-8c.* A session fieldd just birthed is dialed at the cell that took it (see Found).

*GT-8d.*
- In every smoke-like mode, main's OS opener records instead of opening, so no harness run touches the user's browser or Finder.
- Smoke row 11f is the live witness.
- Row 9's errata.

**Found.**
- *TC-S3 carried a race.* A session no observed inventory had placed read as the INTERACTIVE cell's. field-native lists a birth one reconcile tick later (its 100 ms floor), so a terminate or `automate` into a just-born agent session could reach a cell that never held it. That cell answered "unknown session", and terminate returned `{terminated: false}` for a PTY that went on running.
  - How it surfaced: agent-session's default-profile row terminated 66–121 ms after the birth, against 86–112 ms from birth to listing. It failed four of five alone runs at the 0.12.0 pin.
  - It is latent on main, not a 0.12.0 regression: the 0.11.1 control passed the same row by 9 ms.
  - How it was traced: file-written probes into fieldd plus a detached control worktree at main, after the first reading ("load 245, a lottery") was checked instead of believed.
  - `birth()` knew the cell all along, so GT-8c records it until the inventory places the session or it exits. The new TC-S3 row is red without the fix and green with it; the real-floor file passes 3/3 at load 275.
- *0.12.0 reports a local session's SPAWN directory from creation* (`session.rs` seeds the summary's `cwd` with the directory its link finder resolves relative paths against). It falsified "the spawn directory is never reported" in five places: `deck-restore.ts`, `GodviewDeck.tsx`, two godview-deck-frames comments and smoke row 9. Each got a dated correction at its source.
  - A shell with no OSC 7 now restores in its own folder on this Mac, and a peer's pane still restores at home.
  - Row 9's `rehydratedCwd` is now a plain path from creation.
  - The Windows finding narrows but stands: a Windows pane now persists its spawn directory, but `paneCwd` takes no drive path, and cmd.exe still never says where a `cd` went.
- *ghosttea's link hook names no session.* `openExternal(url)` receives the URL alone, so a file link cannot be told from a path on a PEER's pane, and revealing this Mac's file of that name would show the wrong one. The deck asks for web links only, and GT-D22's file half is built, unit-tested and unreached. This is petition G29.
- The builder ran out of context mid-phase-2, in the page test. The orchestrator reviewed its work, finished the key-catalog row and the errata, and built GT-8c and GT-8d.

**Witness.** The lane was rebased onto `fb9dbad0` after AR-S4a–b and AR-S4b2 landed beneath it. The four code commits are patch-identical (`git range-diff`), and the lane's own puppeteer checkout was moved to the new pin `63bf175`.

  - Tests in every project: field-app 107 files / 1061 passed; fieldd 1005 passed / 14 skipped; electron-shell 774 passed / 2 skipped. 22 of the 25 test targets were Nx cache hits on identical inputs that had passed; the rest ran fresh.
