  - the godview monitor's "WEBGPU UNAVAILABLE" state read while still "starting";
  - terminal-settings' theme-browser row at 5 s;
  - fieldd's UA-P-4 board row and service-drain-deadline, GT-7's recorded lottery rows.

  Each passed alone or on the next run. Nx then REPLAYED field-app's cached failure for unchanged inputs, so field-app was run fresh (`nx run @vibefield/field-app:test --skip-nx-cache`, 107 files / 1050 passed, on `97ddf8b6`) before the verbatim gate. After the second rebase, AR-S4b2's changes made field-app run fresh by itself. The agent-session row was the race above, not load.

## AR-S4c — the acts, first slice: what an agent holds turned on, off or out through its own command or protocol, from the grid's cells (2026-09-25; `bd87ef52`, puppeteer `7926ca9` pinned)

**James:** "go ahead" (after AR-S4b2's commit); "commit".

**puppeteer `7926ca9` (RFC 006 C2's first slice).** Core: acts (`enable`, `disable`, `remove`); a plan that says what runs — the agent's own command as argv plus the variables that point it at the profile, or a call on its protocol — and what it reaches beyond its one item (the definition, a remote server's sign-in, every profile, a shared folder), or why the agent cannot (`in-app`, `no-command`, `not-own`, `not-held`); the receipt; `EXTENSION_COMMAND_NAME`, which keeps a name that could be read as a flag or a path out of an argv. Runtime `extensions/act.ts`: `planExtensionAct`, `extensionActPlans` (every act for items a read found, without a second read) and `runExtensionAct` — a fresh read finds the item, the adapter plans, a command runs through the update runner (no stdin, its own process group, the clean environment with the plan's variables, the agent's own folder as cwd, two minutes) or the adapter performs a protocol call, and a second fresh read decides the receipt, never the output. What each agent offers, from James's reports: Codex (a user-layer server on and off through the app-server's `config/value/write` of `mcp_servers.<name>.enabled`, `codex mcp remove`, a shared skill switched for one profile through `skills/config/write`); Grok (`grok mcp enable|disable`, `grok mcp remove --scope user`); Antigravity (`agy mcp enable|disable` under the profile's HOME); Claude Code (no switch for a whole profile, so `claude mcp remove --scope user`, which reaches the definition and a remote server's sign-in); Hermes (`hermes mcp remove`); Kimi, OpenCode and Pi say why not, in their own words.

**VibeField.** contracts: a holding carries `acts` (the command as a person reads it, what it reaches), the lens carries `run`, the door `agents.extensions.act {set, provider, kind, id, act}` on `agents.manage` (local, not idempotent), fixture `agents-extensions-act`. fieldd: acts planned over the same read; `act()` runs only what its last read offered on that holding, one at a time per profile (`CONFLICT`), its output on the profile's frames, the profile read fresh after; audited as `agents.extensions.act`. field-app: a cell with an act is a button (on turns off, or removes where the agent has no switch; off turns on); a click that reaches further opens P7's two-step confirm beneath its list, naming what goes and the command; every cell holds while an act runs; the run card (the command, Running…/Finished, the output, the outcome in words); an item's page gives each agent its switch or its Remove…. Catalog: act confirm, act running, act finished. api.html: the door.

**Witness.** puppeteer: repo typecheck; core 178, runtime 239, Codex 164, Grok 119, Antigravity 63, Claude 258, Hermes 95, Kimi 115, OpenCode 100, Pi 54, builtin-providers 24 — one act through the real runtime and the real Claude adapter on a temp home, its runner faked; `packages:check`, `groundtruth:mapping:check` (Codex's map re-locked for the two writes), Prettier on the touched sources. VibeField, in a clean worktree (puppeteer at `7926ca9`, rosetta at its pin), first on GT-8's `909b116a`: typecheck 25/25 (no cache), contracts 538, field-app 1068 (two timeouts at load ≈530, both green rerun alone); then at `bd87ef52` on `0a419acf`: field-app's typecheck and its touched suites again. fieldd's files are byte-identical to James's tree, where its extension service (14) and the doors — a protocol act through the real daemon, audited, no process started — passed, and its full suite went green once its load failures were rerun (load 400–800). No vendor binary ran; no act has met a real agent yet. The catalog captured in headless Chrome, light and dark.

**Found.** Claude Code turns a server off only per project, inside `/mcp`: for a whole profile its only "off" is removal, which takes a remote server's sign-in. Antigravity's `mcp disable` of a name it never had writes a stub, so only names a read found are offered; its `mcp remove` was never probed and is not offered. `main` moved twice under this work — GT-8's five commits, then `0a419acf` (Godview's swarm and pane fix) during the verification: the code was rebuilt on `0a419acf` (no file shared), field-app typechecked and its Godview, extensions, profiles and catalog suites run again there (199), and the two files GT-8 also touched (`methods.ts`, `daemon.ts`) differ from `main` by this change alone. `godview-monitor.test.tsx`'s "WEBGPU UNAVAILABLE" test fails at `0a419acf` itself too (A/B in the same worktree): flaky, not this change's.

**Owed.** S4c's next slice: a server's sign-in and sign-out (a terminal, like the profile sign-in). S4d, adding once: the definition and the secret kept once, so a cell can turn on for an agent that does not hold it; "Use this one everywhere"; "Remove from Work". Pass 24's "settings with no command" (write those few keys, or ask the vendors) is James's to decide. The first real acts belong on a throwaway profile: `claude mcp remove --scope user` and whether `hermes`/`grok mcp remove` ask to confirm come from the reports, not a live run. AR-D29 and AR-D30 await ratification.
## AC — the agent catalog (2026-09-22)

**The question (James):** does VibeField have a single source of control on the agents it supports?
It did not — puppeteer composed ten providers behind five uncross-checked lists, rosetta registered
nine kinds in one Rust registry, VibeField joined them at runtime by native layout root with no
tripwire between the siblings, three spellings of one agent on the surfaces, no tiers and no place
to record a decision (`draft/thinking-ar-agent-catalog.md` §1). **The ruling:** "deciding what agent to
support is a decision to make, maintain, track" — a HAND-MAINTAINED catalog, verified by the gate
(AC-D1…AC-D11; the DECISIONS row is owed, see AC-6 below). Six slices, one day, one linear chain on main:

- **AC-1 `5f09ef2b`** — `packages/contracts/src/agent-catalog.ts`: `AGENT_CATALOG`, ten rows in display order,
  each a decision (`status`, the two seam ids, the layout root both siblings must spell alike, `offers`,
  `surfaces`, `admitted`, `decision`); STRICT row schema, tolerant wire form; the readers; two generated
  projections under `gen:check` (`gen/agent-catalog.json` for preflight, `fixtures/agent-catalog.valid.json`
  for the phone); the `agent.catalog` door row; the dated erratum in `agent-index.ts`'s header. Contracts
  27 files / 499 rows.
- **docs `7f2978be` + `2f9298a5`** — the three agent-plane pages linted red (biome lints HTML: `aria-label` on
  plain divs), found by AC-1's gate — the docs wave had landed them with a link check, not the gate.
- **AC-3 `e9733df4`** (+ `9cf86be7` typecheck fixups, `190932ed` the wire opened) — fieldd answers from the catalog:
  `agent.providers` iterates the visible rows (status, offers, OUR label, the index's state where history is
  offered, `available`/`resumable` as this device's facts); `agent.catalog {surface?}`; typed refusals
  (no row NOT_FOUND, a row not offering the capability PRECONDITION_FAILED `unsupported-agent`) on spawn,
  personas, update, setActive; resume and the login pane need the agent VISIBLE; releases and usage
  enumerate only offering rows; the executables map over catalog ids (the sibling's closed kind union
  gone from fieldd); `kindFor` reads the row and the roll call WITNESSES (`fieldd.agents.catalog_drift`
  withholds); AC-D8 — a daemon refusal at start (`unknown agent kind`) retires the refused roots and the
  supervisor's own retry brings the index up — **erratum 2026-09-22 (the review): as landed here this was
  BLIND on the real daemon** — the supervisor's failure detail cut a real root's line off before the reason
  (`bfda5f0a` keeps the lines whole) and the real daemon prefixes every stderr line `rosettad: `
  (`09e69344` accepts it; a live row at `f4d99bff` proves the wording against the pinned binary); the
  record row carries `refused: {detail}`, the projection `refused: {reason}` (never a path); the kill-matrix
  row's premise — a persona ENROLLED with no daemon — was itself withdrawn by the review (the witness is
  mandatory, `f4d99bff`); `index.*` rows carry `agent`. `status`/`history` are OPEN strings on the wire
  (AC-4's finding: a closed enum refused a whole list on one unknown word). Eight agent suites green.
- **DEV `c5804e6a`** — the dev runner leaked the shell's `FIELDD_ROSETTAD_BIN` into Electron's env past a null
  resolver (`electron-stack.test.mjs:118` red on every lane's gate — the briefed command and CI export it);
  found by AC-2's gate; `unset` when the resolver names none, 97/98 → 98/98.
- **AC-1 erratum `5931ee9d`** — R23's FIRST run on the real pins: antigravity claimed personas; puppeteer's

## P0-H — Phase 0 on hardware: the phone held a live terminal on this desktop for ten minutes and twenty seconds, and the four things in its way are fixed (2026-09-25; `d2c761b8` P0-H1 · `abc6f9f8` P0-H2 · `b7bbcbc3` P0-H3, branch `p0/hardware`)

**The witness.** James: "for phase 0, i just plugged in my iphone, can you use it instead?" (2026-09-24 22:57), then "you run the desktop", then the hands-on part handed to a computer-use agent ("i think i will hand over this to another agent that is good at computer use"), which drove the phone through the day of 2026-09-25 and left its journal in `work/phase0-debug-2026-09-25.md` and its result in `work/phase0-result-2026-09-25.md` (both untracked, with the raw evidence beside them). What this entry asserts it re-read in the desktop's own audit ledger, `users/1/audit/own-actions.2026-09.fieldd-653510557bf142e6.jsonl`: the first `tailnet` rows this desktop has ever written — `terminal.ticket.mint` at 00:04:11.316Z (2026-09-26 UTC; 17:04 PDT the 25th), actor `tailnet` / the linked login, provenance `ws-tailnet`, target `58b5e140-…`; `terminal.attach.renew` at 00:12:41.314Z, the same actor and target, 510 s after the mint — P0-C's schedule to the second (the 600 s grant less the cell's 60 s margin less the 30 s headroom); nothing between them, so the activation never re-minted. The phone's own report (`phone-debug13-summary.json`): one activation `act-0e65e3cb-…` live from 00:04:13Z to 00:14:33Z, 315 samples three seconds apart at most, every one live with the lease held and input allowed, and three unsubmitted markers typed into the Codex session's prompt and seen in the app's own window captures — at 6 s, at 546 s (after minute nine) and at 616 s (after minute ten, past the original grant's 00:14:11 expiry, which only the renewal could have carried it over). Nothing was submitted and no agent ran; the session was a dedicated one James approved ("go ahead") and it was closed after the run. No `tailnet` row exists in any user's grants ledger, and none should: a product hello writes no audit row, the first audited act of a tailnet caller is its ticket.

**What stood in the way, in the order the day met it.** Four defects, none of them in the record before, each fixed at source with a witness, all landed here. (The "mesh failed" of the night before never recurred and has no cause; a Release build starts its mesh only from the account menu's Connect.)

**P0-H1 `d2c761b8` — the phone's door is reachable: an ATS exception for MagicDNS hosts.** The phone's first probe of the desktop's door, `http://truffle-vibefield-jamess-macbook-pro-9-local.tail17c2fd.ts.net:9423/`, died in the phone's own URL loader with `NSURLErrorDomain -1022`: App Transport Security requires TLS and cannot see that the request rides Truffle's authenticated WireGuard transport. As built: `apps/ios/App/Info.plist`, merged by Xcode into the generated bundle metadata in both configurations (`INFOPLIST_FILE` beside `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE`), carrying one `NSExceptionDomains` entry — `ts.net` with subdomains, insecure HTTP allowed — and nothing global; an on-device control against `http://phase0-ats-check.invalid/` still answered -1022, so other domains keep their ATS. `apps/ios/README.md` carries the reasoning, which is also the App Store review justification.

**P0-H2 `abc6f9f8` — the floor answers its heartbeat while a mesh listener waits: mesh requests enter one bounded FIFO worker.** With the door reachable, the desktop fell over: native control went `unresponsive` right after mesh startup on four consecutive floor boots, the supervisor spent its three restarts and reported `gone`, and every terminal roster read empty. Temporary tracing narrowed it to `native.mesh.serve.add` waiting in `tsnet.ListenTLS` (the artifact serves' TLS listeners, 1.8 s and 0.5 s on the one boot that recovered) — and the management dispatcher awaited every request in its socket reader, so the ping the supervisor's watchdog sends rode the same reader and starved behind the listener; the wedge the record's UA-P-0d rows called a floor hang was this. As built (design-02 §2.7's dated correction, written before the code): authenticated `native.mesh.*` requests are enqueued to one daemon-owned worker — one per server, not per client, so a replacement fieldd's replay cannot race its predecessor's in-flight node change — bounded by `MESH_CONTROL_LIMITS.MGMT_PENDING_MESH_REQUESTS` (32, generated into `registries.rs` like the byte budget beside it; the review moved it there from a literal) and by the existing `MGMT_QUEUED_BYTES`, the in-flight request's bytes included; enqueue never waits, saturation answers retryable `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`; the worker re-checks the current paired client before each request and drops a superseded or disconnected client's queued work, while an operation already started finishes; the reader, the hello gate and the writer are untouched, so the heartbeat passes a waiting mesh call. The supervisor's watchdog deadlines did not move. `mgmt/mesh.rs`'s note that the target path was "VERIFIED" for every proxied request carries its erratum (below). Three real-socket rows in `services/mesh.rs` hold a store lock to make a mesh call slow deterministically: the ping passes it and the mesh replies keep their order; a superseded client's queued `retire` never runs; forty stops saturate the queue and are refused without parking the reader.

**The fix that is not ours — T6, the sidecar's WebSocket forward keeps the route's target path.** Reachable and answered, the phone was refused: `failed("invalid token")`. truffle 0.7.14's `sidecar-slim/main.go` builds every route's HTTP handler with `httputil.NewSingleHostReverseProxy`, whose director joins the target's `/t/<secret>` onto the request path — that is how UA-P-0d keeps the per-boot secret off the tailnet — but its WebSocket branch hijacks the connection and forwards the ORIGINAL request after optional mount stripping, target path and query dropped. fieldd's `ProductApi.classifyDoor` then saw `/`, classified the upgrade as the LOCAL door, and refused a tokenless hello. The fix (a real-listener regression that failed before and passes after, the copied Go suite green) stores each route's director and runs it before the hijack; it is a truffle change and is filed as petition **T6** (`draft/petitions/T6-truffle-sidecar-websocket-target-path.md`, the patch beside it, `git apply --check` clean against `9f0d6287`). Until a released sidecar carries it, the desktop runs a locally built one: `.vibefield/sidecar/sidecar-slim-0.7.14-ws-target-path` (its provenance and the patched sources beside it), named by `.env`'s `FIELD_NATIVE_SIDECAR_PATH` — a local override, not a pin move; `siblings.lock.json` and the npm sidecar are unchanged.

**P0-H3 `b7bbcbc3` — the phone attaches frames only after the cell acknowledges control, and one writer owns each leg's socket.** Admitted, the first attach raced: four ticket mints in twenty seconds (22:56:03Z–22:56:21Z) before the card went live. The routed client sent `AttachControlLeg` and `AttachFramesLeg` at once on two sockets, and the cell creates the activation on the control attach and only BINDS it on the frames attach — frames arriving first earned `ACTIVATION_CONFLICT` and a fresh ticket. As built (TPv3 §5.4's dated ordering correction, written first): frames is sent once per activation, on the matching `ControlLegAttached`; a stale acknowledgement authorizes nothing, and neither a duplicate acknowledgement nor an accepted renewal sends frames again; a replacement activation repeats the ordered handshake and keeps the negotiated resume. Then the residue the first timed run's captures showed (`ph` left of a marker its backspaces should have cleared): the leg sent each message in its own task, and a task can overtake a suspended earlier `send` — the regression observed sequences 2…12, 1. As built (§5.4's writer correction): one serial writer per leg for everything after the hello, at most 256 messages and 4 MiB buffered with the write in flight; overflow or a write failure ends the leg and discards what was queued, closing discards likewise, and no input is replayed after a reconnect. Rows: the ordered handshake over the fake cell door and over the real socket (a stale ack, a duplicate, a renewal, a replacement activation); a suspended send never overtaken; a close discarding queued writes; a write failure ending the leg with pending input discarded; the two bounds.

**Witnesses.** The gate, in a lane worktree over main `49407c29` with the pinned rosetta beside it and the pinned rosettad built: `pnpm verify` verbatim stops at typecheck on two errors in `packages/fieldd/src/agent-extensions.ts` (170, 513 — fieldd passes a wider act and outcome union than the type it is checked against), reported through the six projects that reference fieldd; a pristine checkout of `49407c29` fails the same two, so the red is main's own (AR-S4c/AC's drift against the puppeteer pin), and the other 19 projects — contracts with the registry change among them — are clean. The steps after it, run one by one in the same lane: lint 0 errors (36 warnings), `cargo fmt --check`, clippy at `-D warnings`, `bundle:assert` all green; `pnpm test` red on nine files across eight projects at a load average near 600, eight of them green alone a minute later (audit-store, plugin-build, fieldd-client's spine row, godview-deck-frames, logging's writer and sanitizer rows, target-controller, users-file — every one a wall-clock or fuzz row in code this work does not touch) and the ninth, fieldd's two AR-S4b Extensions rows, red alone on the lane and red alone on a pristine checkout of `49407c29` with its own native build — a `ZodError`: puppeteer at the pin reports a `sign-in` act that main's contracts enum (`enable | disable | remove`) does not admit, the same drift as the typecheck; fieldd otherwise 1021 passed / 15 skipped, field-app 1097; `cargo test -p field-native` 140 passed, 1 ignored, one red — logging's `queue_and_ring_stay_bounded…` deadline row at that load, green alone three times — with the three new mesh-control rows green; `gen:check` dirty only on the regenerated `registries.rs` this landing commits, clean once committed. The kit, on a simulator created for the run: 897 tests in 164 suites (868 + 29 new), no crash restarts; the first full run red on TM-5's real-socket attachment row (its harness waited for frames before acknowledging control — the hardware day's runs never covered that bundle; corrected here) and on two documented real-time FieldMeshTests rows at a load average of 480; on the corrected tree 897 with only `FieldLinkScheduleTests`' two re-ask rows red at load 600, both suites green alone a minute later, FieldMesh untouched by this work. The plist: a Release build for a generic iOS device (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`, `-derivedDataPath` of its own) SUCCEEDED and its merged `Info.plist` carries exactly `NSExceptionDomains → ts.net {NSIncludesSubdomains, NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads}` and nothing else under `NSAppTransportSecurity`. The hardware run itself is above; its raw evidence is untracked under `work/phase0-evidence-2026-09-25/`.

**Not witnessed.** A second account on the same tailnet (UA-4's guest refusal on the phone — the desktop half is paid, §UA-P-4d); the phone across a fieldd restart on hardware (TP-R21's re-mint, headless only); a Release build's Connect on the device (the runs used Debug builds with a development auto-connect); input latency — this run establishes continuity, not a benchmark.

**Errata at their sources.** `packages/field-native/src/mgmt/mesh.rs` (the "VERIFIED, not assumed" probe covered ordinary HTTP only — the WebSocket branch was never probed); `draft/design-02-daemons.md` §2.7 and `draft/specs/terminal-pipeline-v3.md` §5.4 carry the dated corrections; §P0's "a phone on hardware holding a session past ten minutes" is now paid.

**Owed.** T6 upstream (James's repo) and the EL8 event that retires the local sidecar override; a Release build on the device through the account menu's Connect, and the TestFlight build that outlives the cable (build 5 from `b25a9ddd` is archived under `apps/ios/build/testflight/`, unsigned for distribution); the UA-P-4 board row and the rest of §P0's owed list; `pnpm commit-draft` for the two spec corrections, T6 and the thinking docs' status lines.

## AR-S4c2 — the acts, second slice: a server's sign-in, the agent's own login in a pane on the page, and its sign-out (2026-09-27; `22f4d299`, puppeteer `1def18f` pinned)

**James:** "continue" (after AR-S4c's first slice); "commit".

**puppeteer `1def18f` (RFC 006 C2's second slice).** Core: acts `sign-in` and `sign-out`; a plan's run `terminal` — the agent's own login opens a browser and may ask for a pasted code, so it runs only in a terminal the person answers; the reason `no-sign-in` (a server on this machine, over WebSocket, or sending its own `Authorization`); the receipt `unconfirmed`, for an agent that keeps its sign-ins where no read looks. **VibeField.** contracts: the acts, `terminal: true` on an act that runs in a pane, `unconfirmed`, the run's pane while it is open; the door `agents.extensions.signIn {set, provider, id}` on `agent.spawn` (a pane is a spawn, as a profile's sign-in is), answering the run and the caller's ticket; `agents.extensions.act` takes every act but sign-in; fixtures (Work gains notion; the sign-in's answer). fieldd: the lens offers a sign-in unless the server is off or the agent says it is signed in, and a sign-out only where it says so; `signIn()` runs what the last read offered, one act at a time per profile; the pane's end settles it, closes the husk and reads the profile again; a pane nobody finishes is settled after ten minutes and left to the person; audited as `agents.extensions.sign_in`. field-app: an item page's agent rows get Sign in (the agent says the server asks), Sign in… (it doesn't say) and Sign out; P7 asks before a sign-in every profile of the agent shares; while one runs, the run card is the sign-in card — the live pane where this window opened it, a line elsewhere, Cancel. **Witness.** puppeteer: repo typecheck; core 20, runtime extensions 19, the eight adapters' extension suites, builtin-providers extensions 4 (a Claude sign-in opened through the real runtime's host); `packages:check`, `groundtruth:mapping:check`, Prettier. No vendor binary ran; no sign-in has met a real agent yet. The catalog captured in headless Chrome, light and dark.

**Found.** Codex keeps a server's OAuth sign-in, off Windows, in the OS keychain under the server's name and a hash of its address — not its `CODEX_HOME` (`compute_store_key` in rmcp-client/src/oauth.rs; the Direct keyring backend is the default there, config/src/types.rs; rust-v0.150.0): one sign-in serves every Codex profile that holds that server at that address. That answers pass 23's open question for Codex. A floor race, fixed in `terminal-service.ts`: GT-8c's `bornIn` forgot a session's birth cell AT its exit, and closing an exited pane is what an exit listener does (MF-1g), so a pane born and ended inside one reconcile tick was closed at the interactive cell ("unknown session") and its husk stood for good — a login pane that quick too. The birth cell now outlives the exit by 30 s; a TC-S3 row pins it (red without the fix: `{terminated: false}`). ## AR-S4d — adding once, first slice: a server kept once for an Agent Profile and turned on for an agent that holds none of it, its keys in the keychain and given at launch (2026-09-27; `4f6a7a4b0b9023848a2df2ec79b159bbbc070d6c`, puppeteer `524709b` pinned)

**James:** "go ahead" (after AR-S4c2, whose report named S4d next); "commit".

**puppeteer `524709b` (RFC 006 C2's third slice).** Core: a read server's `definition` (`McpServerDefinition`: a stdio command line with the NAMES of the variables it reads, or an http/sse address), set by `mcpServerDefinition` only when the agent's own command line or address needed no masking, names no variable inside itself and sends no header; act `add`; the reasons `held` (the agent holds one of its own by that name, which its add would replace) and `unsupported`. Runtime: an add plans from the server as the agent would hold it once a fresh read finds the name unheld, and the second read holding it is the receipt; `launchEnvironment({providerId, profileSetId, profileId?})`, asked once per spawn and resume after the account resolves — its names checked (none the environment or a loader relies on, no `*_HOME`, `*_DIR` or `XDG_*` root), the values handed to the adapter and kept out of the captured continuation, every fingerprint, any prepared recipe and every log. The built-ins merge them beneath each launch's own variables where the agent's MCP client runs: the terminal's environment, or Codex's app-server's and Grok's leader's (whose backend key is now a digest). Per agent, each naming a variable in its own syntax and never its value: Claude Code `claude mcp add <name> --scope user -e N=${N:-} -- …`; Codex a `config/value/write` of the whole `mcp_servers.<name>` table with `env_vars`; Grok `grok mcp add --scope user --env N=${N:-} <name> -- …`; OpenCode `opencode mcp add <name> --env N={env:N} -- …` into its one config (every profile); Antigravity only a server that reads no variable (it keeps values as literals); Hermes and Kimi in their apps.

**VibeField.** contracts: the definition, act `add`, a row's `definition` · `kept` · `needs` · `offers`, the lens's `values` (names), `values` on the act door, the doors `agents.extensions.add` (agents.manage, not idempotent) and `agents.extensions.plan` (idempotent), the store's file (`AgentExtensionKeep`), LAYOUT `AGENT_EXTENSIONS_DIR` (with the golden vector; the Rust registries and gen/layout.json regenerated from it); fixtures (Work keeps context7, whose key it holds no value for yet, and offers notion to Grok and OpenCode; the add's and the plan's answers). fieldd: `agent-extension-store.ts` — per profile `agents/extensions/<set>.json` (0600) with the kept definitions, the value NAMES and which names each agent was given; the values in the keychain through the P5 `SecretStore` (service "VibeField agent server values", one entry per profile), read only to start an agent they were given to. The lens offers each empty cell the agent's own add, planned from the same read; a remove keeps the definition first; the act's add keeps the values and the definition, then records what the agent was given; `add()` refuses a definition that hides a key, a reserved name and a name the lens shows, then runs each agent in turn holding the profile, each run showing its agent's own line; `plan()`; the runtime's `launchEnvironment` answers from the store; a deleted profile forgets its keep and its keychain entry; audited as `agents.extensions.add`, the values counted, never recorded. field-app: an empty cell turns the server on for its agent; a key the server reads is asked for first, in the confirm, one password field per name (and, on This Mac, that an agent started outside VibeField gets none); P7 before OpenCode's every-profile add; Add server… beside Read again, and its page — Name, Connects to, Command or URL, Environment, Turn on for (chosen where the add is quiet and this profile's alone, greyed with the agent's own reason), Runs, planned as the form rests; the item page's Turn on and a kept server's facts; the I1 line counts only servers some agent holds. Catalog: turn on, add server. api.html: the two doors and the act door's add; 39 doors on the api and system pages.

**Witness.** puppeteer, in a clean worktree at `524709b`: every package and both apps typecheck; core 184, runtime 249, builtin-providers 26, claude 263, codex 169, grok 124, antigravity 67, opencode 105, hermes 98, kimi 117, pi 54 (skips are the live suites); `packages:check`, `groundtruth:mapping:check`, Prettier on the touched files. VibeField, in a clean worktree at `4f6a7a4b0b9023848a2df2ec79b159bbbc070d6c` (puppeteer at `524709b`, rosetta at its pin, James's built field-native linked): typecheck 25/25 (no cache), contracts 554, field-app 1114 of 1115 — the one failure godview-monitor's "WEBGPU UNAVAILABLE", which failed two runs in three here again and loads no file this commit touches (AR-S4c2's A/B caught it at `4ecacb3d` too), fieldd 1044 (+15 skipped; its real-floor suites among them), `check-agent-catalog --literals`. Among them: a turn-on and an Add through the real daemon — the value in a keychain map, never in the ledger, the keep file or the wire — and a spawn on the real floor whose own process carries the key it was given and not the one it wasn't, which reaches neither its session record nor the ledger. No vendor binary ran; no add has met a real agent. The catalog captured in headless Chrome, light and dark.

**Found.** `codex mcp add --url` starts a browser sign-in as soon as a server offers OAuth, and it names no forwarded variable (`run_add`, cli/src/mcp_cmd.rs at rust-v0.150.0): Codex adds through its own config write instead. Hermes's add connects to the server and asks which of its tools to use before it saves (`cmd_mcp_add`, 0.21.4). Claude Code refuses a config naming a variable with no value and no default, hence `${N:-}`: a Claude started outside VibeField keeps its other servers. The keychain entry is written through `security(1)`, as the plugins' secrets are: the profile's values ride its argv for an instant, and any process of the user that runs `security` can read the entry — so "an agent is given only its own servers' keys" holds for what VibeField gives, not against an agent that goes looking. A contracts test run regenerates field-native's `registries.rs` and gen/layout.json from LAYOUT; the golden vector is the hand-kept half.

**Owed.** Skills kept once (the profile's skills folder, links, Codex's move into the shared folder); O1, a change made outside VibeField; Hermes's add in a pane; Antigravity with a key; headers; Paste setup…; Use this one everywhere; Remove from the profile; forgetting a value. The add forms are the reports' and were never probed: the first real adds belong on a throwaway profile. AR-D29, AR-D30, AR-D31 and AR-D32 await ratification.

## AR-S4d2 — adding once, second slice: a skill kept once for an Agent Profile and linked where each agent looks, Codex's copy in the shared folder, and a change made outside VibeField said (2026-09-27; `680b3ab932ba0b64f15d6792bcca9c8c6af5ce6c`, puppeteer `852c288` pinned)

VibeField, in a clean worktree at `680b3ab932ba0b64f15d6792bcca9c8c6af5ce6c` (puppeteer at `852c288`, rosetta at its pin, James's built field-native linked): typecheck 25/25 (no cache); contracts 556; field-app 1120/1121 — the one, the design-system page's states test, timed out at 5 s with the machine's load near 200 and passes alone (6/6); fieldd 1053 (+15 skipped) — the one, PRC-2's drain-deadline window (80–175 ms), missed under the same load and passes alone (2/2); `check-agent-catalog --literals`. Among them: skills through puppeteer's real act runner and file steps on a temp home — a skill still Claude's moved to the profile's folder, linked back and linked for Grok; Codex's move with another profile's Codex switched off; a link taken away and an agent's own folder kept; Add skill with its plan; a change made outside found and settled — and an Add skill through the real daemon, audited, its fake agents' folders in a temp dir. ## AR-S4e — pass 23's per-agent pages, first slice: a plugin an agent holds, on its own page, with its agent's own switch, update and removal (2026-09-27; `48b0b9fed4fbcfcea7bf126336055b7235d19bf0`, puppeteer `78451b9` pinned)

**James:** "Go on" (after AR-S4d's second slice was committed; the plan's S4e: plugins — browse, a plugin's page, update and remove — and each agent's own server and skill lists); "commit".

**puppeteer `78451b9` (RFC 006 C2's fifth slice).** A plugin stays with its agent, and its acts are the agent's own. `ExtensionActTarget` gains `plugin`; `ExtensionActKind` gains `update` (the agent's own update of that one plugin to the newest its marketplace has) and `purge`: `remove` is the agent's own uninstall keeping the data the plugin stored apart from its files where the agent can, and `purge` deletes that data too, offered only where the agent's uninstall does both. `plan` takes an `ExtensionActItem`; the runtime plans a held plugin's enable, disable, remove, purge and update, refuses a plugin's `add` (an install) and sign-ins itself, and an update's receipt is the version moving (`updated 1.2.0 → 1.3.0`) or not (`still holds 1.3.0`). `PluginItem` gains `author`, `homepage` (masked as an address is) and `brings` (the names of its commands and agents and the events its hooks run on); `ExtensionKindSupport` gains `label` (the agent's own word: Pi's "Packages") and `hostedSkips` (a kind a session the runtime starts does not load: OpenCode's hosted sessions run `--pure`). ## TP — WebGPU atlas safety and retained scroll rendering (2026-09-27)

James approved the follow-up to the complete terminal WebGPU flow review.

Ghosttea now keeps bounded, lazy glyph atlas pages and submits pending draws before recycling a referenced page. A pane that exceeds one page's capacity cannot cancel the other panes. Cheap submission/presentation counters run outside profiling. Ordinary routed frames decode through bounded byte views; native frame assembly borrows cached shaped rows. Exact row comparison preserves unchanged raster rows during scrolling, using one shared staging texture (64 MiB ceiling), with complete redraws for catalog/layout resets, selection, fractional-pixel scrolls, clipped viewports and native vertical overhang. Selection changes damage only their old/new rows. VibeField parks covered field mirrors while Godview is open and resumes their existing surface when uncovered. `siblings:pin NAME` permits a focused upgrade while retaining the agent-catalog gate and unrelated pins.

Evidence is retained under `draft/terminal-perf/results/20260927-webgpu-optimization/`. Both atlas collision witnesses now preserve the correct pixels and upload zero atlas bytes in their warm batches; mono and color overflow split submissions correctly, and an oversized pane leaves another pane rendering. The 120×40 DPR-2 scroll witness matches a complete redraw byte for byte: 46,760 vertex bytes versus 232,040, and CPU encoding medians 0.350 ms versus 0.915 ms in the isolated run. This is not an end-to-end FPS or GPU-time claim. The actual native VT/shaper → TRF1 → worker → WebGPU witness also matches a forced full redraw: five repaired rows and 22,040 vertex bytes versus forty rows and 174,720 bytes. Ghosttea renderer 283 tests, frame decoder 13, native core 50 and runtime 133 pass; core clippy, package builds/checks and touched-file lint pass. VibeField mirror/deck/demand tests (83), sibling tests (16), and field-app typecheck pass. `pnpm verify` stops at the pre-existing Rosetta revision/pin mismatch; it is not a green whole-tree gate.

Next: source cadence and session-local frame fan-out, native snapshot/logical-state materialization, and wire-level row movement. The scene/presentation passes remain; steady scrolling adds two texture copies. A quiet-host 1/4/16-pane latency/GPU/compositor comparison is still owed. No running app or user PTY was restarted.

**Errata (2026-09-28, TP change review):** the capacity-isolation claim above is too broad. Preflight overflow is isolated, but a later glyph insertion failure can still cancel pending neighboring panes; a real GPU reproduction submitted neither the valid pane nor the failing pane. The new decoder's Node Buffer input path also leaves glyph pixels aliasing the frame. `siblings:pin NAME` runs the catalog check against available working trees, so a passing check does not prove an unchanged pin when an unselected sibling is at a different revision. These remain open; evidence and required fixes are recorded in `draft/terminal-perf/results/20260928-webgpu-change-review/REPORT.md`. Another 100 retained-rendering comparisons matched full redraws exactly.

**Resolution (2026-09-28, TP review fixes):** these three findings are closed by the TP review-fix slice below; the review evidence remains as a record of the failures.

A `CatalogPlugin` carries the catalog's key (what an install takes), what its listing says it would bring, what the agent asks or does before its code runs (a look, a command to accept, a package manager's fetch, values by name, consent, a scan, apps that sign in), why the agent will not install it here (`blocked`), the plugin the agent holds from it by its own install record (`held`) and whether that copy is older (`newer`); a `CatalogSuggestion` is a marketplace the agent adds by itself later, addable now where a source is given. ## AR-7 — a typed agent is a managed agent: puppeteer's spawn-through kit, fieldd's gateway, and a name typed in a Godview pane that the fold owns before its first byte (2026-09-28; the code at `ar7/integration` `8d8f8ce9`, the landing the branch's fast-forward — this ledger's commit, the third wave boundary `aac22536` and its fixture fix `0022225a` on top; puppeteer `d1945095` pinned = `2a81fc1` + its main `4600241`)

**James:** "good, let's plan and work on both sides(vibefield and puppetear) and do things properly and solid, after you have a solid plan, fan out subagents to work in parallel" (2026-09-27); on the runtime inspector, "ok, this is for dev purposes in puppetear, we do not need these in vibefield"; on strict, "Let's go strict"; "One shot run is out of our scope, they should be treated as regular command run"; on tmux inside a pane, "Accept as limit right now with clear documentation"; "Claude and codex first"; on lanes running real sessions, "Yes"; "add work trees to my portable ssd instead". The plan is `draft/thinking-ar7-typed-agents.md` (its slate AR7-D1…D16, six of them his rulings); twelve lanes built it in worktrees on the SSD, each graded by its own report and by gates run again on the merged tips.

**The rule.** In a Godview pane, an interactive agent session runs managed or does not run (strict, AR7-D1, one constant `AGENT_GATEWAY_STRICT = true` in `packages/fieldd/src/agent-gateway.ts` with no switch). Everything that is not that runs exactly as typed, fieldd up or down: a version query, a one-shot run (`claude -p …`, `codex exec …`, a piped agent — a regular command, AR7-D12; VibeField keeps nothing of it), a launch whose input or output is not a terminal, a launch from a terminal VibeField does not own. The kit refuses only when all three hold — the host is strict, the invocation is an interactive session, and the process sits in a terminal the host owns — and it decides in that order, so a version query never waits on a terminal lookup. Launchers go only to agents whose adapters classify their own grammar (`nativeInvocation.classifies`: Claude and Codex at this pin, AR7-D15); the seven preview agents get none until their adapters learn theirs.

**puppeteer `2a81fc1` (53 commits over its main `0ba060f`; 87 files).** The kit, `@vibecook/puppeteer-runtime/spawn-through` (PU-17, a subpath of the runtime — no new lock row, no new wall): `protocol.ts` (requests `launch` and `exec-failed`; answers `exec`, `fallback`, `refuse`, `ack`; `SpawnThroughDeclineCode` with `launch-refused` among its codes; refusal words bounded to two printable lines and 400 characters), `gateway.ts` (`startSpawnThroughGateway({token, handle, strict})` on loopback), `prepare.ts` (`SpawnThroughHost`, `prepareSpawnThroughLaunch`: classify → terminal → prepare → adopt, and the rule of refusal), `rendezvous.ts` (`gateway.json` with the host's label and bearer, `launch-providers.json`, an 8 s default wait for a host that is starting), `terminals.ts` (the host's own list of the shells it owns, and the owning-process check by pid and start time), `materialize.ts` (a `bin/<name>` launcher per offered command, `PUPPETEER_SHIM_LABEL`), `shell-integration.ts` (zsh, the person's `ZDOTDIR` restored first), `process-watch.ts`, and `shim-main.ts` (interactive means both stdin and stdout are a terminal; an ancestry check of its own when the host cannot answer; a placed refusal obeyed wherever it runs, an unplaced one only under a listed shell). Core: `AgentNativeInvocationResolution` — `accepted`, `passthrough {kind: utility | one-shot | elsewhere}`, `rejected {argument?}` — and `AgentLaunchRefusedError` (branded, recognised across copies of Core). The runtime classifies before it prepares (`classifyInvocation`, synchronous and pure), answers `NATIVE_INVOCATION_PASSTHROUGH` for what is not a session and `AGENT_LAUNCH_REFUSED` with the adapter's own sentence and `error.refusal.code` for what it refuses. The adapters: table-driven invocation grammars for Claude (against a captured `claude --help`, 2.1.283) and Codex (0.157.1, `codex resume --help` too), each with a census test that turns a vendor release into a red list of exactly the new flags. Claude carries most of its flags into a managed session and refuses what a managed session cannot carry — `--session-id`, `--settings`, `--bare`, `--safe-mode`, `--fork-session`, `--teleport`, `-w/--worktree`, `--tmux` alone — plus the `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE`/`CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE` environment switches and a settings layer whose `disableAllHooks` would blind the observation a managed session is made of; a typed launch no longer forces `--permission-mode default`, so the person's own `defaultMode` holds. Codex carries `-c` for most keys, `--enable/--disable`, `--search`, `-i`, `-m`, `-s`, `-a`, the bypass flag, `--no-alt-screen` and the prompt, and a typed Codex starts its thread from the person's `config.toml`. The reference app (Godview) consumes the kit under its own label, runs the shim on a real Node first (`process.execve` exists from 22.15 and 23.11, not 23.0–23.10), sweeps stale launcher homes and refreshes its own six-hourly (macOS empties an untouched temp home after about three days). The two guides carry the seam: `docs/guides/spawn-through-hosts.md` (what a host answers, the rule of refusal, the codes, `providerCode`) and `adapting-an-agent.md` §9.3 (`AgentLaunchRefusedError`). **Held back on its lane:** `7cb15dd` on `feat/launch-refusal-reason` — a host's OWN spawn of Claude refused under `disableAllHooks`, a `feat(adapter-claude)!:` subject Release Please would cut as 0.2.0 — James's call.

**VibeField (51 commits over main `c0753a25`; 56 files).** contracts: `LAYOUT.AGENT_SHIMS_DIR` (`agents/shims`, the 0700 home where the launchers, the bundled shim, the rendezvous and the shell integration live — the bearer is in a 0600 file there, never in a shell's environment); Only `pnpm dev` offers launchers until AR-7j gives the packaged daemon a runtime; the leak detector (AR-7f) is not built. The phone reads neither `spawnedBy` nor `resumable`: a typed run held across a fieldd restart shows there as an unknown row, and its resume is refused with a sentence the phone may not show. ## TP — WebGPU review fixes: reserved atlas positions, owned pixels and honest pins (2026-09-28)

James asked to fix the three review findings properly and commit them. Ghosttea `a8fffb505916fbb1a5e679b3c5c1c0fbbfb8a9fe` reserves preflight's exact atlas positions before geometry can skip or reorder glyphs; uploads remain lazy, and later-visible glyphs use their existing reservation. Bounded frame inputs normalize to plain Uint8Array views without copying the frame, while retained glyph payloads copy explicitly, including direct Buffer sections. VibeField records that Ghosttea revision. Its named-pin CLI now checks every resulting checkout revision before the Rosetta build and R23 gate, rejecting missing or mismatched siblings while preserving unselected pins; dirty trees at the pinned revision still warn.

Regression tests first failed on the prior code, then passed: frame 16, React/renderer 286, sibling tooling 23 (325 total). Frame/React typechecks and builds, touched-file ESLint/Prettier/Biome and diff checks pass. The isolated Electron WebGPU witness now submits both panes in the near-full atlas reproduction, with exact full-redraw pixels. Warm paints upload zero atlas bytes; revealing a reserved glyph uploads it once; genuine overflow preserves the old scene and presents the neighbor. Another 100 composed-scroll paints match complete redraws, without GPU validation errors. The native Buffer witness retains only 240 pixel bytes and survives mutation of the 116,981-byte input frame.

`pnpm verify` remains blocked by the unrelated Rosetta HEAD/pin mismatch. The corrected `siblings:pin ghosttea` records the selected pin and now exits 1 before building/checking the mismatched checkout; this is an honest refusal, not a green R23 gate. Evidence and remaining application-wide performance qualification are in `draft/terminal-perf/results/20260928-webgpu-review-fixes/REPORT.md`. No running application or user PTY was restarted; unrelated working-tree changes and staged files are preserved.

## TP — startup benchmarks: measure shell readiness and native preparation separately (2026-09-28)

James asked for repeatable benchmarks, measurements and further optimization. The Electron perf lab now has a macOS `startup` scenario that sends the real window-local Command–D chord, records pane visibility and routed input permission, then requires one pasted shell command to write an unpredictable acknowledgment. Ready-pane command controls bracket every split; a lost command fails, with no retry. The filesystem observer is armed once outside the timed loops. Echo/flood fixture setup uses the shipping paste/key handlers, and echo starts only after its raw-input readiness record. Labs use an isolated shell/agent profile, fingerprint the built inputs, preserve raw failures and refuse nonempty result directories. Puppeteer `1d02fa5e795af82d8f776a68feead4276360667f` owns the production change and exports it through the existing adapter/runtime composition. Optional model names no longer gate native readiness: late replies enrich current identities without replaying usage and are fenced after closure/disposal. Fresh owned threads skip empty history/context reads; resumed and external threads retain their replay barrier. Socket existence on a native startup wakeup can resolve readiness; quiet servers retain the 50 ms fallback. A tested faster polling variant was discarded because its saving was below measured control variation. VibeField records the new Puppeteer pin via `siblings.mjs`; no vendor-specific production branch or new wire door was added.

Native empty materialization still produced multi-second stalls. Six synthetic delayed-catalog runs reached readiness before the optional reply; the required materialization was retained after native probes rejected resume without it. Failed instrument pilots and the rejected polling experiment remain beside the final results in `draft/terminal-perf/results/20260928-startup-benchmark/REPORT.md`; the checked-in operating guide is `tooling/terminal-perf/README.md`.

Validation: 235 Puppeteer adapter tests pass (6 opt-in live tests skipped), with 38 focused tests rerun after the final buffer-lifetime fix; 92 terminal-perf tests, 9 isolated-profile fixture tests and 3 prewarm integration tests pass. ## QL — the empty pane launcher: resume, or launch (2026-09-28)

A fresh shell pane in Godview (VibeField's overlay and Puppeteer's reference app) now shows the L1 · Ledger launcher from the Minimal Pane Frame's pass 3 (§17–§25). A ruled field, *Resume a session…*, sits over the agent catalog's rows as a two-column legend with ⌥1…⌥0, ordered by last launch. ⌥n launches that agent into this pane, in this pane's folder, under its default profile; the shell it replaces is closed by the unused-shell reaper. ⌥↵ or a click opens the field. It lists this folder's latest sessions at once and fuzzy-searches titles, folders and agents, plus transcript words, as you type. ⇥ switches HERE/ALL, and ↵ resumes the highlighted session in this pane under the persona the index files it under. Plain typing dismisses the launcher and reaches the shell; ⎋ closes the field, and a second ⎋ dismisses it. While the launcher is up in the focused pane it owns ⌥0–⌥9, and the profile strip keeps them everywhere else. Refusals are plain sentences in the owning side's words.

Puppeteer `a783d4d` (`feat/pane-launcher`, 27 commits over `7310f2f`, pinned) owns the component: `@vibecook/puppeteer-views/launcher` (port, model, chrome, `PaneLauncher`, `DeckLaunchers`, `cantLaunchLine`) and `styles/pane-launcher.css`, with the deck's pane-element discovery shared with `DeckFrames`. It also brings `historyKinds` on launch providers, so a host joins rosetta's rows to the agent that resumes them with no table, plus the reference app's host: IPC `launcher:agents|recent|words`, `puppeteer:resume-native-session`, and the protocol range widened to rosetta 23, which also mends the Find sheet. VibeField adds `index.recent`, `agent.resume` by native id (flag-shaped ids refused, the index must file the conversation under that agent and persona, one run per conversation), `agent.providers` `lastLaunchedAt`, the field-app host (`godview/deck-launchers.tsx`, `launcher-doors.ts`, `monitor/launcher-keys.ts`), and a catalog specimen of every state on both grounds. Docs: `docs/agent-plane/api.html` (46 doors).

Found and fixed along the way:
- Two adversarial reviews, 7 + 8 findings. Among them: a click on a resting pane's launcher didn't activate the pane (React portals bubble along the React tree); native resume ids reached adapters' argv; stale transcript hits; a module-level birth record surviving a pool retry and leaking a PTY; ⌥ digits dead when focus was elsewhere; APFS case (`realpathSync` keeps the typed case, `.native` doesn't); rosetta files every non-repo folder under its own project, so home's project swallowed every folder under ~.
- Two more defects a live drive found: OSC 7 `file://` cwds, and a ~100 ms `foreground-job` blip at shell startup.
- The launcher swallowing the Escape meant to close the find sheet.

Validation:
- Puppeteer: views 307, godview 275 and `pnpm -r test` pass, and `godview:launcher-drive-smoke` drives a–g through CDP (open, filter, scope, close, dismiss, launch with the reaper witnessed, first key reaching the shell, a click on a resting pane, OSC 7). Root `pnpm test` is red only at the adapter-codex ground-truth map, the same red as bare `7310f2f`.
- VibeField: `pnpm verify` red only at fieldd's terminal-kill-matrix row S3-A (2/2 green alone; QL touches no terminal or native code), `test:rust` and `gen:check` green; `pnpm smoke:godview` shows, opens and dismisses the launcher live.

## QL-2 — the launch: from the click to the agent's first frame (2026-09-29)

A click on an agent in an empty Godview pane (or ⌥n, or ↵ on a past session) now answers in its own frame. The launcher shrinks away toward the clicked mark, and that mark hops to the middle of the pane on the pop spring. The pane's own cell grid appears as dots under the terminal's ground, one per terminal cell, woken in a patch around the mark; a band of the pane colour ripples out through the cells while the agent starts, and the grid reaches the corners once the agent's process is running in the pane. On the agent's first frame a last ripple opens the ground from the mark and the mark flies into the pane's badge, which held its own mark back meanwhile. A caption under the mark says the agent, `starting` or `opening` (`resuming` for a resume), and from 1.5 s the seconds. A launch drawn inside 320 ms shows no indicator; a first frame that has not come 3 s after the agent runs releases the pane anyway. A refusal drains the grid, hops the mark back to its row, and the launcher returns with fieldd's reason; an agent that exits before its first frame (its pane given a fresh shell again) lets the pane go at once, and the launcher there says it exited before it opened. This is look C · Cells from the Minimal Pane Frame's pass 4 (§26–§33), which James picked on 09-29.

Ghosttea `8a0930e` (`feat/session-drawn`, two commits over `84b98b8`, pinned) publishes a session's first drawn frame: the render worker posts `session-drawn` once per handle on the first committed frame with a glyph or non-blank text, and the runtime answers `sessionHasDrawn(id)`, dispatches `session-drawn`, and forgets the flag when the session is unregistered. It also exports the fixed cell metrics. Puppeteer `973b5b7` (`feat/pane-launch`, six commits over `e4f5379`, pinned) owns the launch: `launch-model.ts` (the reducer over the three facts and the `left` one, the timings, the caption, `watchDrawnSessions`), `PaneLaunchChrome` and the `PaneLaunch` portal (its geometry follows the pane's size), `DeckLaunchers` holding the launch per pane with the port call and its answer and the refusal lines per pane, the launcher leaving toward the mark, and `deck-frame.css` holding the badge's mark under `data-vf-launching`. Its reference app names the born session and watches its first frame, and its drive smoke witnesses the launch. VibeField's `place` names the born session, the deck hands the launcher `watchDrawnSessions(runtime)` and carries ghosttea's cell metrics as CSS variables, and the catalog shows the launch's starting and opening faces through the shipping chrome. DESIGN.md §8 records the recipe, §6 the two loops (the breath and the ripple), §2.7 the ground's floor.

Found along the way:
- Why a click looked dead: VibeField's port answers only after `agent.spawn` and the mount, and the launcher unmounts at that swap, so its own leave could never play and nothing covered the blank terminal. The launch is held per pane, not per launcher, for that reason.
- `godview-deck.test.tsx`'s runtime mock lacked `sessionHasInput` and `remoteSession`, red on main since fb8e77a9; fixed in its own commit.
- An independent review (no HIGH; 2 MEDIUM, 9 LOW; all taken). With main's clean-exit return (d344b4a7), an agent that exits before its first frame left the launch covering the new shell's launcher for 3 s (keys went to the shell, a second ⌥n was swallowed); that is now QL-D17. Refusal lines keyed by session showed in a mirrored pane; the geometry was frozen at mount (a split left the mark off-centre); reduced motion snapped the reveal open; `.vf-pane-mark { width: 1em }` widened letter marks; the live region was filled as it mounted; DESIGN.md had the launcher's fade on island and the dots at 1px; ghosttea's runtime kept the drawn flag after unregistering a session.
- The Electron smoke window is occlusion-backgrounded like any window: covered by another, it gets no rAF and frame-waiting rows (the zoom row) flake. It passes with `--disable-renderer-backgrounding --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows` on electron's command line.

Validation (both lanes were rebased at landing over main's one new commit each, VibeField `0c15cb5e` and puppeteer `e4f5379`; `range-diff` shows every patch identical, the lock aside):
- Ghosttea: ghosttea-react 297 tests pass and `npm run check` is clean; both new tests were red-proved.
- Puppeteer: typecheck (every package and app) is clean on the rebased branch, with views 358 and godview 273 passing; `packages:check`, `support:check` and prettier were clean and `pnpm -r test` was green before the rebase. Root `pnpm test` is red only at the adapter-codex ground-truth map ("stale") and its script test; this branch leaves `scripts/` and every `packages/adapter-*` byte-identical to its base, and QL-1 recorded the same red on its own base. The reference app's drive smoke passed on the same six commits before the rebase with a real Codex launch from ⌥1: the launch was in the pane by the first read after the key (35 ms), the indicator came at 377 ms and the caption counted the seconds, Codex answered at 11.2 s, and it went home on its first frame 210 ms later. It landed at 12.0 s with the badge wearing Codex's mark, and its captures show the grid's patch, the ripple and the caption mid-wait.
- VibeField, on the landed tree: `pnpm verify` passed preflight, deps, iOS fixtures, icons, typecheck (25 projects), biome, `cargo fmt`, clippy and `bundle:assert`. `pnpm test` lost one timing row (field-app's design-system catalog states), which passed alone; `test:rust` passed 268 (9 ignored) and `gen:check` showed no drift. The launch rig passes 14 cases, and eleven mutations of its guards each turn it red. `smoke:godview` (run with the two switches above) passed whole three times. The first read came in the click's own frame, home followed at 172–215 ms and the pane was let go at 634–665 ms, with no indicator because the stub draws inside 320 ms; the pane never passed through `refused` or `left`. Other runs of the same tree: three in one early cluster lost the zoom round trip (the second ⌘⇧↵ never toggled), while main's own code passed three control runs alongside; that row then passed twelve runs in a row, four of them unprobed. ## SB-0…SB-3 — the spawn bloom: hold, reach, let go (2026-09-30)

A long press on the swarm's empty ground (520 ms) now keeps the hold ring as a hub and blooms this desktop's Agent Profiles around it — This Mac, Work, Demo — as buds on an arc that opens up and turns only as far as an edge or the chrome forces it. The field goes quiet under a veil of the monitor's own ground, the sessions under what the pointer aims at stay lit above it, solid clearings keep the bloom readable over any crowd, and the words — huge, in the field's widest empty space — say what letting go does: *Open as Work*, *New terminal*, *Cancel*. Letting go on a profile opens a terminal under it, born where the pointer let go (the bud grows into the body); on the hub, under the default profile; on open ground or ⎋, nothing. A desktop with one profile does not bloom: the hold creates at once, as before, under that profile. The body names its profile (glyph and name, where the desktop has more than one); its pane's empty launcher reads `New · Under Work`, an agent with no sign-in there reads `no sign-in`, and a launch from it runs under Work. Typed in a Work pane that holds no Claude sign-in, `claude` is refused in the pane, before anything runs: "claude was not started: Work has no Claude Code sign-in (Settings → Agents). Change that, then run claude again." A secondary click on empty ground opens the bloom held open; the swarm's hidden list's `＋ New terminal…` opens it for keys; the list view's `＋ TERMINAL` is the same tree as a two-step menu. Other desktops wait on the sync plane (SB-6).

Puppeteer `a4b5290` (`feat/spawn-bloom`, 36 commits and two merges over `973b5b7`, pinned) carries the view side: the seams (`MonitorSpawnMenu`, `createAt(position, target)`, `spawnMenu?` — absent, the hold is today's); the bloom's pure core under `views/swarm/bloom/` — the audited prototype's table and geometry ported one to one (`layoutArc` with its strict turn order and lookahead, `seatLabel`, direction targeting, the words and their placement) and a pure machine for hold, held open and keys; the DOM overlay (buds, seated labels, tether, words, the live region); AgentSwarm's hold → bloom → release; the field under it on the GPU (the grid under the veil, an erase pass for the clearings, the hub drawn last, the pending body that turns its OPENING dashes after 320 ms); the terminal's profile line with the profile glyphs in the swarm's atlas; the launcher's caption; the list's two-step menu. VibeField (`sb/integration`, 28 commits and two merges over `d2488185`) carries the rest. Contracts: `terminal.create {profileSet}`, and the create's answer and the roster say it. fieldd binds a set through puppeteer's `profileBindingEnvironment` and the AR-7d fence (opaque — AR-L1; what the fence drops is counted, never named; a bound birth needs `agent.spawn`), keeps session → set on disk (0600, pruned with the sessions, read back after a restart), audits the set and `bound`, and refuses a typed agent the pane's set cannot run (SB-D7) with `AGENT_LAUNCH_REFUSED` before anything is prepared. field-app offers this desktop's profiles as the spawn menu, births under the chosen one through the deck (⌘D splits, the agent-exit shell and relaunches inherit their pane's set; a relaunch whose set was deleted drops, never an unbound shell in its place), tags the rows so a Work tab keeps a Work shell, and shows the launcher of a bound pane; the catalog mounts the shipping monitor over a fixture door.

Found along the way:
- Two host defects the binding made real, fixed: a refused `terminal.create` faulted the whole deck (the pool called it a transport fault), and ghosttea swallowed the override's throw, so the door said "the workspace could not open a terminal" instead of fieldd's words.
- The spawn hint raced the row: a row that arrived before its hint spawned elsewhere while its birth waited out 4 s. The hint now lands with the row's first appearance, a create that opens nothing rejects, and the views catch every create.
- A `Ref<>` prop typed against puppeteer's `@types/react` failed VibeField's typecheck (two copies); the prop is typed structurally. Comments and fixtures naming agents tripped puppeteer's `packages:check` and wall R23b.
- The record's drift, corrected at its sources: AR-D28 (the bar no longer starts sessions), ProfileTabs' comment, GodviewDeck's `listHosts` comment (the routed runtime throws; it does not answer zero hosts), methods.ts's three "reached by routing" comments, and QL-D3 (revised again: a pane born under a profile launches under it).
- An independent review (no HIGH): taken in the slice — a birth let go near an edge was drawn at the raw point while the physics stands its row in from the edge, so it jumped at the takeover (now drawn where the row will stand, still matched on the raw point); the list's menu put the default first while the bloom and the tabs keep the feed's order (now the feed's, the keys landing on the default); a create that never settles left its birth forever (given up after 30 s); DESIGN.md's retract curve (`cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)`, not `ease-in`), the labels' weights and the record's dead dim numbers. Recorded, not built: a one-profile desktop's hold now births bound to that profile (kept — one pane, one answer); the phone's bound birth meets an in-handler scope read a tailnet principal cannot pass (before SB-5); `layoutArc`'s lookahead grows with the desktops — a reach with eight took 60–71 ms at worst, one desktop 1.5 ms (before SB-6). The rest are in the record's §12 review delta.
- Changing the list's order reddened field-app's catalog test, which reaches the menu by `data-bloom-bud-id`, not by any exported name; it now asserts the feed's order and that the keys land on the default, red-proved against the live effect.
- My first three `pnpm verify` runs pointed cargo at another lane's target directory while this checkout's `target` links to its own, so their fieldd suites ran a floor binary built from the base (before the lane's one Rust change, a registry constant the floor never reads at runtime). The fieldd suite was re-run whole against the tip's own binary (below).
- One run of the WebGPU witness saw every body in the swarm jam toward the top-left corner after the release and drift back within 2.5 s. Nine more runs (six on this build, three on a build from before the review's fixes) did not, and the swarm's container kept its size throughout; cause unknown. The slice's changes never feed the physics (they place the pending body's drawing and nothing else), so it is recorded here, not fixed.

Validation (neither main moved while the lanes were built; both land as fast-forwards):
