## DS-0 — the desktop sync plane is ratified (2026-09-30)

**DS-0 DESIGN RATIFIED (2026-09-30 — documentation event; no runtime landing claimed).** James ruled all eighteen marks of `draft/thinking-desktop-sync-plane.md` on its page (The Desktop Sync Plane; the picks read back from the page's `decisions` store — D1–D8 on 09-29, D9–D18 on 09-30), every one as leaned. The plane's law: **intent replicates, facts federate, bytes go direct** — a CRDT only where several writers edit one object (canvases, the settings document, a new LIBRARY of canvases), rows with a durable cursor for what a desktop observes about itself (catalogs kept when the owner sleeps; the board streamed per device and multiplexed, never re-folded, by the daemon a window or phone is connected to), and a ticket to the owner for bytes. The one pipe missing under all of it is EGRESS: no desktop process can reach the tailnet through VibeField's own node today — PeerLink dials with Node's WebSocket over the OS network, artifact opens likewise, remote terminals in the desktop deck are dark — so federation has only ever run beside the system Tailscale app. Ruled: egress in the sidecar as truffle RFC 026 (E1 the node's SOCKS5 for fieldd, E2 loopback routes for the renderer's cell legs, E3 an authenticated HTTP proxy for pages; petition T7 drafted). Also ruled: the daemon-to-daemon path is the peer's door over E1 with a transport-derived principal; a forwarded call carries `onBehalfOf`; fieldd becomes a Loro-level host synced by version (C6-1 revisited — an opaque daemon cannot merge a checkpoint, and the July probe did not see that); the library is its own system document; every synced canvas replicates eagerly to every awake desktop; history is a replicated catalog with transcripts by ticket and search by asking, grouped by repository FAMILY with device badges (the UI is the PJ track's); the phone HOMES to one desktop with failover (which settles SP-D2, SP-D3 and SP-D10 on the companion page); `field.agents.v1` retires once the mesh board lands; a desktop unseen thirty days folds into an archive.

**One note corrected three sources.** On DS-D5 James wrote: *"i thought this is settled long time ago, which is the latest focused pane takes full control include resizing, LWW. no matter it is local pane, remote desktop pane or mobile pane"* No corpus sentence carried that rule; TPv3 v0.5 had written "focus ⇏ geometry" as if it were policy and TM-D3 had minted the phone `[input, read]`. Reconciled at each source the same day: the lease stays explicit (the cell never mints geometry on focus; a mirror never claims), and the HOST takes the seat for the pane the person last focused, on any device, by one `transfer_geometry` to itself — a *take*, one CAS, one committed resize; every self principal is minted `[geometry, input, read]`, the phone included (DS-4 the rights and the take; DS-4b the kit's lease verbs). tmux's `window-size latest` is the precedent.

**What moved (the record's §13, executed):** design-04 §2/§3.2/§6/§7 · design-02 §2.4/§3.3 · design-00 §4.1/§4.4/§5 · artifact-hub §0 · users-and-accounts §8 · thinking-c6 C6-1 · thinking-terminal-mesh-cells TM-D3/D6, TM-5, TM-6 · terminal-pipeline-v3 TP-D2 · **`draft/design-06-sync-planes.md` v0.1 seeded** (both planes' law; SP's five open marks flagged) · petitions T7 and RO-10 drafted, M2/M3 re-dated · DECISIONS rows SP-D1…D13 and DS-D1…D18, the D30–D38, GM-D and TM-D rows amended · ROADMAP's C row and a Next-up bullet. Nothing built; `pnpm commit-draft` is James's. Next: DS-1 (egress — the RFC on a petition window, `native.mesh.egress.*`, PeerLink over E1; its witness is two desktops federating `device.list {device}` with the Tailscale app QUIT), DS-2 in parallel; the ICE1 envelope spike before DS-5. Still owed from the companion page's 09-29 rulings: the mini-app bridge and the upload plane, as designs.

## DS wave 1 — the desktop sync plane, built across five repositories (2026-10-01)

**LANDED on main at `d71883fe` (55 commits over `d1232ccb`; fast-forward; `pnpm verify` verbatim EXIT 0 on that tip — its second run, at load 37; the first, at a load average of 166, was red on one pre-existing load-lottery row, `godview-monitor.test.tsx`'s 3 s WebGPU wait, green alone and on the previous tip).** The day after James ratified DS-D1…D18 he said *"go ahead, work on all sides (vibefield, rosetta, puppetear, ghosttea, truffle) to push things forward, plan, split works, fan out opus5.5 subagents to help and work on parallel works."* Ten Opus builders ran in parallel, each in its own worktree on the SSD (`/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/ds/`), from one shared base commit; the lead resolved the unions, witnessed every lane's gate in its own worktree, and landed the six VibeField lanes in order (facts → egress → board → terminal → history → intent). Then, on James's *"now do a review"*, eight Opus reviewers read the landing branch and the two security-critical sibling branches read-only; the review (`draft/work/ds-wave1-review-2026-10-01.md`) held the landing on one blocker and named seven cross-lane seams, and on *"go ahead, fix properly"* a fix-up wave (the lead's errata commit, two builders) closed them on the landing branch before main moved. Plan of record: `draft/work/ds-wave1-2026-09-30.md` (lanes, ownership, the shared shapes, every mid-wave ruling with its time, the review and the fix-up). The four sibling branches are James's to merge and release; the pin moves follow.

**The base (`9f25c86f`, DS-0).** `contracts/rows.ts` — DS-L3 as zod: `RowsCursor {epoch, revision}`, the OPEN answer (resumed | snapshot, paged with `more`), deltas `{epoch, since, revision, upserts, removed}`, `MeshScope`, `RowsDeviceState`, the mesh-scoped open and frames (one device's chain at a time), `RowsDigest`. `contracts/forwarding.ts` — `OnBehalfOf`, `IdempotencyKey`, `ForwardReceipt` (`applied | refused | outcome-unknown`), the envelope (namespaced under `forward` by DS-2 the same day). `ROWS`/`FORWARDING` in registries.

**DS-2 — the facts ground (ds/b, 6 commits).** A forwarded call says who it is for: the routing hop (product-api's `DeviceForwarder`, not service-registry.ts) builds `onBehalfOf` from the calling context, the owner reads a peer's envelope tolerantly, the audit actor names the node and the window; a non-peer carrying the envelope is refused. Receipts: a keyed forwarded mutation applies once and answers retries from the journal; one lost in flight is `outcome-unknown` on the caller and read back by the retry; `forward.receipt` reads it. The roster tells `awake | restarting | asleep | incompatible` apart (`DeviceInfo.state`, `PeerLink.doorState`). Agent and index doors leave `local` (acts federate, the fold streams, reads federate). The gate found and fixed its own regression: PeerLink's sweeper dropped links with a request in flight (false outcome-unknowns), and a remote's own UNAVAILABLE was rewritten "unreachable" and dropped the link — `isRemoteAnswer` now passes every coded remote reply through. **Owed:** the client half of DS-D15 — no window or phone sends `forward.idempotencyKey` or reads `forward.receipt` yet (SP-L5).

**DS-1 — the egress facade, the VibeField half (ds/a, 9 commits).** Six mgmt verbs `native.mesh.egress.*` (proxy, httpProxy, route.add/remove/list, route.subscribe) with goldens both sides parse; the floor serves them through `EgressBackend` — `UnsupportedEgress` in production (UNAVAILABLE `egress-unsupported`), `FakeEgress` for tests (real loopback splices), `TruffleEgress` behind cargo feature `truffle-egress`, OFF and uncompiled until truffle's RFC 026 is consumed (truffle-core + npm sidecars together, protocol 5 → 6); the route table carries a revision scoped to the floor's boot; only port 9422 is routable (DS-L6). fieldd: `egress.ts` (`EgressRoutes` port: `ensureRoute/release/onDropped`, peer-left → route.remove sent), `socks5.ts` (RFC 1928/1929, no new dependency), PeerLink dials through the node's SOCKS5 when the floor offers one and falls back to today's OS-network dial, logged once per link. **Owed (DS-1b, with the RFC 026 consumption):** fail-closed per floor boot, not per dial (today any answer but a proxy grant dials the OS network — unchanged behaviour while every answer is `egress-unsupported`); the egress ask cached per boot (every dial now queues on the floor's mesh FIFO); the uncompiled arm re-typed against truffle's `NodeError`.

**DS-3 — the mesh board (ds/c, 4 commits).** `agent.subscribe {scope: "mesh"}`: one hub per projection, this desktop's board plus one federated upstream per awake `docHost` desktop, frames relayed verbatim (never re-folded), states live / stale (3 missed heartbeats) / asleep / incompatible, a gap resets, each desktop's last board kept past its readers (DS-L8). The `desk` projection (280-char reply, the blocker's question, cost) for one person's own desktops; `full` and `mesh` refused to a peer, `desk` to a phone. Godview reads the door: the two-second remote poll and `listHosts` deleted, every row says where it lives, a device dropdown before the profile tabs narrows swarm and list, catalog specimens mount the shipping chip. *The lane reported fixing two `federated-subs.ts` defects (first-tick frames lost; stale params on re-subscribe); the fix was not in its commits — the file diffed as binary and hid it — and landed in the fix-up instead (below).*

**DS-4 — a terminal on another desktop (ds/e, 6 commits).** The take in the cell: `transfer_geometry` to the CALLER on its own geometry right, the live holder and the revision still checked — one CAS on the lease, one committed resize, witnessed on a real PTY. Every self principal is minted `[geometry, input, read]` (DS-D5's note; the phone and a forwarding peer daemon included). `terminal.openTicket/renewAttach/terminate` federate: the owner hands a self peer daemon its cell's tailnet doors, the caller's `forwardVia` refuses to launder a mint and adopts the ticket's doors through the `RemoteCellRewriter` port (default: honest `egress_unavailable`; the egress routes plug in late). The deck passes `takeGeometryOnFocus` to the workspace — inert until the ghosttea pin moves. `terminal.takeGeometry` declared, `not_implemented` until DS-4b. **Owed:** the take is a CAS on the lease and not on the engine (two concurrent takes leave the engine's controller with the loser until the runtime's retry; `door.rs` `handle_geometry`); finalize never re-checks the destination activation; DS-4c window-keyed attach ledgers.

**DS-6 — history across desktops, the daemon side (ds/f, 7 commits).** `project-family.ts` (`normalize(git_repo)`; ssh and https spellings agree; no remote → no family). `catalog-rows.ts` (a source table with a journal, a subscriber pump, a reader's copy; paged snapshots with `page`/`pages`). The follower of rosetta's `/ws/meta` (snapshot diffed, mutations upserted, roots only, a fresh snapshot every 10 min because removals are silent). `index.catalog.subscribe` (peer daemons only), the replica of every self desktop persisted at most once a minute (`mesh/catalog/<device>.<table>.json`, temp + durable rename), `index.projects/sessions {scope: "mesh"}` paging the merged replica by keyset, `index.search {scope: "mesh"}` by asking with `sources`, `index.changes.subscribe`; one row per `{kind, native session id}` with several devices. `PEER_FIELDD_SCOPES` = the tailnet preset + `index.search`, minted only for a peer daemon (the phone's preset untouched, SP-D13 open). Two real daemons witness B keeping A's history while A sleeps, and saying so. *Its last commit (`030463f1`) made the peer doors avoid UNAVAILABLE on a premise DS-2 had already removed; the fix-up restored the honest kind and fixed the real hazard in fieldd-client (below).* **Owed:** an interrupted forced reset freezes a replica; a reader-dropped row makes the digest disagree forever; `heardAt` not written at dispose; stale temp files unswept; the follower must send RO-1's bearer at the pin move.

**DS-5 — the intent plane (ds/d, 7 commits).** The ICE1 spike PASSED: a checkpoint is a fixed frame (`"ICE1"`, a version byte, a u32 header length, a JSON header, a full Loro snapshot) and fieldd lifts the bytes without ICE; a fresh `LoroDoc` imports them plus the journal records and converges with a second holder in one version-vector round; a checkpoint's folded edits are never emitted as updates (DS-D18 (a) holds). Built: fieldd is a Loro-level host — a liftable checkpoint puts its canvas in Loro custody, a peer's checkpoint MERGES instead of `would-clobber`, lanes open VERSION then HAVE (older peers keep working), oversized records cross as CHUNKs; the library system document (keyed by the linked login; `doc.delete`, `doc.list` gains `elsewhere`) rides the host; eager replication to every awake desktop, phones out of the doc peer set; an open window is pushed what a peer merged, exported from the version fieldd can prove it holds, behind a capability the client declares; the holders slice on `field.docs.v1`. **The settings document does NOT ride the host yet** — the review's blocker: design-06 §4 makes PA-32's revocation bias the merge rule the day settings cross, and the install reconciler still defers it, so the fix-up held settings off (DS-5b: per-capability revocation generations a grant must name; then settings cross). **Owed:** the HELLO/GET proof race; a lost eager-replication answer is never resent; the host never evicts an idle document; system-doc persistence neither fsync'd nor serialized against merge persists; chunk reassembly slots per peer shared across docs; the inbound doc lane does not yet refuse a phone by kind (outbound does).

**The landing (the lead's):** `187d7699` the forwarded-ticket test expects the forwarder's fifth argument; `3441c914` `DeviceForwarder.envelope` optional at the type and the index census test reads the reconciled rows. **Landing ruling:** `index.discoveries`, `index.status`, `index.recent` stay `local` — DS-6's doors are the index rows that leave the device (DS-2 had moved every index read). **The fix-up (after the review, before main moved):** `7ad4d96f` the review's errata at ten sources and `federated-subs.ts` as text again; fx1 (`ds/fx1`, seven): `e453e432` the settings document stays off the Loro host — PA-32's revocation bias is not the merge rule yet (B1) · `9d5198cc` a forwarded birth is a mint, and a born run answers as born (S1) · `41443164` a routed board ask is judged for its caller — a phone reads no desk through its home (S2) · `feeeb4a1` a retryable refusal leaves no receipt (S5) · `aec3cb40` one roster truth — the published major, the roster's state on the board, a woken node's silence forgotten, this desktop named per answer (S6) · `2d732b57` a peer daemon acting for no one is minted [read] (D2) · `8ef55f4a` honest states name their service, and the field projection's cadence is a floor; fx2 (`ds/fx2`, four): `eca9a8a4` a refused replay ends one subscription, never the link (S3; fieldd-client isolates hello-time replays, a params supplier, PeerLink drops one member) · `0714ba45` the federated manager hands a reader what followed its snapshot, and re-subscribes from where its readers are — the 23:47 ruling, executed · `bcc51476` Godview's mesh reader heals itself — a failure that may heal asks again on a backoff (S4) · `fd5b764a` the device chip lets the keys go when it leaves with its menu open; the lead's `d71883fe` the history mesh reads the roster's incompatible (DS-L9) and two comments follow the fix-up.

**The sibling branches (built, witnessed by the lead, reviewed, NOT merged — James's):** truffle `rfc026-egress` (E1 `tsnet:loopback`, E2 `egress:add/remove/list` raw TCP splices admitted by netmap membership, E3 a CONNECT-only Basic-auth proxy; `Node::loopback/egress_*`, NAPI, `docs/rfcs/026-egress.md`; sidecar protocol 6; 62 Go tests on two real tsnet nodes, truffle-core 364; review: a route is pinned to its target name not the admitted node; the idle reap is per direction; the RFC's threat model omits browser pages on loopback) · rosetta `feat/direct-plane-grants` (RO-1 `--token-file` a bearer on EVERY route — an Origin is never a credential — `--allow-origin`; RO-10 `--grant-key-file` + `Authorization: Rosetta-Grant <b64url(JCS)>.<b64url(HMAC)>` exact `sid`, `exp`, scope; the WebSocket subprotocol carrier; `clients/ts` `mintGrant`; 222 Rust tests; PROTOCOL_VERSION unchanged — main is already 24; review: the `/work` template admits a grant to another session's rows (latent); no `exp` upper bound; sockets outlive `exp`) · puppeteer `feat/device-dimension` (`MonitorDeviceFacet`, line OS marks in the body's ink, `DeviceFilter` + `DeviceFilterChip`; 576 views tests) · ghosttea `feat/geometry-take` (`takeResizeControl`, holder tracking from commits and refusals, `geometry-holder-changed`, `takeGeometryOnFocus`; a refusal is the announcement; 326 tests; G23 item 6 was already closed in 0.11.0).

**Found, no record carried (file:line in the plan and the review):** no desktop process could reach the tailnet through our node (PeerLink rode the OS network); design-02 §2.4's facade `reset` notification was never built; `peer-link.ts:126` dropped a whole link on a remote's UNAVAILABLE (fixed in DS-2); `device-service.ts:517-541` a peer row from a slice without an endpoint; `doclane.ts:387` hands every non-presence frame to the reply waiter; ICE's autosave re-journals applied remote updates; strata quarantines a store on any pending import; a window opening an adopted canvas before content creates its own root (renderer should wait); rosetta's `/ws/meta` has no removal event and REST caps at 1,000 roots (RO-11 drafted); the SSD rosettad spoke protocol 24 against the pin's 23 (a protocol-23 build for lanes at `rust/ds-rosettad-pin`); `terminal-grants.ts:142` one clientId per peer daemon (DS-4c owed); TPv3 "focus ⇏ geometry" and TM-D3's `[input, read]` corrected at their sources on DS-D5's note; the system volume hit 99 % mid-gate (cleared); `federated-subs.ts` carried two raw NUL bytes that made every diff to it binary; the `peer-fieldd` principal still rides the hello's self-declared kind, which now carries real grants (D1 — transport-derived identity once E1 lands; until then gate the preset on the roster's `docHost`).

**Not built:** any two-machine witness over a real tailnet (needs the truffle release consumed); E3 and in-app artifacts (DS-9); transcripts by ticket (DS-7: fieldd minting rosetta grants); the phone's re-home (DS-8); DS-4b (the kit's lease verbs), DS-4c (window-keyed attach ledgers); DS-5b (PA-32 stamps, settings on the host); journal trimming/compaction; the History UI (PJ, unruled); retiring `field.agents.v1` (DS-D14, now possible); the pin moves (puppeteer, ghosttea, rosetta — the last carries PROTOCOL_VERSION 24; truffle on a petition window with the sidecars).

## DS wave 2 — the plane consumed, hardened, and the phone's ground (2026-10-01)

**LANDED on main at `6856b52e` (65 commits over `d71883fe`; fast-forward; `pnpm verify` verbatim EXIT 0 on that tip — its third run, started at a 1-minute load of 23; run 1 (62 commits) was red on ONE real row the lead's fsync'd writer had exposed and run 2 (64) on ONE real row SP-1's stream floor had exposed, each attributed by bisection and fixed as a landing commit, neither a lottery).** The same morning wave 1 landed James said *"good, plan and go ahead"* to the roadmap status, and seven Opus builders ran in parallel on their own SSD worktrees from main `d71883fe` (plan of record `draft/work/ds-wave2-2026-10-01.md`; every mid-wave ruling is in its "Decisions taken mid-wave" list — twice a lane never received the lead's message and found the ruling there instead). The lead cherry-picked each lane sha-for-sha onto `ds2/landing`, resolved eight small conflicts (imports, adjacent fields, and the forwarding envelope block one lane had moved while another changed a guard inside its old location), and added seven landing commits of its own. No pin moved; the four sibling branches of wave 1 stay James's.

**D1 — the peer identity is the transport's to give (ds2/identity, 8 commits).** `peer-fieldd` is minted only when the sidecar-injected node id correlates to a roster row that is a `docHost`; a hello that merely CLAIMS the kind is admitted as `tailnet` (the phone's preset), logged once, and its connection is closed for a fresh hello when the roster later admits that node as a desktop. The product hello ack names the daemon's own `deviceId` (optional, a fixture). PeerLink: a call's deadline is the call's, never the shared link's — a timed-out call sends ONE liveness probe (`system.unsubscribe` on a subId no client mints) and drops the link only when that goes unanswered; the silent mark's whole cycle red-proven (offline → online → no call → `awake`); ticket mints leave the keyed-result store (a replayed stale ticket is a refused dial); `FORWARDING.RESULT_CAP_BYTES` replaces a literal; the forwarding envelope is judged on EVERY path (the built-ins and the dynamic router returned before it) and narrowed to what asserts — `onBehalfOf` from a non-peer and a malformed envelope are refused, a bare key anywhere but a routed mutation (and an empty `forward: {}`) is set aside with a debug line. Component gate: preflight, biome, the workspace typecheck, gen clean, contracts 666, fieldd 1610.

**DS-1b — RFC 026 consumed on this repo's side (ds2/egress, 5 commits).** The `TruffleEgress` arm is re-typed against truffle `92ab2b7` as built — every `NodeError` and `NetworkError` variant matched EXHAUSTIVELY, so a new upstream variant breaks the feature build at the pin move — and COMPILED under a local `--config` cargo patch to the branch (`cargo test -p field-native --features truffle-egress` EXIT 0; clippy clean; red before: five `E0631 expected fn(NodeError) found fn(NetworkError)`); the committed tree keeps `truffle-core = "=0.7.14"` and the feature OFF. `FloorEgress` asks the floor ONCE per `NativeHealth.bootId` and caches only a grant or `egress-unsupported`: unsupported or a pre-DS-1 floor → the OS network, logged once per boot; anything else → the dial FAILS `UNAVAILABLE {service: "mesh", state}`, retryable, and never builds the OS socket (DS-L5); a grant whose proxy fails at connect, greeting or auth is forgotten once. `EgressCellRewriter` (new) is the production rewriter DS-4 left a port for: one route per owner desktop to the roster's tailnet name:9422 (id `egress-<deviceId>-9422` — the route-id charset refuses `cell:<id>`), one reference per owner however many tickets, both doors re-homed onto the loopback listener with path and query kept, removed when the owner leaves the roster and at clean stop, wired as the default in `daemon.ts`. **The two-floor probe PASSED on the real tailnet** (`field-native/tests/mesh_egress_probe.rs`, `#[ignore]`, feature-gated, the sidecar built from the branch): floor A answered `native.mesh.egress.proxy`; a SOCKS5 client dialled floor B's door by its MagicDNS name through A's proxy and B saw A's `Tailscale-Node-Id`, the only connect the proxy's loopback address, a wrong credential refused; A bound a route to B's name:9422 and B saw A's node id through it; a target outside the netmap → `TARGET_NOT_PEER`; a removed route's listener gone — 9.7 s. The two-desktop run with the Tailscale app QUIT is James's, after the pin move. Production still answers `egress-unsupported`.

**DS-5c — the host hardened, and the inbound phone gate (ds2/host, 12 commits).** D3: the inbound doc lane is gated on `isDocHostPeer` (the row rule the outbound fan-out already used) — a phone's VERSION is refused unclaimed. The HELLO/GET proof: the daemon keeps the read HELLO_OK described until the GET, so the proof cannot overstate what the window read — no client change. A lost eager-replication answer is re-greeted on a doc-sync BEAT (`DOC_HOST.BEAT_MS` 15 s, `ANSWER_TIMEOUT_MS` 30 s, backoff to 10 min) and no send is refused for size (large records chunked). Residency: a hosted canvas idle `DOC_HOST.IDLE_MS` (10 min) is persisted and evicted by a sweep every minute, its head version kept for the holders slice, reloaded on the next VERSION or open. `SystemDocFile` (new): one writer queue per system document, `<file>.<pid>.tmp` → fsync → the previous file kept as `.last-good` → rename → dir fsync; a torn file is moved aside and the last good copy loads — adopted by the library. Reassembly is fair (slots per peer per DOCUMENT under `REASSEMBLY_BYTES_PER_PEER`, refused not evicted); version-speaker marks leave with their peer; the S4 epoch fence holds on the checkpoint-merge path; a `local` canvas held elsewhere is listed with its `home` and not openable there (DS-D7); two falsified claims corrected at their sources.

**SP-1 — every subscription the tailnet can open says what its frames are (ds2/projection, 5 commits).** `subscription: true` becomes `true | {shape: "rows" | "snapshot-delta" | "stream", cadenceFloorMs}` and the registry lint refuses a bare `true` on any subscription with a tailnet-preset scope or a `federate`/`stream` locality, pinning the reachable set and the three scope-less product rows so a new one must be classified (red proof: a stripped descriptor → `expected [ 'device.subscribe' ] to deeply equal []`). `projection.ts` — `projectRows · diffRows · RevisionedSubscription` with a per-subscriber trailing-edge floor (19 rows, 4 mutation probes); the field board rides it with its 91 rows untouched. The roster, the artifact catalog, the service providers and the profile sets ride it at `PRODUCT_API_LIMITS.STREAM_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` (250) with their wire unchanged; the index streams' floors are clamped at the daemon call sites (they were defaults a caller could undercut to 16 ms). `system.tick`: a notification table (`PRODUCT_NOTIFICATIONS.TICK`), a `SystemTick` schema and fixture — not a METHODS row — sent on every hello'd door connection every `TICK_INTERVAL_MS` (120 s), one timer per connection, gone with it; fieldd-client hears it (`onTick`) and takes every unknown notification quietly.

**DS-6b and the client half of DS-D15 (ds2/readers, 9 commits; `pnpm verify` EXIT 0 in one run at load 58).** The replica's forced reset holds until a snapshot LANDS (`RowsApplied.replaced`; a half snapshot is abandoned at every attach, drop and detach; `ROWS.MAX_PENDING_DELTAS` 256, then reset); a row the reader cannot parse keeps its KEY as unreadable in the digest and in the kept files, so the writer's digest and the reader's agree; `useSubscription(method, params, {params, onReplayFailed})`; the search sources read the ROSTER (away = asleep, awake/restarting = timeout, a not-ready door = building — the error is not the state); dispose rewrites only the tables whose kept `heardAt` is behind; a dead write's `.tmp` is swept at start; a refused `/ws/meta` upgrade is phase `refused`, WARN once, retried at the resnapshot cadence (the bearer follows at RO-1's pin move). DS-D15's client half: `isKeyedForward(def)` and `KEYED_FORWARD_METHODS` are the rule's ONE statement in contracts; `request(method, params, {idempotencyKey})` keys every forwarded mutation routed to a foreign device once, every error of a keyed call carries `error.forward.idempotencyKey`, the client's own post-send cut reads `outcome-unknown`, `forwardReceiptOf()` tells a receipt-in-place-of-result apart; field-app's `requestResolvingOutcome` retries once with the same key at the launcher's spawn and resume and at the routed-host ticket — a window echoes the key. Found: at `d71883fe` no renderer site forwards a mutation by `device` (the launcher, the routed host, Godview's remote attach), so the renderer half of DS-4's remote attach is owed.

**DS-5b — PA-32's bias, and settings cross (ds2/settings, 4 commits).** The install-set is split into ROOT MAPS per field (plugins · enabled · grants · revocations) so independent fields merge independently — B1 was one last-writer-wins value per entry. A capability's revocation GENERATION is the NUMBER OF REVOCATION KEYS it holds, a grow-only set that is race-free (loro-crdt's counter merged two concurrent first revocations to 1, the exact race the generation exists to win); every grant decision records the generation it saw; contracts' `standingDecision` answers `{granted, reason: decision | revocation-bias | stamp-ahead}`; `apply()` applies a grant that missed a revocation as REVOKED, audited `REVOCATION_BIAS`; `publish()` writes only the act's own decision (the `plugins.grants.set` handler passes `{capability, granted, changed}`); a dev-linked or sideloaded plugin never enters the document. The settings document is registered with the host beside the library, the three B1 hold notes replaced with dated lines, `users.ts`'s claim corrected. Rows (each red first): a revoke on A beats a concurrent grant on B in both merge orders; a re-grant after the revoke was seen stands; a daemon-level merge never re-grants a revocation; a spine preference set on A reads on B; an entry from before the stamps still applies.

**SP-2 and DS-4b — the phone's door brick v2 and the take (ds2/phone, 14 commits; the kit suite green, its two known time-sensitive re-ask rows green alone).** `PHONE_BUDGET` in contracts (as built: doors, two terminal legs, one web view; SP-D12 OPEN), mirrored and pinned in the kit, `check-ios-fixtures` extended. `ProductKeepalive`: the receive deadline is 2.5 × the interval the door's tick announces (the registry's 120 s until the first tick; intervals outside 1 s…1 h noted, not applied), ANY inbound frame is liveness, and the phone sends a WebSocket PING when it has sent nothing — the sidecar reaps EACH DIRECTION of a served socket on its own ten-minute clock (`sidecar-slim main.go idleCopy`, read at source), so the door's tick alone keeps only door→phone alive. The roster is asked before every dial (asleep never dialled, restarting always). A subscription table per door: a cursor per subscription, a gap resnapshots, the cadence rides every subscribe, a door naming no revision passes frames through. Bytes per second per subscription logged. A client the door stopped is replaced on a backoff while its peer stays online. The door outranks the slice once it has hello'd. Pause and resume one desktop at a time, with an epoch so a pause and a resume inside one answer cannot cross. DS-4b: the phone's pane takes the seat when it gains focus — a claim on an empty seat, ONE transfer from a held one, one retry on the announcement, the client owning the retry; a grant without `geometry` sends no verb.

**The lead's landing commits (7).** `2f499b40` the full fold refused to `tailnet` (SP-L4 — a phone's bare `agent.subscribe {}` was the whole board at the 16 ms tick; the shipped kit asks `field`) · `745c44e1` the door's auto-pong pinned with a row that trips when it is off · `590a0066` the door's three inline keyed-forward statements → contracts' `isKeyedForward(def)` · `16b5d1cf` a dial that failed closed is an ANSWER: fieldd-client keeps the egress stand-in socket's structured error as the dial's verdict and rejects every pending call and `ready()` waiter with it on the close that follows, still redialling; PeerLink maps the verdict to the caller as the floor's own UNAVAILABLE state and leaves the peer's record untouched (red: the client `did not settle within 1000 ms`; PeerLink `expected RpcCallError: peer call timed out … to match object {…}`) · `f0640800` `SystemDocFile` adopted in `settings-doc.ts` (red: the interleaved persists lost the merged change; a torn file read as first boot) · `f1e56140` the phone's ping follows the door's own interval (`min(announced, 120 s)`) and the ping timer re-arms on a tick (red: four silent closes, then one) · `0a1c8698` the install reconciler never applies a document older than this device's own acts — `publish()` registers each in-flight local publication and `applyOnce` waits for them (red, deterministic: the full gate's `plugin-settings.test.ts` "disable keeps settings/KV on disk; re-enable restores read access" — `invalid token` at a fresh principal's hello; bisected to the fsync'd writer, which widened a pre-existing race from a millisecond to tens; the probe showed `teardownPlugin ← applyEntry ← applyOnce`) · `6856b52e` the artifact hub's convergence row waits for the floored delta (the only bare instant-assertion on the four moved streams; bisected to SP-1's streams commit).

**Rulings taken at the landing (all in the plan):** the keepalive is BIDIRECTIONAL — SP-L7 corrected at its three sources · `system.tick` is a notification table, not a method row · `full` is refused to the phone · the lint pins the three scope-less subscriptions · `services.subscribe` and `agents.profileSets.subscribe` ride the helper too · the envelope refusal narrows to what asserts and the hello ack names the device · DS-D15's window half is one helper and no dormant device plumbing · the settings file's race is the shared writer's to close · no lane runs the full gate; the one `pnpm verify` is the lead's on the landing tip · ready lanes land first (the written order only moves who resolves which conflict).

**Found, no record carried:** the sidecar reaps each direction of a served WebSocket separately (`main.go:2753-2771`, `idleCopy :2987-3001`) · `system.health.subscribe` is phone-reachable (scope null; D36's `local` refuses only peer daemons) — EL7-adjacent, James's to weigh · the four moved whole-value streams now reach a window up to 250 ms after a change that used to arrive at once (a leading-edge emit when idle is the trade, against the board's "one frame per window") · nothing sweeps egress routes a superseded daemon left · the truffle sidecar refuses ANY held route id even for the same target and lists no in-flight placeholder — the floor mirror is the only idempotence (T7 follow-up) · mgmt error data nests under `data.details` · the probe harness reads `.env` relative to the worktree · `egress:add`'s `login` glob buys nothing a linked node's gate does not · `FORWARDED_MINTS` and the keyed-forward set are different sets · a terminally failed fieldd-client handed every caller the same `lastError` (fixed in readers) · mid-flight SendMessages to busy builders were lost outright three times.

**Not built:** the two-desktop run with the Tailscale app quit (James, after truffle's release and the protocol-6 sidecars); E3; the renderer half of DS-4's remote attach by `device`; the engine-side CAS for the take and DS-4c; DS-7 (RO-1/RO-10 at rosetta's pin move); DS-8; DS-9; retiring `field.agents.v1` (after the phone reads the field through the door, usage fields included); SP-3…SP-8; the two owed designs (SP-D7, SP-D9); a leading-edge emit for the moved streams; local idempotency for self-served keyed calls; the kit's device run.

## TL — Godview's timeline: the swarm through time, and fieldd's status ledger (2026-10-02)

Godview has a fourth view, TIMELINE: each agent is a lane in birth order, and its afternoon is one wake. The wake swells into work in its project's colour, with a soft glow, and narrows through a short S-curve into an orange or blue thread for a wait and a hairline for rest. The swarm's bodies sit at the head, lit as the swarm lights them, each with its readout ("12:42 working"), and the one you owe rings. Pointing at a lane (or ↑ ↓) quiets the rest and prints every span's length. Looking back relights the bodies to that moment ("4:39 idle · of 7m"); NOW glides back. Above the axis, the map of the day: the whole field as one ridge, work stacked by project above a line, waits below, gray outside the window in view. Pressing the map puts the head there, and dragging plays the afternoon back on the bodies; it is a slider (← → 5 min, ⇧ 30, Home, End). An agent that ended stays as a faint lane; rows outside the chosen profile recede; bare terminals sit in a quiet group. James ruled design F with its map (TL-D1) and every other mark at its lean on 2026-10-02.

Puppeteer `feat/timeline` carries the view side. `monitor/status-history.ts` defines the book a host hands the views: spans per lane, `recordedFromMs`, and the ended rows. `AgentMonitorProps.history?` is optional, and a view without it draws births and current states. `monitor/status-ledger.ts` is a host's record, built purely from the rows it projects: unseen replies, peers from first heard, and a durable record merged under. `views/timeline/` is the view. Its pure model (lanes, scale, wake geometry, Pulse, words) is unit-tested; the component paints two canvases and keeps DOM for heads, names and the slider. The registry gains TIMELINE after rain (swarm stays first), the bar gains its mark, and `MonitorPalette.timeline` (ground, muted, border) is read from the host's aliases. Puppeteer's own Godview app keeps a ledger too. VibeField `tl/timeline` carries the rest:
- DESIGN.md §2.6 records one exception: a working span may wear its project's colour where the shape carries the state. §8 gains the timeline's entry.
- Contracts add `agent.history` (`agent.observe`, `local`), `AGENT_HISTORY` (a day, 2,000 changes, 160-char texts), `LAYOUT.AGENT_HISTORY_DIR`, and the mirror's `activity`.
- fieldd's fold keeps a ledger per run in `users/<fuid>/agents/history/<run>.jsonl` (0700/0600). It is appended on each status change at Core's `statusSince` and never runs backwards. A working span keeps its last activity line, and a blocked one its blocker's words. `unknown` marks a stop, a withdrawn run and a pending re-attach. A re-attached run resumes its file. Retention follows the records.
- The reader is EL7-tolerant: safe ids, `O_NOFOLLOW`, single-link regular files, the last MiB only, bad lines skipped.
- Godview asks `agent.history` when the fold goes live and lays it under the window's own ledger. Runs that ended inside the day are named from their fold rows, and the stage narrows ended lanes as it narrows live rows. The catalog mounts the shipping view over a fixture fold and ledger.

Found along the way:
- The merge dropped fieldd's activity line at a moment both had seen. VibeField's stage test caught it, and it was fixed in puppeteer `48651ab`.
- An independent review of the view found ten defects:
  - A zoom pressed mid-tween left the head detached.
  - Every fold projection repainted both canvases in full: lanes were rebuilt per frame and up to 2,000 spans were walked unwindowed.
  - A drag stayed armed after a release outside the body.
  - The focus ring parked on lane 0 on a mouse click.
  - The lit and focused lanes were indices, so ↵ opened the wrong agent after an ended lane scrolled out.
  - Panning back pushed the map's lens off the map.
  - The map repainted on every hover.
  - The canvas keys missed the device pixel ratio.
  - `matchMedia` and `closest()` ran every frame.
  - The slider lacked its aria values in the first markup.
  All ten are fixed with tests. The four that needed real input were checked against the pre-fix view.
- Mounted in Godview, the view had painted an opaque ground over the stage's glass, ignored the usage column, and printed under the claims strip. It now shows the stage through, insets by `--vf-monitor-chrome-right`, and godview.css pads it as it pads the list.
- The ambient-motion audit (GT-D15.1) now admits the owed ring by name. It is pinned to transform and opacity, runs only while the timeline is mounted and a body is owed, and stops under reduced motion and animations-off.
- Wall R23b caught agent ids spelled in the catalog fixture; it now names agents by catalog row. The fieldd builder's first test run built field-native into the shared cargo target; main's sources were touched so main rebuilds its own.

Validation:
- Puppeteer:
  - typecheck is clean in every package and app.
  - views passes 609 tests, godview 273; `packages:check` is clean.
  - `pnpm -r test` is green in every package.
  - Root `pnpm test` is red only at the adapter-codex ground-truth map ("stale") and its script test, the same at the pin `a4b5290`.
  - The view's real-input CDP checks pass 25/25, and its shots match the prototype's F at 1320 and 400 px in both themes.
- VibeField, on the lane:
  - `pnpm verify` passed preflight (R23 and R23b), deps, iOS fixtures, icons, typecheck (25 projects), biome, `cargo fmt`, clippy and `bundle:assert`.
  - `pnpm test` lost one row: fieldd's DS-5c "reassembly is fair", at load 27; it passed three times alone. contracts passed 689 and fieldd 1,718.
  - `test:rust` passed 297 (9 ignored), and `gen:check` showed no drift.
  - `smoke:godview` (with the two switches) failed three runs under load 22–27, each on a different deck row (the zoom round trip, a pane's cwd, a ⌘-held link). A control built from main `6856b52e` failed the cwd row once at load 57 and passed twice as load fell. The branch then passed three in a row.
  - The catalog's timeline specimen, in headless Chrome through the real door, hook and ledger, drew with no page errors.

Not built:
- Threads (TL-D15 ruled Pulse).
- A peer's durable history: `agent.history` is `local`, and a peer waits on the sync plane.
- Unseen moments across Godview closes: `unread.ts` reseeds at open by design.
- A crash's gap: only a graceful stop records `unknown`.
- Peer rows draw a generic desktop mark, because `MonitorRemoteFacet` carries no OS.

Decisions: TL-D1…TL-D17 (ruled 2026-10-02 on the page *Where the Time Went*), `draft/godview-timeline/design-timeline.md` §B.

## AR — a verified sign-in re-reads that account's usage at once (2026-10-02)

A persona's login pane could end with the agent signed in while the usage meter kept the pre-login reading: the row went on saying "Sign in required", and that failure's cooldown held the next reading back for up to 30 minutes (Claude's poll interval). Now a login pane that EXITS and verifies as signed in calls `onProfileSignedIn`, a new `AgentRuntimeServiceOptions` seam, and fieldd wires it to `AccountUsageService.signedIn(profileId)`. That reconciles the persona registry without polling, asks puppeteer's monitor to drop that account's pre-login reading (`invalidateProfileAuthentication`), and reads that one account again only while a window is subscribed. Unwatched, the old reading is still cleared and the next subscriber reads afresh. A failure in the hook is logged (`fieldd.agents.login_usage_failed`) and never fails the pane's own close.

The monitor method is puppeteer `6392865`, and the pin moves to it. Only a local authentication failure is reset: a rate limit or a Retry-After still in the future survives. A reading already in flight settles first, so a fetch that began before the login cannot restore the failure. The account's last good meters are dropped either way, since a login can switch accounts.

Tests: agent-usage gains two rows (only the newly signed-in account is rechecked instead of keeping its pre-login failure for 30 minutes; a completed login's old usage is cleared while unwatched and waits for a subscriber). Agent-session's login-pane row now drives a fake Claude usage service from `unauthenticated` to `available` across the login, with exactly two readings. Puppeteer's monitor gains three rows; its runtime suite is 441/441. Witness (2026-10-02, a clean worktree at this commit, puppeteer at `6392865`): fieldd typecheck; agent-usage 16 passed, 1 skipped; agent-session 36 passed, 2 skipped over the real floor, the login-pane row among them; the landing's `pnpm verify` EXIT 0 at its tip (the runs: LANDED §UI the living mark, 2026-10-02).

Provenance: James's work in both repositories (2026-09-27/28), carried uncommitted across DS waves 1–2 and TL.

## UI — After Hours: the Fieldmarks sticker edition, in the catalog (2026-10-02; drawn 2026-09-22)

Edition 02 of the Fieldmarks study: 77 new drawings and the exact VibeField loop, as a set of retro laptop stickers in three registers (character and brand at 112 units, desk objects at 72, action stamps at 48/50), with unequal contours, black side planes, hatching and bitmap lettering instead of one line weight. Two finishes share each drawing: the sticker adds a white die-cut keyline, the artwork omits it. Both have an ink layer in `currentColor` and an opaque paper layer (`--vf-sticker-paper`).

What is real: `tooling/fieldmarks/generate.py` (the drawing source) emits `packages/design-kit/assets/fieldmarks/` (both finishes and the sprites), the kit's `src/icons/data.ts` and `catalogue.json`, and the SVG archive. `@vibefield/design-kit/icons` exports `FieldIcon`, typed names, metadata and `fieldIconSvg(name, finish)`. The catalog mounts `IconsSection` as 02a "After Hours", and `tooling/fieldmarks/build.mjs` bundles the same section into the offline `docs/design/fieldmarks.html`. DESIGN.md §11 is the direction; `docs/design/fieldmarks.md` and `fieldmarks-review/` are the study and its photographs.

It is an illustration register, not chrome: the chrome's functional icons are §13's glyphs, and §11 keeps the app, tray and Icon Composer masters exact. Nothing in the product draws it yet. The review JSON was formatted by biome at the landing; unformatted, it failed the whole-tree lint. `biome.jsonc` leaves `packages/design-kit/assets/` to its generators, as it leaves the glyphs' `data.ts`: the lint refused the sprite sheets' root `<svg>` for want of a `<title>`, and a sheet of `<symbol>`s is not an image. ## UI — Face Club: the account deck drawn in After Hours ink (2026-10-02; drawn 2026-09-22)

All 48 emoji in contracts' `FACE_DECK`, in deck order, redrawn as original black-and-white stickers. Each subject has two optical masters: 112 units, detailed, from 40px, and 56 units, simplified, at 16–39px. They are separate geometry, not a filter, and the switch sits on the face's existing 40px tilt threshold. Anatomy and silhouette carry recognition; colour never deals or disambiguates users.

What is real: `tooling/face-stickers/art.py` (the drawing source) and `generate.py`, which checks all 48 emoji against the current policy before writing 192 SVGs and two sprites to `packages/design-kit/assets/face-stickers/`. `@vibefield/design-kit/face-stickers` exports `FaceSticker`, typed ids, metadata, `findFaceSticker(emoji)` (variation selectors ignored, as `faceKey` does; unknown emoji return `undefined`) and `faceStickerSvg`. The catalog mounts `FaceStickersSection` as 02b "Face Club", beside the shipping `UserFaceView` for comparison, and `build.mjs` bundles it into the offline `docs/design/face-stickers.html`. DESIGN.md §11.1 is the direction; `docs/design/face-stickers.md` and `face-stickers-review/` are the study.

§2.8's emoji face stays the shipping policy and renderer: dealing, collisions, tilt, the coin and persistence are unchanged, and adopting the art is a separate step. Recognition at 16px is a review question, not a claim a bounds test settles. `.gitignore` gains `__pycache__/`, which the generator's import of `art.py` leaves behind. Witness: at this commit, design-kit and field-app typecheck; the catalog, ui-system-boundaries and glyph suites, 29/29; the landing's `pnpm verify` EXIT 0 at its tip (the runs: LANDED §UI the living mark, 2026-10-02).

## UI — the living mark: the logo as a WebGPU ribbon, and its studio (2026-10-02; drawn 2026-09-22)

The infinity and RGB identity as a continuous paper-white ribbon with a fine spectral edge in a radial field of light, with a definite over/under crossing and a Möbius half-twist that circulates along the fixed path while both lobes stay readable. Five presets (Prism, the reference, then Afterglow, Daylight, Signal and Ink) over independent parameters for geometry, edge colour, field, grain and movement.

What is real: one native WebGPU renderer behind the kit's `./logo` leaf (`shader.ts`, `renderer.ts`, `parameters.ts`, `motion.ts`, `LivingLogo.tsx`), with a static SVG of the same curve for missing GPUs and for export. Reduced motion starts still, and hidden or offscreen canvases stop rendering. The catalog's 02c "Living mark" specimen links to the Logo Studio, a design-mode entry (`logo-studio.html`, `pnpm dev:logo`, built by `build:design`, never a production document entry). Tests cover the renderer, the parameters and the motion; the dev-runner's vite-server rows name the studio in the shared optimizer graph and in the design build's inputs, still disjoint from the product's; `@webgpu/types` joins the kit's dev dependencies. DESIGN.md §12 is the direction and `docs/design/living-mark.md` the study.

It is authored brand artwork: its colours are not interface or status ink, and it does not replace the packaged icon masters. Not committed: `docs/design/logo-review/`, the study's 53 MB of review renders, which the doc's image links name. That is larger than every image the repository tracks today combined, so it waits on James's call; the links resolve in his tree only. This in-tree study is separate from the gitignored `draft/mark` lab. Witness: `pnpm verify` EXIT 0 in a clean worktree at the landing's tip, on run 3 (started at a 1-minute load of 23). Run 1 stopped at lint on the three generated sprite sheets (After Hours now leaves `design-kit/assets/` to its generators). Run 2 was red on the two dev-runner rows this commit's studio entry moved (updated here) and on one 5 s timeout in TL's status-ledger file under the test graph's load (12/12 alone, three times; no commit here touches it). In run 3 fieldd (1721 passed, 16 skipped) and dev-runner (117) ran fresh, and Nx replayed run 2's passes for the 23 projects whose inputs had not changed.

## Godview — local rows carry their cost again; TL's stage test stops expiring (2026-10-03)

Two host fixes found while building SV (the spend view). They land alone: James held the view itself until it is rebuilt on the monitor-view SDK (DECISIONS, the laws). Both are runtime data the stage already receives; neither records anything.

- **Local cost (`bce71770`).** Since AR-5 (`fe6b3d0a`) the renderer's `coreUsage` copied tokens and the token burn into the usage ledger and dropped `costUsd`, `costCoverage`, `costRatePerMin` and `costHistory`. LANDED §AR-5-1 (2026-09-21) had named that key list as "the only thing holding a USD readout back on the desktop" and left it. Read from the code, no local swarm body ever had a cost to print. They are carried now; each 30 s bucket is checked, and an unknown coverage word is left out.
- **Peers' totals (same commit).** Another desktop's row carries `agent.usage` from its desk row's `usage.costUsd` and coverage: the total and no steps (none cross desktops; zeros would read as ten quiet minutes). An unpriced run has none, never $0. The swarm now prints a peer body's total as it prints a local one's.
- **TL's stage test (`9b395179`).** `godview-status-history.test.tsx` seeded fieldd's record with literal 2026-10-02 timestamps under the ledger's wall-clock 24 h horizon. From about 2026-10-03 12:10Z the seed was trimmed and two rows went red on main for everyone. Isolated before fixing: the same rows failed with main's own files and on the previous base. The afternoon is now offsets from the suite's own clock. (The ledger itself is to be removed in the SDK migration, TL-D8 reversed.)

- **The WEBGPU UNAVAILABLE row stops flaking.** Its marker follows the swarm's `data-swarm-renderer` through a MutationObserver, which happy-dom 20.11 holds only in a WeakRef. A collection mid-run silenced it: about 2 in 10 whole-file runs, always green alone, and twice in this branch's full runs. The row now delivers the observer by hand, as the spawn-bloom row does. It passed 49/49 three times under forced scavenges, and a probe with the host reading a wrong attribute turns it red.

Validation: `pnpm verify` green on this branch (`NX_DAEMON=false`, the lane's own cargo target, load ~60–90): preflight (one warning: James's rosetta checkout has uncommitted edits), typecheck 25 projects, biome, `cargo fmt`, clippy `-D warnings`, `bundle:assert`, `pnpm test` (field-app 1,480, fieldd 1,722 with 16 skipped, contracts 703, electron-shell 804 with 2 skipped), `test:rust` 297 (9 ignored), `gen:check` clean. The two runs before the WEBGPU row's fix were red on that row alone; main's own code passed it once in a full field-app run, red only on the two expired TL rows. The SV branch carrying the same two fixes had passed `pnpm verify` three times and `smoke:godview`.

**The pin event, twice.** `pnpm siblings:pin rosetta` against the dedicated checkout `../rosetta-pin` (W-D10) moved the lock `886baede` → `ee6724e` (`65111956`): rosettad rebuilt at the pin, wall R23 green (28 self-checks, 10 providers through fieldd's edge, 9 history kinds from the daemon's own `discover`). **The lane's `pnpm verify` then went RED at typecheck** — `rosetta-pin/clients/ts/client.ts:152` named `HeadersInit`, a DOM-lib type: rosetta's own `tsc -p clients/ts` passes with the DOM lib, fieldd compiles the linked client under `lib: ["ES2022"]` + `@types/node`, where `RequestInit` is a global and `HeadersInit` is not. ## AR-8b — fieldd's History doors and the direct plane's ticket: rosettad behind a bearer, three reads, and a grant that opens one session's socket (2026-10-03; `e5003804` contracts · `349f6b69` fieldd; lane ar8b-doors over the pin `eecae7a`)

**James:** the AR-8 plan ruled 2026-10-03 (AR-D36 the shape; D37…D43 as leaned — "Go ahead and do them for me"); this is the fieldd half, built beside AR-8a (the room as a package, upstream, still in its lane). The plan is `draft/thinking-ar-history-room.md` §3; its errata from this build are recorded there.

**The doors (contracts first; all `index.search`, `federate`, idempotent; fixtures parsed both sides; `pnpm gen` committed).** `index.session {sessionId, device?}` → `{session}`: the header row — `IndexSession` plus `parentSessionId`, `profileId`, `project {id, name}`, `projectId`, `provider`, `startedAt`; a 404 is `NOT_FOUND`. `index.project {projectId, sinceMs?, offsetMinutes? (−840…840), device?}` → `{projectId, heatmap[], usage {models[], hours[]}, contribution[], clipped}` — rosettad's three bearer-only project aggregates read in ONE flight and parsed against VibeField's own snake_case readers (five goldens transcribed from the pin's `wire.json`); a 503 is `UNAVAILABLE building`; a tailnet caller's contribution rows stop at `INDEX_TAILNET_LIMITS.MAX_ROWS` with `clipped`. `index.projectDay {projectId, day (a real YYYY-MM-DD), offsetMinutes?, device?}` → `{projectId, day, models[]}`.

**The ticket.** `index.openTicket {sessionId}` answers `IndexOpenTicket {device, endpoints, grant, expiresAt}`. For a window the endpoints are a NEW loopback shape, `IndexEndpointSet {sessionUrl: ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/ws/sessions/<id>, restUrl: http://127.0.0.1:<port>}` — the plan had said `RemoteEndpointSet`, which refuses loopback by law (D36: a routed set names a served process on the tailnet), so the loopback pair sits beside it as the cell's `CellEndpointSet` does, and `IndexOpenTicket.endpoints` is the union of the two. The grant is `mintGrant` (`@rosetta/protocol/grants`, Node) with `sid` = the session, `cid` = `clientIdFor(principal)`, `scope ["read"]`, `exp` = now + `INDEX_TICKET.TTL_MS` (600 s, strictly increasing); the mint is audited as `index.ticket.mint` on target `index-session`. Refusals: a plugin, an MCP agent or a guest → `FORBIDDEN_SCOPE`; the phone and a peer forward → `UNAVAILABLE direct-plane-unbuilt` (DS-7's); the flag off → `direct-plane-off` (`INDEX_TICKET.STATE_OFF`); the daemon not ready → its phase; a lone-surrogate id → `PRECONDITION_FAILED` (a `URIError` in both session-path composers fixed on the way).

**The supervisor.** Credentials are minted PER DAEMON START, not per boot (the plan's word, corrected: a restart revokes every grant): a bearer of 32 random bytes base64url and a 32-byte grant key, written 0600 in a 0700 `users/<fuid>/index/auth/` (`token`, `grant.key`; LAYOUT `INDEX_AUTH_DIR`, `INDEX_TOKEN_FILE`, `INDEX_GRANT_KEY_FILE`; `registries.rs` regenerated, the Rust layout vector green), passed as `--token-file`, `--grant-key-file` and `--allow-origin` — the last derived from fieldd's own allow-list filtered to rosetta's grammar (`vibefield-app://shell` passes; a `file://` entry would make rosettad refuse to start), never a literal. The files are REMOVED as soon as the daemon's ready line arrives (`auth {bearer: true, grants: true, origins: [...]}`) and the credentials are held only in memory (`supervisor.credentials()`), never in `RosettadState` or health; fieldd's own reads carry `Authorization: Bearer`. A ready line without `auth`, or a binary that says "unknown flag --token-file", is a TERMINAL failure — the pin's daemon has the flags and an older one is the wrong binary. `indexDirectPlane` is now ON unless config says false, gated on the generation's auth modes.

**Witnessed on the REAL pinned rosettad (`eecae7a`).** fieldd starts the daemon with the three flags; the ready line says `auth {bearer: true, grants: true, origins: ["vibefield-app://shell"]}`; the ground-truth claude transcript is indexed; a window asks `index.openTicket {sessionId}`; rosetta's own `RosettaClient` holding `{credential: {kind: "grant"}}` reads the header row and receives a `subscribeSession` snapshot — **the first byte of the direct plane**. The same grant is refused as wrong-session for another `sid` (page and socket) and as wrong-route on `/api/sessions` and `/ws/meta`. Kill matrix: after a daemon restart the old grant is bad-signature on the new generation and the next ask re-tickets and streams. **W-D10's leftover fixed:** three older real-rosettad rows read `../rosetta/groundtruth` and had skipped in every lane since the checkout moved; they read `../rosetta-pin` now and run.

**Tests.** contracts 38 files / 763 (the new `agent-index-history.test.ts`, 11 rows); fieldd 147 files / 1,833 passed / 6 pre-existing skips — supervisor +7 (1 real), the ticket 17 (3 real, 3 minter unit rows), the doors 9 (`index-history-doors.test.ts`), serve +2, catalog +1 (the bearer row). Red proofs: 16 contracts + 30 fieldd mutations, each red on its named rows, the tree restored under a sha256 check (the 7 timeout reds were the mutation's own, judged from their messages).

**Gate (the lane).** Run 1 EXIT 1 at preflight — the pin skew (the lane's lock said `ee6724e` while the shared checkout had moved to `eecae7a`; the lock move was taken as a cherry-pick, dropped at landing as already upstream). Run 2 EXIT 1 at test — `agent-gateway-panes` row 15, "the terminal floor is not available", at load 217; the file alone 11/11 twice. **Run 3 EXIT 0:** preflight · check:deps · ios-fixtures · icons · typecheck 25 projects · biome 1,758 files, 0 errors, 37 warnings none new · cargo fmt · clippy · bundle:assert 756.0 KB raw / 190.1 KB gz · test 5,635 passed, 11 skipped across 24 vitest suites, dev-runner 117/117 · test:rust 302 passed, 9 ignored · gen:check clean. Landed by rebasing the two commits onto main `7b6edaa1` — the rebased tree differs from the gated one by main's four docs files only — then a fast-forward.

**Findings for AR-8c (the mount).** rosetta's client retries a refused 401 upgrade silently with no `onError`: the renderer's `SessionPort` must renew before `expiresAt` through `client.setCredential()` and build a NEW client when `restUrl` changes after a daemon restart. `<img>` assets need the fetched path (AR-D40). **Owed:** the tailnet ticket set (SP-6, DS-7 — a `rest` leg on a routed `RemoteIndexEndpointSet`) · `index.openTicket` in `forward-receipts`' `TICKET_MINTS` once a forward can be answered with a ticket · `api.html`'s hero numbers (corrected in this landing's docs commit: 54 agent-plane doors, 12 that federate) · the catalogue's "every door local" sentence, older than this slice.

## FS-1b / FS-2 — History opens its worktree; the phone chooses a desktop folder and launches there (2026-10-05; `83909e1f` + `634f0582`)
