## RD-1 + RD-2 — one lock, two coordinates, two shapes: a sibling's `release` is its prod coordinate, `pnpm siblings render --prod` writes the committed rows and the pre-commit hook holds them, and `pnpm siblings use NAME` links a released sibling through a gitignored root `.pnpmfile.cjs` with a dev lockfile — the committed lock is never the overlay's (2026-10-15; `60eb1cf5` `c4431a62`)

**Why:** thinking-release-deps.md §2/§3/§5 — the fourth rung of the prod-builder brief's order (RD-0…RD-4, then RD-6):
the committed repo in prod shape, development a local overlay generated from the same lock, one verb to link a sibling
and one to stand on the published pins again. RD-1 builds the verbs and the mode; RD-2 is the npm spike that decides
how pnpm installs the overlay. They land together (the PM's call: one story on the RD row).

**What landed:**
- **RD-1 (`60eb1cf5`).** `siblings.lock.json` gains a `release` block per entry — the prod coordinate per plane (`npm`:
  one exact version for all the sibling's `packages`; `cargo`: `{ git, rev }`). A plane with a release is committed
  exact; one without stays committed as its link:/path rows. rosetta's entry carries both coordinates (`packages`
  clients/ts and clients/room — the overlay's link targets — and `release.npm` 0.1.1). `scripts/siblings.mjs`:
  `render --prod [--check] [--staged]` writes (or compares) the committed overrides and `[patch.crates-io]` rows from
  the lock, in place (on today's tree a no-op: "12 npm, 6 cargo"); `use NAME…`, `use --none`, bare `use`; `status`
  prints the shape first; `siblingShape` is the one derivation of the shape (preflight, status and use print it in the
  same words, the overlay marked); `linkedPackages` the one answer to "which packages are linked here" (check:deps asks
  it); the Nx stamp carries the overlay. Preflight checks each package's committed row as the lock renders it. A new
  `scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit` runs `render --prod --check --staged`: a commit whose staged rows its own lock does not
  render is refused in words (SKIP_SHAPE=1 bypasses, said in the commit). `pnpm siblings` is the bare CLI.
- **RD-2 (`c4431a62`).** The overlay is a gitignored ROOT `.pnpmfile.cjs` that pnpm loads for every command. Its
  `updateConfig` sets the overrides (each linked package → `link:` its checkout; every relative link: row made absolute),
  `lockfileDir` (the dev lock, `.vibefield/dev/pnpm-lock.yaml`) and `virtualStoreDir` (the tree's one store); its
  `readPackage` gives the root manifest the linked packages' own dependencies. `use NAME` seeds the dev lock from the
  committed one (importers rebased) and installs; a root `postinstall` (`siblings.mjs align`) links each linked package's
  dependencies and peers into its checkout and re-points pnpm's hidden hoist; `use --none` installs the committed lock
  frozen and points the hoist back at the store's release copy; every switch ends with `ensureElectronBinary`.
  Preflight FAILS a root pnpmfile with no overlay recorded and WARNs an overlay that is not installed. `.gitignore`
  names `/.pnpmfile.cjs`.

**Validation:**
- RD-1: `pnpm verify` EXIT 0 in lane rd1 (07:07Z; vitest 8,525 / 17 skipped, cargo 302 / 9, node --test 160/160); the
  hook refused a staged leaked-overlay row and passed the clean tree.
- RD-2, the spike (lane rd2, ICE 0.16.0 as the stand-in, linked from a worktree at `54b02b8`): **the dev-shape proof is
  run 2 plus the suite re-run** — `pnpm verify` in dev shape with ICE linked: vitest 8,525 passed / 17 skipped / 0
  failed, node --test 163/1 (the one red the guard's own unit test, environment-dependent through Node's search beyond
  the root, fixed in `c4431a62`), then the dev-runner suite 164/0 in BOTH shapes; check:deps one copy each of loro,
  ICE, strata, React and react-dom in both shapes; `git status` naming only the sources after every switch.
- **The prod-shape proof is the landing gate:** `gate:landing --with-stages` on `c4431a62` — 07:46:14–08:17:44Z, 26 of 27 ok (`lanes/rd1/gate-c4431a62.log`): verify's fourteen stages in prod shape (the dev-runner suite 164/0, cargo 302 / 9 ignored), `still`, and every smoke but smoke:canvas, smoke:bundled included.
- Timings: `use ice` 5–7 s, `use --none` 4–5 s; the overlay survived `pnpm exec`, `pnpm run` and a plain `pnpm install`.

**Found:**
- **pnpm 11.13.1's mechanics decide the overlay** (§3's dated note): a pnpmfile's readPackage loses to the workspace
  `overrides` (`createReadPackageHook` pushes `createVersionsOverrider` last); any pnpmfile writes `pnpmfileChecksum`
  into the lock it installs with; a moved lockfile directory resolves relative `link:` overrides against itself and
  builds a second store; a `link:`'s own dependencies are never installed; and an overlay selected by the environment
  dies at the next bare `pnpm exec` (`verify-deps-before-run: install`). The root `.pnpmfile.cjs` answers all five;
  skip-worktree was not needed.
- **A switch's re-import drops output built outside the content store.** The way back's frozen install re-imports the
  virtual store (`Packages: +494`), and Electron's binary (its own install.js) is not in it: the first both-shapes verify
  was red in both shapes on smoke-profile's ENOENT alone. The resolution never moves Electron (resolution-only installs
  keep `electron@43.1.1(supports-color@7.2.0)` in every variant). The guard handles it and says so; neither the shape
  line nor check:deps shows it; run 2's way back is the live witness (`electron-guard=[1]`). CI never switches shape.
- **`minimumReleaseAgeExclude` takes name globs** (`@vibecook/*`), read from pnpm's source; the refusal itself needs a
  fresh publish to witness.
- **Erratum at source (RD-1):** CLAUDE.md's AR-0 paragraph and the overrides block's comment said the npm exit deletes
  the lock entry; since RD-1 the entry stays as the overlay's coordinate. Both corrected where they stand; CLAUDE.md also
  names the verbs, the hook and where the overlay lives — flagged for James's review.
- **The gate's one red is main's:** smoke:canvas (929 s) on ONE row, DK-14's AIMED rung (`@'s list open with a pane to send to did not happen within 10000ms`), word for word the red RD-5a proved main's and WP8's gate named; the occluded, HAND and COVER rows all passed.

**Owed:**
- RD-3: the ghosttea patch into a generated cargo config, `Package.swift` reading the environment, preflight checking
  both shapes. RD-4: the five repos' pipelines (mostly James's hands) — its hand-off. RD-5 per sibling, then RD-6.
- §6's witnesses still open: puppeteer linked with an HMR edit (it is committed dev until RD-5); the dev lock's snapshot
  keys equal the committed lock's outside the linked subtrees (a peer-suffix move shows there); an age refusal (needs a
  fresh publish); rosettad's checksum refusal (RD-D7); CI green on origin with no clone step.
- The spike's lane rd2 (branch `rd/2-spike`, the throwaway `ice` entry) and its ICE worktree stay until the landing is
  read; nothing of them lands.

## RD-3 — the cargo and Swift overlays: a released cargo plane links back through a generated root `.cargo/config.toml` with Cargo.lock hidden while it stands, and a released Swift plane is the manifest's own rendered release line, which the overlay renders nil — SwiftPM caches a manifest by its contents plus its environment, never a file it reads (2026-10-15; `e38dfdc6`)

**Why:** thinking-release-deps.md §2/§5 — the ladder's third rung (RD-0…RD-4, then RD-6): the overlay that RD-1 and RD-2
built for npm, for the other two planes, so that a sibling whose cargo or Swift plane is released can be linked back
with one verb and the committed tree stays prod shape. Nothing flips to prod: ghosttea's fork line `10d0b17` is on no
remote (RD-4 §4, James's push) and truffle's Swift exact waits on G28, so both mechanisms are proved on stand-ins.

**What landed (`e38dfdc6`):**
- **Cargo.** A plane is released when the lock records `release.cargo` = `{ git, rev }`; `render --prod` writes its
  `[patch.crates-io]` rows as git rows. `use NAME` writes a generated, gitignored root `.cargo/config.toml` of
  absolute-path patches (cargo applies a config file's patch over the manifest's); one the verb did not write is
  refused, never overwritten or deleted. Stable cargo has no lockfile path of its own (`-Z lockfile-path` is nightly), so
  the path build rewrites the committed Cargo.lock: it is skip-worktree while the overlay stands, and `use --none`
  removes the config (and the `.cargo/` it made), clears the mark and restores the lock byte for byte.
- **Swift.** A plane is released when the lock records `release.swift`; `render --prod` writes
  `let <name>Release: Version? = nil | "<version>"` into the manifest, and `Package.swift`'s `truffleDependency` is the
  exact URL row when it carries a version and `.window/truffle` when it is nil (today: nil, so the committed shape
  resolves exactly as before). `use NAME` renders the SAME line nil in the working tree and `use --none` renders the
  lock's value back — a line rewrite, never a checkout, so another edit survives. The manifest stays VISIBLE as modified
  while the overlay stands (the PM's ruling); its Package.resolved, whose URL row the path package drops, is hidden by
  the lock rule.
- **The commit rule and preflight.** The pre-commit check refuses ANY commit while a lock is hidden, and a staged
  release line the lock does not render. Preflight names each state in its own words: a generated `.cargo/config.toml`
  with no overlay FAILs; a root `.cargo/config.toml` this repo did not write WARNs (gitignored, so `git status` will not
  show it); a hidden lock WARNs while its overlay stands and FAILs after; a manifest's release line is checked against
  the lock, or the overlay's nil; a released git + rev row is the render check's.
- `use` installs through pnpm only when the overlay's npm half changed, and its closing line names each half linked; the
  shape names the cargo rev only when it is not the checkout's own. CLAUDE.md's overlay paragraph gains both halves and
  `.window/truffle`'s role after G28 (flagged for James's review). `.gitignore` names `/.cargo/config.toml`.
- No interaction with the truffle bump (the History lead's EL8 lane): `truffle-core` is an exact registry row, not a
  patch.

**Validation (lane rd3; stand-ins on the throwaway branch `rd/3-spike`: ghosttea's cargo plane released as git + rev at
`10d0b17` through `file://`, truffle's Swift plane at `0.7.14`, unsatisfiable until G28 — its refusal is the witness):**
- Cargo: prod `cargo check -p field-native` rc 0 from `…/electron-ghostty?rev=10d0b17…`; `use ghosttea` → Cargo.lock
  `S`, `cargo check` rc 0 from the checkout with `git status` empty; a commit while hidden refused (`siblings:render
  FAIL: Cargo.lock is skip-worktree — an overlay is active …`); `use --none` → the lock `H`, `git status` empty, the git
  rev again. Repeated in the second window after the directory cleanup.
- Swift, through the real verbs in ONE environment (`xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies`): the exact row refused
  (`Dependencies could not be resolved because root depends on 'truffle' 0.7.14.`); `use truffle` → the line nil,
  Package.resolved `S`, `git status` exactly ` M apps/ios/VibeFieldKit/Package.swift`, preflight OK with its two words;
  the rendered nil line resolved (`Truffle: …/.window/truffle @ local`); a commit refused; `use --none` → the line
  `"0.7.14"`, `git diff` empty; the exact row refused again.
- The kit compile from a fresh derivedData: `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, 378 compile lines, `.window/truffle @ local`.
- `pnpm verify` EXIT 0 on `bee8bcab` (vitest 8,525 / 17 skipped, cargo 302 / 9 ignored, node --test 169/0) and on
  `020a0fac` before it; siblings-shape.test.mjs 17/17.
- **The landing gate:** `gate:landing --with-stages` on `86cc9b3b` (lane rd3, 09:05:39–09:36:40Z, the internal disk 15 → 14
  GiB free; `lanes/rd3/gate-86cc9b3b.log`, the gated sha kept in its name), 26 of 27 ok — verify's fourteen stages,
  `still`, and every smoke but smoke:canvas, smoke:bundled included. smoke:canvas (925 s) red on ONE row, DK-14's AIMED
  rung (`@'s list open with a pane to send to did not happen within 10000ms`) — main's own, word for word, as RD-1's and
  WP8's gates named it. **Landed as `e38dfdc6`, a tree-identical reword of the gated `86cc9b3b`: tree `2ccf6992`, diff
  empty, only the Tests line filled** (the placeholder was the builder's miss before the gate; the PM's ruling of 09:38Z
  makes it the rule — a reword after the gate lands only when tree-identical by tree hash, and the ledger names both).

**Found:**
- **SwiftPM's manifest cache eliminated the first build.** RD-3 first read a gitignored `.siblings-overlay` FILE beside
  the manifest (Xcode's GUI passes no shell environment). `swift package dump-package` read it in every mode, and
  `xcodebuild` ignored it. M1–M6 moved only the cache key: the file present, the same environment → the stale URL row;
  a never-seen variable → the path package; the file GONE, that variable again → the path package still (stale the other
  way); the manifest's own line → right both ways. The key is the manifest's contents plus its environment, never a file
  it reads (§3·A). The environment variant "worked" only because a new variable is a new key.
- **Kit builds and verify keep TMPDIR=/tmp; derived data and cargo targets go on the SSD** (the PM's house rule, from
  this window). With TMPDIR moved to the SSD for the full internal disk, the kit compile was red, rc 65:
  `metal: error: unable to make temporary file: Operation not permitted` in GhostteaKit's "Compile Ghosttea Metal shaders"
  CustomTask — SwiftPM's build-tool plugin sandbox lets `xcrun metal` write only under the system temp, even with
  `-skipPackagePluginValidation`. Green on `/tmp`. Written into docs/desk-gates.md's hygiene.
- **Preflight's third warning was the builder's bug, and taught a rule:** under a Swift-only overlay preflight warned
  `the dev overlay names truffle but .pnpmfile.cjs is missing` — the check assumed every overlay name has a released npm
  half. **An overlay name has up to three planes, and only a released plane has a half to check.** Fixed: the warning
  names only an overlay with a released npm plane (proved on the spike: exactly the two intended warnings).
- `xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies` with `-derivedDataPath` needs `-scheme` (rc 64, `The flag -scheme,
  -testProductsPath, or -xctestrun is required when specifying -derivedDataPath.`) — the first Swift pass was void on it.
- Package.resolved has Cargo.lock's hazard class once truffle's committed shape is a URL: built under the same rule,
  live only after G28.

**Owed:**
- RD-5 per sibling as RD-4's pipelines land (James's hands: `draft/handover/2026-10-15-rd4-james-pipelines.md`); the
  ghosttea fork's `release.cargo` once `10d0b17` is on its remote; truffle's `release.swift` at G28. Then RD-6.
- The Swift overlay in Xcode's GUI is a premise, not a witness — nothing here can drive the GUI.
- The spike's branch `rd/3-spike` stays in lane rd3 until the landing is read; nothing of it lands.

## WP12 L1 — the updater core: VibeField's UpdateProvider verifies the trust-root, the channel heads, the channel's policy and the feed before any download (TD-3's client half), channels resolve by signed heads, and the one verifier becomes a Node-only spine library, `@vibefield/trust` (2026-10-15; `dfc4b832` `9f9e4ec5` `0682ac15`)

**Why:** `specs/build-wp12-updater.md`, read and approved at the leans by the PM (09:58Z). It is L1 of four serial lanes:
WP12a (the shapes) + WP12b (the verifier and the controller core), with D3's spike first and D13's pins as one
deliberate commit. Before it, a packaged VibeField could not update: no electron-updater, no publish configuration,
no release workflow, and the tray's "Check for Updates…" rendered disabled.

**What landed:**
- **D13, the pins (`dfc4b832`).**
  - electron-builder `^26.0.12` (locked 26.15.3) → `26.15.7`, and electron-updater `6.8.9`, both exact (EDP-39).
  - `electron-builder.yml`'s `publish:` block names the frozen origin. It is REQUIRED: electron-updater reads
    `Resources/app-update.yml` for its cache dir name (`AppUpdater.js:545`) even with a custom provider, and
    electron-builder writes that file only with a publish provider configured. Nothing publishes from it.
  - The lock: `Packages: +8 -4`.
- **WP12a, the shapes and the one verifier (`9f9e4ec5`).** The contracts, all TS-only:
  - `ChannelHeads` (D4): a head of another channel's tag shape is refused.
  - `updatePolicyFile(channel)` (D5).
  - `UPDATES_SERVICE`: seven honest states, TD §4's four among them.
  - `UPDATES_AUDIT_ACTIONS`, which fieldd's `audit.append` now accepts.
  - `UpdateClientStateFile`.
  - `UpdateFloors`, the build-time floor: the staged identity's optional `updateFloors`, written by the stager from the
    embedded trust-root's version.
  - **D2, decided by the walls:** R2 forbids every `@vibefield/plugin-*` import under the shell's main, so the verifier
    moved to a new Node-only spine library, `packages/trust`. The kit re-exports it (one verifier). Walls R27/R28
    hold it.
- **WP12b, the updater core (`0682ac15`, `electron-shell/src/main/updates/`):**
  - **The verify chain:** §3's order. The policy is read from the NEWEST release (D5). Every document is judged against
    `max(remembered, build floor)`. Every accepted document is remembered even when a later step refuses.
  - **The custom provider:** as the D3 spike proved it.
  - **`decideUpdate`:** the one decision, renamed from EDP §11.1's `UpdatePolicy` (D14).
  - **The UpdateController:** single-flight; bounded codes; declines persisted; the off switch honored at every
    boundary; refusals become `UNAVAILABLE` plus a warn line plus an audit row; an unreadable state is moved aside
    loudly and the updater restarts from the build's floor; `doctorLines()`.
  - **Nothing installs:** `autoInstallOnAppQuit` is forced OFF, a staged update is HELD `apply-unbuilt`, and
    `restartToInstall` is honestly refused until WP12c.
  - **D9's dev-only fixture origin.**
  - **The tray:** `ready` → `staged`; with no apply, a staged update reads "Update Downloaded".
  - **Packaged-only wiring:** a manual check, one launch check after 30 s, and a stale-resume check.

**Validation:**
- **The D3 spike** (10:01–10:03Z): headless, against a loopback origin signed with dev keys. The custom-provider seam
  holds:
  - `getLatestVersion` runs once per check (`AppUpdater.js:389`, cached at :413, reused at :436);
  - the payload URLs come from our `resolveFiles` (`MacUpdater.js:53`);
  - no GitHub logic runs (`providerFactory.js:56-62`);
  - a forged feed is refused with zero payload requests (`ERR_VF_UPDATES_FEED_UNVERIFIED`);
  - a signed feed whose sha512 lies is refused by electron-updater's own check (`ERR_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH`).
- **`pnpm verify` EXIT 0** on the L1 tree (verify-3, 10:30:43–10:35:40Z): vitest 8,590 passed / 17 skipped / 0 failed
  (+65 over main), cargo 302 / 9 ignored, node --test 169/0. The walls' `--self-test` passed, including the R27/R28
  probes. The chain's tests name every refusal state; the controller's tests run over a fake updater that drives the
  real chain.
- **The landing gate:** `gate:landing --with-stages` on `0682ac15` (lane wp12, 10:37:55–11:08:57Z, the internal disk
  14 → 14 GiB free; `lanes/wp12/gate-0682ac15.log`), 26 of 27 ok — verify's fourteen stages, `still`, and every smoke
  but smoke:canvas, smoke:bundled included. smoke:canvas (923 s) red on ONE row, DK-14's AIMED rung (`@'s list open
  with a pane to send to did not happen within 10000ms`) — main's own, word for word. The gate armed on a still-held
  window seconds before the PM's grant; the PM let it stand (the same scope, nobody waiting), and two rules follow —
  the builder arms a gate only after the grant message, the PM flips PM-WINDOW to idle the moment a window's end is
  reported.

**Found:**
- **R2 decided D2 before any code ran.** `@vibefield/plugin-*` is walled out of the shell's main, so "the kit's
  `./trust` subpath" was never possible. The spine library is the shape, and the PM's condition held: the walls decide,
  then the spine library wins without asking.
- **electron-updater defaults `autoInstallOnAppQuit` to true.** An updater wired naively would install a staged update
  on any quit, past EDP-35's census gate. It is forced off until WP12c.
- **electron-updater turns `allowPrerelease` ON for a prerelease build** (`AppUpdater.js:218`, a nightly or a beta) and
  filters nothing by it after the provider returns. Channel selection must be ours (D4); the controller's tests keep
  the fact.
- **`app-update.yml` is load-bearing even with a custom provider** (the cache dir name). D13's `publish:` block is
  required, not cosmetic; W8 checks it on `package:dir`. *(Corrected 2026-10-15, WP12 L3a `3eb90abf`: not on `package:dir`
  — on darwin electron-builder writes `app-update.yml` only for a dmg or zip target (`PublishManager.js:77-80`), and
  `--dir` is neither. W8's clause is witnessed on a dmg/zip build; the release build job's assertion is L3b's.)*
- **The plan's §3 step 5 contradicted D5.** It read the policy from the head release; D5's whole point needs the newest
  release's copy. It was corrected at the source, dated.
- **The malformed-before-expired order:** a schema's refinement ("cannot expire before it was generated") speaks before
  the expiry clause. A test of expiry must build a WELL-FORMED expired document; verify-2's one red was the fixture's,
  not the code's.
- `AuditAppendV1` lives at `@vibefield/contracts/diagnostics`, not the contracts root (verify-1's one red).
- pnpm 11's `verify-deps-before-run` made a `pnpm exec biome` install the new workspace links: +22 lock lines, said.
- electron-updater's npm `latest` is 6.8.9, but its `v26` dist-tag carries 6.8.10 (2026-09-26). The pin stays EDP-39's.
- **Differential downloads fetch `<zip>.blockmap` from the same release.** The assembled file is still checked against
  the signed sha512, so blockmaps need no signature.

**Owed:**
- **L2 = WP12c.** Adoption after an update (D10: a production build identity, the bounded replace path, and the three
  fall-through spawns become refusals), D11's shutdown-before-swap, the apply gate (EDP-34/35), and the prepare-restart
  op with its Rust gen and both-side fixtures (moved from WP12a by the PM). This closes the debt row filed below.
- **L3 = WP12d + WP12e.** The policy's levers, the doctor surface that renders `doctorLines()`, per-channel policy
  sources (which raise the policy floors from null), the release workflow with the TD-3 `sign` step, and the asar
  allowlist audit (the second `sidecar-slim`).
- **L4 = WP12f.** The physical `smoke:update` against the fixture origin.
- **W10** (a real nightly: TD-3's gate) waits on TD-1, the tag rulesets and the first push. **W11** (the signed
  N-1 → N apply) waits on WP10.
- **Root-key rotation:** a rotated root is verified and judged but the adopted set is not persisted, so the next check
  judges from the embedded root again; WP12d persists it in the client state beside the policies.

## WP12 L2a — adoption after an app update: a packaged app adopts only its own build's fieldd and replaces any other, field-native's single-client rule the backstop; and the hello refuses with no server details until the credential is checked, on both daemons (2026-10-15; `2490459e`)

**Why:** after an app update, the shell could adopt the OLD fieldd. Production adoption checked only the user id and
the contracts major; `expectedBuildId` was dev-only. So the new app could keep running the old app's plugin roots and
trust anchor, which fieldd reads once at spawn. This is the debt row WP8 promised and L1 filed. The plan's D10 was
ruled by the PM on 2026-10-15 at 11:18Z. WP12c is split in two: **L2a is adoption**; L2b is the apply, as its own
landing with its own gate.

**What landed (`2490459e`, one commit):**
- **The build identity reaches production.**
  - `StagedReleaseIdentity.buildId` is optional, in ProductInfo's shape.
  - The stager stamps `<appVersion>+<commit7>` from git, and warns when it cannot.
  - `readBundledTrust` returns it.
  - A packaged shell passes it as `expectedBuildId` with `buildMismatch: "replace"`. Development keeps `refuse`.
- **The supervisor's replace path** (`fieldd-supervisor`):
  - The probe checks the USER before the build, so another user's daemon is never asked to stop.
  - On a different or null build, the probe returns the client our token authenticated.
  - `replaceStaleBuild` sends `system.shutdown` (bounded to 1.5 s), closes the client, and waits up to 3 s for the run
    file to go or change `bootId`. Then this build's fieldd is spawned either way.
  - A fieldd that does not stop is **superseded at field-native**: the single-client rule (`mgmt/mod.rs:578-585`)
    closes its API and it exits. **No signal is ever sent to a pid read from a file.**
  - `incompatible-contracts`, `user-mismatch` and `foreign-listener` keep spawning, as **named takeovers**
    (`fieldd.supervisor.takeover {probeFailure}`). The debt row's "three refusals" was ruled out: a refusal would let
    any same-uid listener stop the app's own fieldd (EL7 backwards).
  - The post-spawn poll never adopts the old build.
  - Four new lifecycle events: `replacing_build`, `replaced_build`, `replace_wait_expired`, `takeover`.
- **The hello order (EL7), both daemons.**
  - fieldd's contracts-major refusal stays first and now carries no details.
  - UA-2's user check moved AFTER the credential check. A refusal there withdraws the half-granted connection before
    the mismatch is said.
  - field-native gets the same reorder: `refuse_incompatible_major`, with no details.
- **The support bundle reports the running pair:** fieldd's recorded `buildId`, and field-native's `nativeBuild` from
  `system.health`. Both are bounded to 1 s ("unavailable" past that), replacing the two `app.getVersion()` stand-ins.

**Validation:**
- **The witness the debt row closes on**, a real field-native in the kill matrix: `✓ the kill matrix (NF-4, real field-native) > row WP12-D10: another build's fieldd is superseded at field-native; the PTY lives; the new build records itself  721ms` (verify-4).
  - fieldd A (`build-x`) serves a PTY. Fieldd B (`build-y`) boots while A still serves, with no stop asked, so the
    backstop is witnessed alone.
  - A reports `superseded` through `onFatal`, and product.json records `build-y` on B's port.
  - B lists the same PTY on the same native boot (equal UDS auth token), and terminates it.
- **`replace.test.ts`, 7 cases**, over the supervisor's fixtures:
  - replacing another build, and replacing a null build;
  - a stop that never comes: superseded, never signalled (the recorded pid is the test process itself);
  - the same build adopted, with nothing asked;
  - dev refusing;
  - the user checked first;
  - a foreign listener as a named takeover.
- **The hello order:** `user-hello.test.ts` +3 (unauthenticated wrong-user → `UNAUTHORIZED` with no server userId;
  authenticated → the mismatch with its details; a foreign major → no version and no user). Plus field-native's
  `a_major_refusal_before_the_credential_carries_no_server_details`.
- **`pnpm verify` EXIT 0** on the L2a tree (verify-4, 11:35:45–11:40:40Z): vitest 8,602 passed / 17 skipped / 0 failed
  (+12 over L1's 8,590), cargo 303 / 9 ignored (+1), node --test 169/0, gen:check fresh. One comment-only edit
  followed it (product-api.ts's doubled EL7 sentence), so the gate's stages are what verify the committed tree.
  Verify-1…3 were red on the lane's own (see Found).
- **The landing gate:** `gate:landing --with-stages` on `2490459e` (lane wp12-l2, 11:41:58–12:13:02Z, the internal disk
  14 → 14 GiB free; `lanes/wp12-l2/gate-2490459e.log`), 26 of 27 ok: verify's fourteen stages, `still`, and every
  smoke but smoke:canvas, smoke:bundled and smoke:godview included. smoke:canvas (922 s) was red on ONE row, DK-14's
  AIMED rung (`@'s list open with a pane to send to did not happen within 10000ms`), main's own word for word. Its
  red-path teardown has the same shape as L1's gate.

**Found:**
- **A refusal sent before the credential is checked must carry no server details.** fieldd told an unauthenticated
  local caller its userId (UA-2's check ran before the credential). Both daemons named their contracts version in the
  major refusal. No reader used either detail.
- **design-02's D10 lock file was never built.** fieldd has no single-instance lock. Field-native's single-client rule
  is the mechanism, and EDP §8.4 step 7 already held by it. The erratum is at design-02's D10 line, dated.
- **The supervisor checked the build before the user.** In replace mode that order would have asked another user's
  daemon to stop.
- An ambient `FIELDD_BUILD_ID` still reaches fieldd when the shell sets none: the supervisor spreads the caller's
  environment, which the shell defaults to `process.env` (a dev run outside the runner, or an older stage). Noted,
  unchanged.
- The three verify reds were all the lane's own:
  - an `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` test option (verify-1);
  - rustfmt breaking a call at `fn_call_width` (60), not at the 100-column line (verify-2);
  - fieldd's RPC error data nesting under `details` (verify-3).

**Owed:**
- **L2b = the apply:**
  - EDP-35's census veto at `before-quit` (`lifecycle.ts:81-82`); the quit flow can only delay, it has no reason;
  - EDP-34's safe window;
  - `restartToInstall` through the quit flow with a reason;
  - D11's shutdown-before-swap;
  - planes treated as native-touching until L3's signed planes;
  - the prepare-restart op with its Rust gen and both-side fixtures;
  - the tray's "Restart to Update".
- **L3, then L4** as filed in §WP12 L1. **W10 and W11** wait on James.

## WP12 L2b-i — the consented native stop: an update that touches field-native stops the floor only when fieldd's own live set is exactly the set the person consented to end; the floor records its restart intent and stops itself over the paired channel, and its next boot says the stop was planned (2026-10-15; `19cec349` `77e1401f`)

**Why:** `build-wp12-updater.md` §9 is L2b's reading. The PM ruled every lean at 12:15Z, R2's mechanism at 12:20Z and
R3's event at 12:22Z. Three facts drove it:
- `system.shutdown` stopped fieldd and LEFT field-native running, and nothing in production ever stopped field-native.
  After a swap, the new fieldd adopted the OLD floor (L2a's own kill-matrix row shows it), so old native bytes ran under
  the new app until a reboot. D11's "an old floor only ever outlives a release whose native binaries are byte-identical"
  was false.
- The session census is not "vacuous until agent sessions exist": `terminal.list` answers live PTYs today.
- The kill ladder has no pid for an ADOPTED floor (`native-supervisor.ts:45`), and the update path is the adopted case
  by construction.

design-00's EL1 carries the dated note: this is the ONE consented exception to the two-planes law. **L2b-ii, the shell
half, is a separate landing.**

**What landed:**
- **`19cec349` (test-only, the PM's ruling 12:47Z).** `agent-session.test.ts`'s `setup()` now waits for the floor's
  terminal endpoints, as `agent-gateway-floor.ts` has since `ec011806`. This is the 10-08 fix's second site. The race's
  sightings here: QL-D10's row at the MV landing (`8a851973`) and PJ-7's row in this lane's verify-2. It was on the
  History lead's debts list (`s-debts-fieldd.md` Appendix 3), which closes at this landing.
- **`77e1401f`, the consented native stop:**
  - **Contracts (EL9: both sides parse the fixtures).**
    - Management: `NativeRestartReason`, `NativePrepareRestartParams/Result` and `NativeShutdownParams/Result`. Their
      doc says the single-client rule IS their authorization, and that a superseded connection is refused with the
      existing `superseded` answer before any effect. Both are generated into Rust as named types.
    - `HelloAck.lastExit: NativeLastExit` (`planned | unplanned`).
    - The layout's `RESTART_INTENT_FILE` (`native/restart-intent.json`), with the vector updated.
    - TS-only: `UPDATE_PLANES`, `RestartScheduled` and `SystemShutdownParams/Result`.
  - **field-native.**
    - `restart.rs` writes the intent atomically and privately, then renames it into place. The boot TAKES it: present
      and well-formed reads `planned`; garbled, foreign or absent reads `unplanned`; a present file is always removed.
    - `native.lifecycle.prepareRestart` records the intent.
    - `native.lifecycle.shutdown` replies, then wakes **the third arm of main's `shutdown_signal()`**. That runs the same
      drain SIGTERM runs, so nothing new ends a session (row S2-B; `shutdown_sweeps_every_session_within_budget`).
    - The ack carries `lastExit`. The `native_build()` comment is corrected, dated.
  - **fieldd.**
    - **`NativeSupervisor.stopForUpdate()`** does everything in ONE function: suppress respawn → `prepareRestart` →
      `shutdown` → a bounded wait for the management socket to close → its own TERM→KILL ladder, only if this fieldd
      holds a pid and 5 s have passed. An adopted floor that doesn't close is reported `lingering`, never signalled.
    - **`TerminalService` closes to births for the census.** The live set is the observed inventory plus every session
      born and not yet observed (GT-1's race). Births in flight count. A refusal reopens births.
    - **`system.shutdown {native: {stop, sessions, toVersion?}}`** proceeds only on an exact match; otherwise it refuses
      `PRECONDITION_FAILED {live, births}` or `UNAVAILABLE {state: "unobserved"}`. On a match: `restartScheduled` is
      pushed on health, then the floor stops, then fieldd.
    - `FielddHealth` gains `nativeLastExit` and `restartScheduled`.

**Validation:**
- **The witnesses**, the kill matrix on a real field-native that fieldd ADOPTED (no pid: the socket closing is the
  witness):
  - `✓ the kill matrix (NF-4, real field-native) > row WP12-R2a: a consented stop ends exactly the consented set — the floor drains, records its intent, and the next boot says planned  1308ms` (verify-3) — consent names both PTYs; `native: "closed"`; **the floor exits 0 under the drain**; both PTY pids are gone;
    the intent is on disk; the next floor's fieldd reads `lastExit: "planned"` and the file is taken.
  - `✓ the kill matrix (NF-4, real field-native) > row WP12-R2b: a session born after consent refuses the stop — nothing ends, and births reopen  537ms` (verify-3) — consent names one PTY, then a second is born; **the refusal is `{live: [both], births: 0}`**; the floor still
    serves, both sessions are listed, the shutdown owner is never asked, and births reopen.
- **`native-stop-for-update.test.ts`, 6 cases:**
  - the adopted case: no pid, no ladder, the socket closing as the witness;
  - adopted-lingering, never signalled;
  - a spawned floor: TERM, then KILL;
  - TERM alone sufficing;
  - closing in time, with no signal at all;
  - a failed intent that still stops.
- **A terminal-service row:** a born-unseen session refuses a `[]` consent; a malformed ask refuses; an unobserved floor
  refuses.
- **field-native:**
  - `restart::tests` ×6;
  - `mgmt_server` ×3: a planned stop recorded, with the next boot saying `planned` ONCE; **a superseded client can
    neither record an intent nor stop the floor**; a malformed ask changes nothing;
  - `restart_verb_fixtures`.
- **`pnpm verify`** (verify-3, 12:47:21–12:52:16Z, on `19cec349` with the L2b-i tree uncommitted):
  - vitest 8,621 passed / 17 skipped / 0 failed (+19); cargo 313 / 9 ignored (+10); clippy and fmt clean.
  - gen:check was red only because the generated files were uncommitted. `pnpm gen:check` on the staged tree gave rc 0.
  - Verify-1 and verify-2 were red on the real-floor endpoint race, outside the diff: AR-7b's row, then PJ-7's.
- **The landing gate:** `gate:landing --with-stages` on `77e1401f` (lane wp12-l2b, 12:54:12–13:25:20Z, the internal disk
  14 → 14 GiB free; `lanes/wp12-l2b/gate-77e1401f.log`), 26 of 27 ok: verify's fourteen stages (test 120 s, test:rust
  82 s, gen:check on the committed tree), `still`, and every smoke but smoke:canvas, smoke:bundled and smoke:godview
  included. smoke:canvas (923 s) was red on ONE row, DK-14's AIMED rung (`@'s list open with a pane to send to did not
  happen within 10000ms`), main's own word for word, with the same red-path teardown shape as L1's and L2a's gates. The
  gate's stages are the verify on the final sha; the PM ruled a separate verify-4 would only repeat them (12:54Z).

**Found:**
- **A lane that changes generated files stages or commits them before verify, or gen:check reds by construction (it
  diffs the index).** This is now a house rule (the PM, 12:54Z), in `docs/desk-gates.md` beside the TMPDIR bullet.
- **The kill ladder has no pid for an adopted floor.** The update path is the adopted case by construction, and on
  Windows a signal is a hard kill. Hence the verb, with the single-client rule as its whole authorization.
- **The old `killLadder` skips its KILL rung once `stopped` is set,** so the stop carries its own ladder.
- **A naive census misses a session `create` answered before the inventory listed it.** The consent check counts births
  that are born but unseen, and births in flight.
- **R3's event as first leaned had no carrier.** fieldd sends no free-standing product notifications, and
  `system.health.subscribe` is local-only (D36). Peers read a native-touching stop as `asleep` today, because the node
  goes down with the floor. The local half is `FielddHealth.restartScheduled`; the phone/peer half is owed (below).

## WP12 L2b-ii — the apply: "Restart to Update" takes one census, asks consent in EDP-35's words, durable-closes, holds fieldd and stops the pair, and only then stages Squirrel and installs; from the stop on nothing may start a daemon and every branch exits — WP12c complete on macOS (2026-10-15; `60e7c264` `4b6f4ab4`)

**Why:** `build-wp12-updater.md` §10 is L2b-ii's reading. The PM ruled S1–S7 at 13:31Z. The lane's reading then changed
the plan three times:
- **R4 reversed (13:36Z).** Electron's own docs say "a successfully downloaded update will always be applied the next
  time the application starts" (`electron.d.ts:2103-2104`). So "Squirrel first" would have armed an install that every
  later refusal could no longer stop. **Order (A):** Squirrel is staged only after the daemons stopped.
- **S4 rewritten (13:37–13:40Z).** After the stop the flow never restores; it always exits.
- **The coordinator hold.** Without it, the update's own stop would have respawned the pair.

**What landed:**
- **`60e7c264` (test-only).** Kill-matrix row WP12-R2b polls the inventory for the late session. Its one-shot read raced
  GT-1's lag, the lag the census itself closes.
- **`4b6f4ab4`, the apply. `restartToInstall()` over an `ApplyPort`:**
  - (1) ONE census snapshot: `terminal.list`, bounded to 2 s; unknown holds.
  - (2) The consent box when sessions live: "Updating ends N terminal sessions", the sessions as `title — cwd`,
    "Cancel" (the default) and "End N sessions and update". Cancel holds.
  - Then the `app.update.apply` ATTEMPT row through fieldd while it lives.
  - (3) The quit flow's update mode: `before-quit`'s durable close (fieldd alive) → **hold fieldd** → its consented stop
    with the snapshot's ids, byte for byte. A refusal aborts: nothing stopped, the window reopens.
  - (4) Squirrel's staging (120 s).
  - (5) `quitAndInstall()`; only Electron's own quit, which follows it, exits.
- **After the stop, every branch exits:**
  - a Squirrel refusal (nothing armed) → relaunch;
  - a timeout or a failed install (Squirrel may have armed) → a message box in DESIGN.md §9's voice, auto-closing at
    60 s, then exit WITHOUT relaunch.
  - `lastApply` names the branch, synchronously, before every exit. Its outcome row reaches the ledger at the next
    launch, once.
- **The supporting pieces:**
  - `FielddHandleCoordinator.holdForUpdate()`;
  - QuitFlow's `armUpdate`, with an install watchdog;
  - the lifecycle's `resetAfterAbortedQuit()` and the registry's `cancelShutdown()`;
  - the tray's census-aware verb, re-read every 60 s while staged;
  - EDP-34's `safeWindow()` with its four named clauses, named in doctor;
  - the contracts: `apply-refused`, `census-unknown`, `app.update.apply`, `UpdateLastApply`.
- macOS only; elsewhere the update stays `apply-unbuilt`, and doctor says so.

**Validation:**
- **The no-spawn probes:**
  - `fieldd-recovery.test.ts`: held, a closed client attempts no upstream `ensure()`, and `ensure()` refuses.
  - `controller-apply.test.ts`: in every post-stop branch (installed, refused, timeout, stalled), nothing reaches fieldd
    after the stop.
- **The aborted update quit** (`lifecycle.test.ts`): after the close, a window reopens and an ordinary quit
  durable-closes and exits. A control without the reset shows the stale replay flag skipping the close.
- **QuitFlow's update mode** (`quit-flow.test.ts`): every branch, re-entry, and an ordinary quit untouched.
- **The words** (`apply.test.ts`): pinned to DESIGN.md §9 (sentence case, buttons that say what they do, numbers, no
  apology), with the tray's labels and the predicate's table.
- **`pnpm verify` EXIT 0** (verify-2, 13:53:54–13:58:53Z, on `60e7c264` with the L2b-ii tree): vitest 8,674 passed / 17
  skipped / 0 failed (+72 over main's 8,602), cargo 313 / 9 ignored, node --test 169/0, gen:check fresh. Verify-1 was
  red on ONE row, the landed WP12-R2b's one-shot inventory read, which `60e7c264` fixes.
- **The landing gate:** `gate:landing --with-stages` on `4b6f4ab4` (lane wp12-l2c, 13:59:46–14:31:03Z, the internal disk
  14 → 14 GiB free; `lanes/wp12-l2c/gate-4b6f4ab4.log`), 26 of 27 ok: verify's fourteen stages (test 123 s, test:rust
  83 s, gen:check), `still`, and every smoke but smoke:canvas, smoke:bundled and smoke:godview included. smoke:canvas

  10000ms`), main's own word for word, with the same teardown shape as the last three gates.

**Found:**
- **The handle coordinator auto-recovers a closed fieldd client by `ensure()`, so without `holdForUpdate()` the update's
  own stop would have respawned the pair under a possibly armed install with no caller asking.** The hold makes the
  no-spawn rule structural (`fieldd-handle-coordinator.ts:73-99`).
- **After the daemon stop, nothing may call `ensureFieldd()`, which spawns; the audit's outcome waits for the next
  launch.** The shell's audit row travels through fieldd (wall R17).
- **An irreversible step goes after the last refusal, never before it.** R4 was reversed on `electron.d.ts:2103-2104`.
- **Two EDP sentences were wrong for a native-touching apply, and are corrected at source, dated:** EDP-38's "updater
  failure is shell-local by construction" and EDP §8.4 step 5's "a failed shell swap leaves the running daemons
  untouched". A reader of the old spec would build the wrong thing: restoring the pair after a Squirrel failure, under an
  install that may be armed. The rule now reads: after the stop every branch exits, so there is never a running shell
  over a stopped floor.
- **`willQuit`'s later calls only defer.** So an update without the mode would have exited before ShipIt took over.
- **An update quit aborted after `before-quit` leaves the registry shut and the replay flags set.** Both need an undo.
- **A row that reads the inventory right after a birth must poll:** the inventory is observed, and lags (`60e7c264`).
  Main's WP12-R2b was a flake at this rate, and this landing closes it.

## WP12 L3a — the release workflow: plan → verify → build → sign → converge → publish, its permissions table held by a test; electron-builder never publishes, nothing update-visible goes out unsigned, and the asar carries no dependency (2026-10-15; `3eb90abf`)

**The honest limit, first:** the workflow cannot run on this Mac. Its witnesses are:
- its scripts' tests;
- a workflow lint (actionlint, plus a structure test);
- a CI emulation run here.

Its first real run is James's (J3). Like `verify.yml`, it is red until the sibling pins are on their remotes, because CI
clones every sibling from its remote.

**Why:** `build-wp12-updater.md` §11 is L3's reading; the PM ruled the split (L3a → L3b → L3c) at 14:36Z and the
permissions table at 14:47Z. The 14:36Z "secrets in the sign job alone" could not hold, because the stage signs the
bundled index inside the bundle (EDP §12.1's own list) and WP10's Apple step joins the build job. So the table has two
jobs in the one `release-signing` environment, each secret scoped to its one step.

**What landed (`3eb90abf`):**
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`.**
  - Triggers: a schedule and a dispatch make a nightly, skipped when main is red, unchanged, or already released today
    (a tag name is used once, D7); a `v*` tag makes a beta or a stable at the committed version.
  - verify is `verify.yml`, called. Its concurrency group now names the running workflow, so a push's verify cannot
    cancel the release's gate.
  - build is cache-free and runs `cargo build --release --locked -p field-native` first. It packages signed when J4's
    credentials exist, and UNSIGNED otherwise, said in a warning; then come the asar allowlist (D12) and the plane
    hashes (D11).
  - sign installs zod alone, with no lifecycle scripts. It carries D4/D5 from the newest SIGNED release and compares
    `touched` with the newest release of the same channel, failing loudly on a failed download. Then it signs, with the
    release secret in that step alone, and verifies with the client's own chain.
  - converge verifies again, checks the zip's nested signatures with codesign (once the build is signed), and writes
    SHA256SUMS.
  - publish runs §12.4's draft transaction: metadata last, the assets compared on the draft, then the un-draft. Nightly
    retention keeps the newest nightly and never deletes a tag.
- **Five scripts** (`release-plan`, `release-manifest`, `release-sign`, `release-verify`, `audit-asar`).
- **Contracts:** `UpdatePolicySource` and `ReleaseManifest`.
- **The committed policy sources** in `apps/desktop/packaging/policy/`.
- **Every third-party action SHA-pinned** (24 refs), with Dependabot proposing the next SHA.

| job | environment | permissions | secrets (step-scoped) |
|---|---|---|---|
| plan | — | contents: read, actions: read | none |
| verify | — | contents: read | none (`verify.yml`, called) |
| build | release-signing | contents: read | `VIBEFIELD_BUNDLED_INDEX_SECRET` in the stage step; the Apple credentials in the signed-package step |
| sign | release-signing | contents: read | `VIBEFIELD_RELEASE_SECRET` in the sign step |
| converge | — | contents: read | none |
| publish | — | contents: write | none (GITHUB_TOKEN only) |

**Found:**
- **electron-builder publishes IMPLICITLY under CI or a git tag.** Given no `--publish`, it chooses `onTag` or
  `onTagOrDraft` (app-builder-lib 26.15.7 `out/publish/PublishManager.js:46-60`). On a `v*` push that would have
  published a draft from a build nobody signed. `run-electron-builder.mjs` now passes `--publish never` on every build
  and refuses any other value; electron-builder.yml carries the correction.
- **A committed source under an output directory never reaches CI.** The policy sources were first written under
  `apps/desktop/release/`, electron-builder's output dir, which `.gitignore:46` ignores. The witness is the CI
  emulation (a copy of the tracked tree, no siblings, zod alone), whose sign step failed ENOENT. The sources now live in
  `apps/desktop/packaging/policy/`, with a correction on D5.
- **The dependency collector widens the asar.** electron-builder searches apps/desktop too (`appFileCopier.js:236`)
  and counts `optionalDependencies` as production (`nodeModulesCollector.js:169`). `audit-asar` found the same three
  `node_modules/@vibecook/truffle-sidecar-darwin-arm64` paths in the builds of 08-16 and 10-14: a second signed
  `sidecar-slim` inside the archive. `files` gains `"!**/node_modules/**"`. Measured on electron-builder 26.15.7, on one stage, with one variable: without the negation, three paths and a 67-file asar with 3 UNPACKED, which puts the second `sidecar-slim` on disk at `Resources/app.asar.unpacked/node_modules/@vibecook/truffle-sidecar-darwin-arm64/bin/` beside the real `Resources/bin/sidecar-slim`; with it, zero paths and a 64-file asar with 0 unpacked (14,660,408 bytes), one `sidecar-slim` at `Resources/bin`, and `package:dir`, `audit-asar` and the fuses audit green (9 fuses).
- **The stage does not build field-native** (it names the command); the release builds it, locked.
- **W8's `app-update.yml` clause could never pass on `package:dir`.** On darwin, electron-builder writes
  `Resources/app-update.yml` only for a dmg or zip target (`PublishManager.js:77-80`), and the D12 build has none. The
  claim is corrected at its sources (the plan's W8 row and §3, and L1's entry above). The PM ruled (a) at 15:19Z: the
  release build job's assertion and its local zip witness are L3b's. `--publish never` leaves the file written.

**Validation:**
- `pnpm verify` EXIT 0 (verify-3, 15:12:32–15:17:34Z): TS 690 files / 8,698 tests; Rust 23 suites / 313; gen:check clean. verify-1 was red on a typecheck in the new test (fixed); verify-2 on AR-6-0's interrupt poll, the 10-14 lottery (green in verify-3, 7,381 ms).

The other is `test`: main's latent 1 ms race in `index-activity-doors.test.ts:548`, where `day()` reads `Date.now()` twice, so a tick between the reads makes the window DAY + 1 ms and the contracts refuse it (`untilMs - sinceMs <= INDEX_ACTIVITY.MAX_WINDOW_MS`; TL `3de3706a`, 10-09). It surfaced under load 112. The file alone is green (20/20, 12.17 s, load 2.77). The one-line fix, `const day = () => { const now = Date.now(); return { sinceMs: now - DAY, untilMs: now }; };`, is L3b's FIRST commit, test-only (the PM, 15:52Z). df 14 → 14 GiB internal, 419 → 419 GiB SSD.

## WP12 L4 — `pnpm smoke:update`: a DEV-keyed packaged app against a loopback fixture origin, five runs judged from outside the process, and W8's remainder on the zip a person downloads (2026-10-17; `18aa2a25`)

**Why:** `build-wp12-updater.md` §4 WP12f and §14, ruled by the PM on 2026-10-15 at 21:41Z:
- R1: the stage's DEV-only `--dev-trust-root`;
- R4: the staged line;
- R6: the apply stays W11;
- R7: a landing-only row 30.

The leans stood for the rest: R2, the zip; R3, no knob; R5, every run inside its temp root. Built during James's focus
session, run after it. WP12's DEV-provable half is complete.

**What landed (`18aa2a25`):**
- **The fixture origin:** `apps/desktop/packaging/update-fixture.mjs`.
  - The run's keys are minted in memory, and its trust-root is root-signed (public).
  - Release trees are signed by `release-sign`'s own `signRelease`; `latest-mac.yml` names a random payload by its sha512.
  - A loopback server in GitHub's shape counts every request.
- **The smoke:** `apps/desktop/packaging/run-update-smoke.mjs`.
  - It builds the zip a person downloads, staged on the run's trust-root, and runs W8's audits on that app.
  - Each of the five runs gets an unzipped copy inside its own root (`HOME`, `FIELDD_DATA_DIR`, `--user-data-dir`).
  - It judges from outside the process: the desktop log, the fixture's requests, and electron-updater's cache.
- **R1:** `bundled-plugins.mjs` `--dev-trust-root`, with the bundled key in `VIBEFIELD_SMOKE_BUNDLED_SECRET`, in the
  stager's environment only. A release stage (`VIBEFIELD_BUNDLED_INDEX_SECRET` set) refuses it. The stage report reads
  "KEY CLASS: DEV, smoke trust-root".
- **R4:** the controller logs `desktop.update.staged {version, sha512}`, the sha512 being the verified feed's.
- **The reaper** (`smoke-daemons.mjs`) names the packaged layout.
- **desk-gates:** row 30 and its doors.

**Found:**
- **A staged update left no trace outside the process** (R4). No log line said "staged", and the state file holds no
  state kind. A support bundle or a person reading the log could not tell a downloaded update from none. Closed by
  `desktop.update.staged`.
- **The existing `VIBEFIELD_BUNDLED_INDEX_SECRET` could not carry the smoke's bundled key: it IS the stager's release
  switch** (`keyClass = secret ? "release" : "dev"`). The smoke's key has a DEV-only env of its own, and that switch's
  presence refuses `--dev-trust-root`.
- **A reaper keyed on dev process names misses a packaged layout.** `smoke-daemons.mjs` knew `Electron Helper` and

## TM/DS — the terminal doors publish after a fresh pair start: the serve drivers declare again when the mesh node comes up and record a serve the node reports live, and the floor's serve stream subscribes before it snapshots (2026-10-17; `6521616f` `b7de8660`)

**What James saw:** twice after a fresh pair start (10-16 23:56Z, 10-17 00:33Z) the phone read "not publishing its
terminal doors" until fieldd alone was restarted. Both boots logged `RpcCallError: mesh node not up` at fieldd's start and
`mesh.node_ready` about a second later.

**Found** (`draft/handover/2026-10-17-focus-audit.md` §3), three candidates, two convicted:
- **(a) convicted by a mock row** that failed on `b5de2156`: a declaration the node refused while it was still coming up
  (the declare closure's `removeServe` answered UNAVAILABLE, so it returned before `lastTerminalServeSpec` was set) was
  never declared again. Nothing told the route drivers the node had come up; ArtifactService's maintenance reconcile is
  why the product serve recovered and the terminal one did not.
- **(c) convicted by the code:** `native.mesh.serve.subscribe` took the snapshot, sent it, and then spawned a forwarder
  that subscribed INSIDE its own task (`mgmt/mesh.rs:1464`). A proxy that started between the two was never reported, so
  fieldd's fused view stayed at `starting` and the serve was never published.
- **(b) open:** the live boots also show a post-ready removal reaching the sidecar (NOT_FOUND, 6 ms after
  `mesh.node_ready`); whether it cost the declaration cannot be read from info-level logs. The two warn lines below make
  the next one readable.

**Fix:**
- `6521616f` (fieldd), one mechanism for both drivers:
  - `MeshClient.noteNodeState`, fed from the floor's own health stream (`meshNodeUp`: the `mesh-gateway` unit at `up`,
    tolerant of a floor that sends no units). On a turn to up it re-places the desired set and emits `node-up`.
  - The terminal and index route drivers refresh on `node-up`.
  - `RouteServeDriver` records a serve the node reports LIVE at its signature instead of declaring it again — F-M5's
    other half: a remove-then-add would drop every connection on the listener.
  - The deferred lines (the driver's `declare_deferred`, both closures' `remove_deferred`) are at WARN.
- `b7de8660` (field-native): the serve stream subscribes before it snapshots and hands the receiver to the forwarder; an
  event from before the snapshot replays after it, and the client merges by `serveId`.

**Tests:** terminal-serve.test.ts "a declaration refused while the mesh node was down lands when the node comes up — and
nothing else changed" (red on `b5de2156`); mesh-client.test.ts "a turn to UP re-places the desired set and says node-up
once" and `meshNodeUp`'s reading; route-serve.test.ts "records a serve the node now reports live …" and its converse.
fieldd's full suite 2282 passed / 29 skipped (185 files); field-native 313 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored across 23
binaries in its own target; tsc, biome, rustfmt and clippy `-D warnings` clean.

## DS/GT — the ghosttea pin moves to `feat/geometry-take` on `10d0b17`: the desktop takes the seat back (on a focus gain, and on a press of a pane that has focus) and its wheel reaches a program that tracks the mouse; the deck's cast is retired (2026-10-17; `c5c59813`; ghosttea `218e11f`, EL8)

**What James saw:** once the phone attached, "desktop never gets back resize control, no matter how i click or input"
(03:36Z, and again at 04:00Z with the phone's seat fixes installed), and the desktop pane could not scroll codex (10-16,
again 04:00Z).

**Causes:**
- The seat (the audit's §1a): the pinned ghosttea-react predated `takeGeometryOnFocus`, so the deck's prop rode a cast
  that did nothing and the desktop never took the seat. The branch that adds it takes only on a focus GAIN, and a phone's
  take moves no focus on the desktop — its window and pane keep it — so pinning the branch as it stood would not have
  fixed James's case.
- The wheel (the audit's D0): a routed frame goes from its frames leg straight to the render worker; only the legacy
  bridge read mouse modes, from frame headers on the main thread. `isMouseTracking` stayed false for every routed
  session, so the wheel became a local scroll, which the engine turns into arrow keys on codex's alternate screen.

**The pin, one EL8 event** — ghosttea `feat/geometry-take-on-pin` (James's `feat/geometry-take` untouched):
- feat/geometry-take's eight commits cherry-picked onto the pin `10d0b17` (`aa4f762`→`8b83f50`, `83b8e04`→`aaac935`,
  `d952944`→`619e8fa`, `a24a28d`→`70d6dbd`, `4027551`→`3337654`, `d613e50`→`b311d3e`, `5c9b533`→`569daaa`,
  `13103a3`→`280dbe1`), one conflict in `routed-control.ts` (the pin's `replacements` map beside `aa4f762`'s retyped
  `pendingGeometry`; both kept);
- `42a61ed`: the worker says a routed session's mouse modes (`terminal-modes`) when a committed frame changes them,
  again after a re-attach; the runtime takes them through the legacy path's one setter;
- `218e11f`: a press of a pane that already has focus takes, under the focus gain's own policy (opted in, controls
  resize, takes input; a mirror never does) — so a press takes exactly once either way.
- React only: nothing under `native/` moved, so the six cargo patches compile the same sources.
- VibeField: the lock's one sha line (`siblings:pin` typechecked the 27 consumer projects green; its serializer's
  re-escape of the file was not kept); `takeGeometryOnFocus` is a real prop on the deck, the cast and its note gone.

**Erratum (mine, before anything consumed it):** `42a61ed` was first committed as `b8663ff` with a message claiming
`tsc --noEmit` clean. That run never happened: a lane's ghosttea root has no `tsc` (install-js skips the workspace root;
TypeScript is per package), and the `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'` timeout wrapper exits 0 when its exec fails. The
package's own tsc (TypeScript 7.0.2) then ran — a planted type error turns it red — and the message was amended before
the pin recorded it. A timeout wrapper must `exec(@ARGV) or exit 127`, and a claimed run needs the tool's own line.

**Checks:** ghosttea-react at `218e11f` — tsc `--noEmit` exit 0, vitest 41 files / 341 tests, prettier 3.9.5 `--check`
clean on the changed files; preflight OK (one warning, rosettad freshness, from before); biome; field-app typecheck;
godview-deck.test.tsx 72/72.

**Validation:** the stack's one gate, in the entry above — 24/27; `test` the Nx output cap, read alone green; the two
desk smokes red under the LOCKED screen on main's own words, their second samples OWED before the freeway branch lands.
The pin's own witnesses are green: `smoke:godview`, `smoke:terminal-door`, `smoke:terminal-direct`. ~~**The pin is on an
UNPUSHED branch** — ghosttea `feat/geometry-take-on-pin` at `218e11f` is local to this Mac — so CI's sibling fetch is
red until James pushes it.~~ *Corrected 2026-10-21: `218e11f` is on ghosttea's `origin/feat/geometry-take-on-pin`
(VF-PM's check, 20:32Z, `git branch -r --contains`). CI's `verify` on main `984e9ea15` reached clippy, so its preflight
passed with all five siblings at their pins.*

**Owed:**
- ~~James pushes ghosttea: `feat/geometry-take-on-pin` is local, so CI's sibling fetch of `218e11f` is red until it is on
  the remote.~~ *Paid by 2026-10-21 (the check above).* His `../ghosttea-0.11.2` has the new branch checked out at

- The desktop witness on his machine: the phone takes the seat; a press of the deck's pane takes it back (the PTY is the

## smoke:canvas's aimed draft calls the terminals up first — DK-14's AIMED row was main's own red from W7 to here, never a flake (2026-10-17; `c524837d5`, test-only, through lane mvland (`mv/canvas-aimed`) on `e1bc6111`)

**Why:** DK-14's AIMED row checks that a draft already aimed takes the chip with no @, and that send arms. It went red
in every smoke:canvas from 10-12 on: PORTALS' PT-5c2, 5d, 6a and 6b gates, the dui lane, and RD-5a's landing gate on 10-14
("DK-14: @'s list open with a pane to send to did not happen within 10000ms"). It was carried as a flake that a rerun
passes, but it never passed: **main's smoke:canvas was red from W7 (`42f8d5b6`, 10-12) to this landing.** land3's
landing gate ran verify, smoke and smoke:godview only, so main never ran smoke:canvas in that time. W7's entry carries the
History lead's correction, and ROADMAP's law is now the whole list at every landing. PORTALS named the cause on 10-12, and
the PM gave the row to the MV lead on 10-14. **James's ruling:** "Fast-forward now" (asked 2026-10-14 19:51Z, answered
2026-10-17 15:57Z; main had moved on, so it lands rebased).

**The cause** (read from the code and the logs, then measured on main): W7 opens a launch with the terminals away and
the deck uncalled (`GodviewOverlay`'s `called`). So there is no workspace and no shell. On Canvas the line's door then lends
no pane, and @'s Send to says "No panes open yet" (`at-list.ts`). The product is right: a person who has called no
terminal has no pane to send to. The row's precondition ("the pane the deck shows") is what had gone stale: before W7, the
deck birthed a shell at every launch. Only smoke:godview called the terminals up, through the Godview markers' lab seam
(`window.__vfGodviewDeck.up()`).

**What landed** (`c524837d5`; no product file):
- `testing/smoke.ts` loads the canvas run with `godviewMarkers: "1"`, for the lab seam alone. The markers add console lines
  and the deck wrapper's witness; the canvas run reads neither.
- `testing/smoke-send-to.ts`: the AIMED row calls the terminals up first (`askGodviewDeckUp`, the helper smoke:godview's
  rows share), as a person's first call would.
  - Since LR, the called deck asks the last run's question itself (`last-run.ts`). A fresh smoke profile left nothing, so it
    answers start clean at once and the deck births its opening shell, the pane the row aims at.
  - The bound is 20 s instead of 10, because it now counts that birth.
  - A failure names what the deck ask did (`sayingDeckAsk`) and Send to's own words.
  - `SMOKE_CANVAS_SEND_AIMED` records `paneMs`, and the file's header names the row and its precondition.

**Validation:** this is a test-only change over a gated main (`e1bc6111`: one stack gate 24/27 under a LOCKED screen, the
desk smokes' second samples owed), so its evidence is verify plus the row's own smoke. The logs are in
`lanes/mvland/logs/c524837d5/`.
- `pnpm verify` on `c524837d5`: EXIT 0, 16:03–16:09Z, no failed test. field-native was built from the lane into its own
  target (`/Volumes/SamsungRed/rust/mvland`).
- **smoke:canvas alone, on the shown window, with James's leave:** ok, EXIT 0, 16:14:54–16:29:57Z (903 s). Load was 9/36/37
  at the start and 9 at the rows that record it.
  - All 99 row lines passed. AIMED aimed at the opening shell 88 ms after the call; the draft read "Clock ", send armed,

  - The HAND bars came back in 218–235 ms, inside the bound: main's known ~250 ms class did not occur.

  - This run also discharges `e1bc6111`'s owed smoke:canvas sample.

  - gate:landing 12/12 on the exact tree, and smoke:canvas 2/2 (the pane in 138 and 141 ms).

## TP-S3d — an activation's own catch-up is not background to its own deltas: the frames writer reorders only across activations, and a phone card closed and reopened keeps its scene (2026-10-17; `0e15237a` `d609aa90`)

**What James saw:** "as long as i slide to close it and then tap bubble to bring it up, the scroll just broke and froze,
can tap either" (05:42Z, on the dev build carrying the seat and swipe fixes). A first attach scrolled; a close and
reopen froze the picture and held every swipe and tap.

**Cause (the focus audit's C1 — named at 02:29Z, convicted at 06:24Z):**
- A reopen declares demand none → live. The pump repairs that lineage break with a CATCH-UP transfer (base = the
  revision it last sent, result = a forced full frame), queued as `Outbound::Bulk`, and its next deltas as urgent
  `Outbound::Binary`.
- The frames writer's `pick_next` drained the urgent lane before ANY bulk — for all activations — so codex's next delta
  (it redraws on the reopen's keyboard and resize) overtook its OWN activation's catch-up on the wire.
- The worker reads `activationSequence` as what §5 says it is, "only a correctness check on an ordered socket": every
  unit of the overtaken catch-up arrived behind a later one and was dropped without a trace. The scene stayed on the
  base the catch-up was to replace, every later delta named a base the sink never held, and nothing repairs a lineage
  break (the audit's D2/C6) — so it stayed frozen, input held, for good.
- TP-S3d's own words were "a background transfer yields to an urgent incremental": another activation's, never the
  delta's own base.

**The fix (`0e15237a`, field-native's `tp` — the `field-terminal-host` cell):** `Outbound::Binary(bytes,
Option<Arc<str>>)` and `Outbound::Bulk(bytes, Arc<str>)` name their activation (the pump tags both; the calibration echo
is `None`). The writer's `Lanes` record each unit's arrival order; an urgent unit waits only while a bulk unit of its OWN
activation that arrived before it is still queued, and that bulk unit goes first. Other activations' urgent units, and
units of no activation, still pass every bulk unit — the bulk-induced-HOL floor holds for them — and a delta queued
BEFORE its activation's catch-up still goes first.

**The kit (`d609aa90`, diagnostics):** the phone's sequence check says what it drops — "frames: unit #N (kind) dropped —
#M of its activation arrived first". The drop is unchanged.

Both were rebased from `0fc42241` `49a9f8fa` onto `003cec64` before the gate; `git diff 49a9f8fa d609aa90 -- apps/ios
packages/field-native` is empty, so the checks and the witness below were made on the same cell and kit.

**How it was found:** dev phone builds from focus/freeway carrying uncommitted diagnostics (exact input-gate reasons,
the cell's presentation/input changes, the sink's refusal runs with their stamps, each transfer's begin and outcome):
- console 13 (06:13Z): after a reopen "a delta did not fit the scene held"; the drop line "input is held: the picture
  is seeding — the sink holds a different scene";
- console 14 (06:24Z): "refused 1 in a row — a delta on r3798 where the scene holds r3797 (renderer: 0 stale, 0 full
  refreshes asked)", and no catch-up begin anywhere in the run;
- the mechanism's second witness, the same build (06:36Z): a reopen while codex was quiet logged "a catchup of 37322
  bytes begins, on r4012 to r4014" → "a frame applied after 214 refused" and the stuck scene recovered; the next reopen
  froze again ("a delta on r4025 where the scene holds r4018", no begin).

**Erratum (mine, corrected to James at 05:56Z before anything consumed it):** at 05:46Z I told James the touch takes
caused it ("each committed take re-seeded the view, and input was held through every re-seed"). ghosttea applies a
resize only `if prepared.size_changed()` (`native/ghosttea/src/session.rs`) and the cell's commit only bumps the lease
revision (`tp/activation.rs` `geometry_finalize`); the engage skip built on the claim was reverted, never committed.

**Checks:** `cargo fmt -p field-native --check` 0 · `cargo clippy -p field-native --all-targets -- -D warnings` 0 ·
`cargo test -p field-native --lib` 174 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (armed 06:38:31Z at 1-min load 9.19, the lane's own
target) · the mutation probe: with the hold switched off the new row `an_activations_delta_never_overtakes_its_own_queued_transfer`
FAILS with the old order (the delta first), `door.rs` restored blob-identical (`dee36d0d`; 06:40:23Z at 9.36) · TP-S3d's
row moved to `Lanes`, meaning unchanged · the kit, built and run whole on this branch: 1121 tests in 213 suites, 12 runs
passed, 0 failed, 0 restarts (07:42:56Z at 9.80).

**Validation:**
- **Before / after, on James's floor** (his word 06:42Z; `pnpm dev` from this lane on his own dev root, the cell
  confirmed by `nm` as the fixed `field-terminal-host`): BEFORE, 2 of 3 reopens froze (console 14: r3798/r3797 and
  r4025/r4018; the third, with codex quiet, recovered through its catch-up); AFTER, 0 of 3 (console 16, 06:59–07:00Z:
  2 seeds and 3 reopen catch-ups on the glass, 0 refusals, 0 dropped units, no lag flapping).
- **The gate:** `pnpm gate:landing --with-stages` on `d609aa90` in `/Volumes/SamsungRed/focus-tp` (its own cargo
  target, `TMPDIR=/tmp`), armed 16:58:22Z at load 4.76/15.23/17.18 with James's lane dev app stopped at his word (16:51Z,
  relayed by VF-PM), ended 17:31:50Z: **24/27**.
  - Green: preflight, check:walls, check:retired, check:ios-fixtures, icons:check · typecheck 74 s · lint · fmt ·
    lint:rust 26 s · bundle:assert · `test` 193 s (load 10→124) · `test:rust` 95 s · gen:check · still · smoke ·

## GV-D4 re-ruled — a session opens in the focused pane: every pane is an observer, and a session another pane shows is mirrored there (2026-10-19; `43b048b70`, lane `focus/fix-pane-observe`, sha unchanged)

**What James asked (2026-10-18 22:30Z):** "when i select a pane, and then click on any bubble, it should actually attach
the clicked bubble to this terminal pane, because the meaning behind this action is that each pane is an window/observer,
and it can monitor any of the sessions user want to observe".

**The ruling (23:33Z, the focus session):** asked whether it applies to monitor clicks only or replaces GV-D4 everywhere,
James answered "Everywhere". Asked about a session another pane already shows, he answered "Mirror it". This re-rules
GV-D4's answer of 2026-10-02 ("Beside the focused pane, up to three", built at `06ad0ecf6` on 10-11). That build's "never
mounted twice" came from the drawing's code, never from a ruling. The new rule returns to GT-D17 (08-05): "clicking a
bubble attaches the CURRENT ACTIVE pane".

**The change (one commit, built by an Opus builder in `/Volumes/SamsungRed/focus-tp`):**
- `deckPlacement`: the focused pane already shows it → focus; any focused pane → replace, a mirror when another pane shows
  it; no focused pane → none. The `beside` answer, `DECK_PLACEMENT_PANES` and the empty-pane field are removed. ⌘D is
  the one deliberate way to more panes.
- The deck only mounts; it never adds or splits. `mountLocalNow` skips the floor read only when the focused pane itself
  shows the session. The zoom rule and the geometry seat are unchanged: in a mirror, the pane that holds the seat sets
  the size.
- Every door follows the rule: a body, a list row, a rain column, a timeline lane, a spend row, a search result, History's
  Resume and Jump to, the Peek's Open, a peer's attach, ⌘T and the bloom. Their notes now say "… in the active pane".
- Docs first, in the commit: DESIGN.md §8 "A session with no pane", DECISIONS GV-D4 RE-RULED, `docs/agent-plane/system.html`.
- smoke:godview's 13a now clicks a local terminal row (its selector had clicked "＋ New terminal…"). It prefers a session
  another pane shows and asserts the mirror. The jump rungs' steps 6 and 6b assert the mirror too.

## IOS — signed in is connected: the phone keeps its mesh up by itself and re-dials a drop; the corner's Connect and Disconnect are gone (2026-10-19; `dd109bfd9` → `b844febfa`)

**What James asked:** "on mobile, there should not be a connect button, the phone should automatically connect to desktop
as long as the account is logged in, user should not need to manually tap connect or disconnect, it is auto connected and
maintained connection all the time".

**Before:** in a Release build nothing connected by itself, and a drop was never retried. Found on the way: a `.stopped`
runtime made the next start refuse silently.

**The change:**
- `MeshModel.keepUp()` runs at launch, on coming to the front, and when the network returns. Its steps are a pure table
  (`keepUpStep`).
- A drop is `reconnecting(reason)` and re-dials on the product client's ladder (0.5 s doubling, held at 60 s).
- `signIn()` is the person's act; an automatic start never opens Safari.
- `connect()` and `disconnect()` are removed.
- The corner offers Sign in only while the tailnet asks, and the open menu's line says "reconnecting…".

**Checks:**
- FieldMeshTests 264 and FieldHomeTests 44 passed.
- Probe: a waiting re-dial never taken up fails the step table's two reconnecting rows.

- The node stays up in the background.

## IOS — the phone's swarm paints at 120 Hz, blends by the clock, and steps its physics at the display's rate with Matter's constraint law: a held bubble follows the finger (2026-10-19; `e022459c4` `94a6d1408` `67c6f69ab` `6b3fb0b70` → `cfb002763` `dac958e3b` `bed8d0e72` `afeaccb68`)

**What James asked:** "on phone, the physics feels not as smooth as long before, the interaction sometimes feels laggy, and
lacks the buttery smooth feeling".

**Cause** (the audit of 10-18; the regression is IOS-6b `2ac903281`, 09-13): the phone went from one step per vsync to 30
Hz steps plus a blend drawn one step behind, all on the main thread, with the app capped at 60 Hz (no
`CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone`). The blend took a frame's AGE, so draw jitter stalled a frame and jumped the next.
The MV lead measured the same one-step cause on the desktop (probe-8, about 37 px behind a 1000 px/s pointer); the desktop
fix is its own.

**The four commits:**
- **The DEBUG frame meter:** every 5 s, the rate, p50 / p95 / max of the frame interval, the long frames and the steps a
  frame.
- **The 120 Hz key.**
- **`SwarmWorld.blend`:** accumulator ÷ step, in place of the frame-age blend.
- **`SwarmParameters.phone` (120 Hz) and Matter's constraint law** (`stiffness × min(1, Δ/16.67)²`). In Verlet a drag is a
  mass on a spring, and only the square keeps July's 60 Hz swing at 120 Hz.

**Errata at source:** `physicsHz`'s "a cost knob and not a smoothness knob" is corrected, dated.

**Checks:**
- FieldSwarmTests 35 and SwarmPhysicsTests 29 passed.
- Probes:
  - the frame-age blend put back stalls 3 frames under jitter;
  - the flat spring put back swings 24–60 pt apart from 60 Hz.

**Witness on James's phone (01:39Z):** the meter over 71 windows read 67 at ≥ 110 Hz, p50 8.3 ms, ≈1.00 steps a frame.
James, 01:47Z: "good, i think they all work pretty good". Some windows in use still show long frames. P4–P7 (text-layout
cache, FieldLink publishing only on change, LivePulse off-page, pause under a card) are recorded and held until he asks.

## W4 re-ruled — the monitor's field never shrinks past rest: a deck set above rest slides over the swarm, which keeps its bounds (2026-10-19; `d658b5d4b` → `40bb598d0`, lane `mv/swarm-squeeze`)

**What James asked (2026-10-19 02:10Z, through the focus session):** "for the swarm squeeze issue, let's tackle this
way, when at the default terminal pane height, the swarm area is at its min height, so when user move the terminal pane
further up, no more squeezing the swarm bounds".

**The rule:** the monitor's field ends at rest + max(0, the edge's shift as last set) − the gap (12).
- It replaces round 3's W4, "the monitor makes room", under which the field ended 12 above the edge as last set, down to
  a floor of 220. Up past rest, the sheet now slides over the field: the bodies go on moving beneath it, and the swarm
  keeps the bounds rest gave it. Down past rest, the field still grows with the edge.
- The field's own floor (220, `--vf-godview-deck-field-floor`) is subsumed and removed. Rest is the larger of 5/13 of the
  stage and 232, which is 220 plus the gap, so the field is still never shorter than 220.
- At rest nothing moves: the deck-up field on James's Mac stays 1712 × 393, so the swarm's numbers measured there stand.
- The SWF entry above ("The swarm's crowd fits its field", 2026-10-14) said his min-height ruling stands. This entry
  re-rules it.

**The change (one commit, code-only, docs first in it):**
- `godview.css`: `--vf-godview-field-foot: calc(var(--vf-godview-deck-rest) + max(0px, var(--vf-godview-field-shift,
  0px)) - var(--vf-godview-deck-field-gap))`.
- No JS change. `deck-edge.ts` still writes the edge as set, above rest too, and the stylesheet counts a shift below
  zero as none. Its doc comment now says so.
- `tokens.css`: `--vf-godview-deck-field-floor` is removed.
- Docs:
  - DESIGN.md §8 "The monitor makes room" is rewritten with James's words and a dated note (until 2026-10-19 the edge
    shrank the field to a 220 floor). §8's Rest is updated, and §2.7's token lines carry a dated note on the floor
    token.
  - DECISIONS: the One Frame row's status (round 3's W4 RE-RULED), and the SWF row's min-height clause points to it.
- Tests:
  - `godview-stage-rule.test.ts` gains a new row. For windows 780, 1040 and 520, with the edge set 1 px up, at the fill
    line and at the window's top, the field's foot stays at rest's. At the fill line the edge stands above the foot,
    so the sheet is over the field. 96 px down, the foot follows the edge less 12. A 400 px window keeps 220.
  - The same file's shift row now expects `300 + max(0, shift) − 12`, and the floor token's entry is gone.
  - `godview-deck-edge.test.tsx`: the layout model and the CSS pin read the new calc, and the floor token's row is gone.
