## AL-9 — main takes ⌘Q and ⌃⌘F above every page, and the deck's closing verbs swap no session: ⌘Q over a focused terminal minimized the deck and swapped the active pane's session out instead of quitting (2026-10-27; `933d2fba3`, lane `al/chords`; AL-D14 "A", AL-D15…D18; VF-PM's GO)

**Why:** the quit gate's acceptance run (08:24–08:39Z, §AL-7) passed every row it ran, except one: ⌘Q over a focused
terminal hid the deck instead of quitting. The read (`draft/thinking-app-lifecycle.md` §9):
- On macOS Electron offers a key to the page first, and a key the page claims never reaches the menu (SNAP-3's
  finding, `screenshot-chord.ts`).
- ghosttea's workspace (`Workspace.js:690`) claims Ghostty's `quit` (⌘Q), `close_window` (⌘⇧W) and
  `toggle_fullscreen` (⌃⌘F) on the window's capture phase, and never checks `defaultPrevented`. A page product chord
  on the same node cannot stop it.
- The deck gave it no `quit` hook, so ⌘Q fell back to `closeWindow`: the terminals minimized, N16's `emptyLastPane`
  swapped the ACTIVE pane's session out (any pane, not only the last), and nothing quit. ⌘⇧W and
  `close_all_windows` did the same. The deck's `toggleFullscreen` is empty, so ⌃⌘F did nothing.

**What landed** (electron-shell · field-app; ruled by James at the PM board 17:12:47–17:13:47Z, DECISIONS' AL-D14…AL-D18
row in the same commit):
- AL-D14 "A": `window-chords.ts` `installWindowChords` acts in main's `before-input-event`, before the page is offered
  the key. `preventDefault` keeps the chord from the page and from the menu shortcut, so it acts exactly once. ⌘Q
  calls `app.quit()`, the call the menu role and the tray's Quit make, so it reaches AL-3's census gate as a person's
  quit. Installed on the main window (beside SNAP-3's screenshot chord) and on Studio's window.
- AL-D15: ⌃⌘F through the same door (`setFullScreen(!isFullScreen())`). ⌘H, ⌘⌥H and ⌘M are taken only if a hand row
  shows a pane eats them; ⌘W never. Off the Mac nothing is taken: the Windows port measures first (§9.3).
- AL-D16 (keep GT-D5/N16's ⌘W lend) and AL-D17 (⌘N unclaimed): nothing built.
- AL-D18: ⌘⇧W, `close_all_windows` and any other chord bound to Ghostty's `quit` put the terminals away
  (`putTerminalsAway`: the owner minimizes, or a deck no overlay owns asks for Canvas) and swap no session. N16's
  emptying is kept for the deck's LAST pane alone (`panes.length === 1`). With one pane ⌘⇧W still reads as ⌘W, because
  ghosttea gives the two no separate hooks. A ghosttea "last pane closed" hook is a recorded upstream ask (DECISIONS,
  §9.3), filed with the next ghosttea petition round.
- The words:
  - `product-chords.ts` gains `takenBy: "shell"` rows for ⌘Q ("Quit VibeField") and ⌃⌘F ("Full screen"); `matches`
    is optional for a chord no page listener hears.
  - Settings → Terminal → Keyboard's rows say them. keyboard-model's platform words for
    `close_window`/`close_all_windows`/`quit` said "Closes Godview" and now say "Puts the terminals away"
    (`close_window`: "— with one pane, it empties that pane too").
  - The keyfoot names ⌘Q and ⌃⌘F as the app's, taken before any page.

**What a test reaches, and what only a hand does:**
- Tests:
  - the predicate (`windowChordOf`: darwin only, keyDown, no auto-repeat, ⌘ alone or ⌃⌘, never ⌥ or ⇧);
  - the installer (`preventDefault`, then quit once, or full screen toggled);
  - the deck's verbs (⌘⇧W, close-all and quit minimize and never empty a pane among several; the last pane alone
    empties);
  - the words.
- No test or smoke here can press a physical key (no input injection on this Mac). Only James's row 1 proves the whole
  path: a physical ⌘Q over a focused pane brings up the census box, logs `desktop.quit.census_read` and sends no
  `deck_changed`. His ten rows are in ROADMAP's Eyeballs ("The window chords (AL-9)").

**Rows:**
- `packages/electron-shell/test/window-chords.test.ts` (new, 7).
- godview-deck.test.tsx "the closing verbs put the terminals away and swap no session (AL-9, AL-D18)" (3).

## AO — item 82: one slow row is one red in the Setup Assistant's suite — no act() outlives its row; and the suite's cold first row takes its measured budget (2026-10-27; `714ecbaae` + `8828601ed`, lane `fix/item82-act-scope`; VF-PM's rulings 20:50Z and 21:08Z)

**What happened:** item 81's `pnpm verify` at `6e0da9902` (20:42–20:48Z, load 185 at its end) went red on field-app's
`onboarding-wizard.test.tsx` alone, with 40 of its 42 rows red:
- its first row ("walks a fresh install…") timed out at 5022 ms, and one more ("records Agents answered from the
  inventory and moves on to History (AO-5)") at 5005 ms;
- every other row failed in 1–8 ms on an EMPTY DOM (`no button labelled "Get started" in: ` with nothing after it;
  `expected '' to contain …`).
Alone it was 42/42, its first row 1202 ms and the next-slowest 28 ms. One slow row read as 40 findings and hid which,
if any, were real.

**The cause is React's own act scope, not a stale render** (VF-PM's two suggestions, a fresh render per row or a wait
on the wizard's ready word, would not reach it: `mount()` already makes a new container and root every row):
- react 19.2.7 (`cjs/react.development.js:806` on) keeps one `actScopeDepth` for the module. `popActScope` restores
  the depth an act was ENTERED at, and an act entered at depth > 0 resolves without flushing.
- The row that timed out was inside `arrive()`'s act, awaiting `vi.dynamicImportSettled()` (a lazy pane's cold import).
  That act stayed open past its row, so afterEach's unmount and every later mount nested inside it and committed
  nothing.
- The row itself ran on as a zombie, through `arrive`'s turns on the next row's container and fake clock. Acts that
  finished out of order left the depth above zero for the rest of the file, which is why the AO-5 row timed out too.

**The fix** (`714ecbaae`, test-only, file-local by VF-PM's ruling: a shared helper the day a second file needs it):
- A file-local `it`/`it.fails` runs each row's body in an `AsyncLocalStorage` scope that holds vitest 3.2.7's
  `context.signal`, which the runner aborts synchronously at the row's timeout, before afterEach
  (@vitest/runner `chunk-hooks.js:641`, `:1914`), and the row's end as one promise with one abort listener. One per act
  would trip Node's MaxListenersExceededWarning, since a row makes more than 10.
- A file-local `act` races an async callback against the row's end, so the act a row was in when it timed out ends with
  it and React pops its scope. A row that is over starts no act. Outside a row (afterEach's unmount) `act` is React's
  own.
- afterEach awaits the row's acts before it unmounts. `arrive` stops after the import when its row is over, because the
  clock it would advance is the next row's.
- The proof, at the file's end ("item 82 — one slow row is one red"): an `it.fails` row times out inside an act on
  purpose (100 ms), and the row after it must mount the wizard, read "Welcome." and answer Get started.

**The budget** (`8828601ed`, VF-PM 21:08Z: "not a budget" was for the cascade; a cold row that is one honest red under
load is the budget case): row 1 is the file's first walk through every pane, so each lazy pane's code arrives inside act
on its way. 30 s in doc-manager.test.ts:168's form, with 1029–1347 ms alone (×5) and 5022 ms under item 81's verify
beside it.

**Validation** (this Mac's SSD lane `/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/item82`, guard, nice 19; the slot from 21:44Z):
- **Red-first** (records/redfirst-onboarding-wizard.test.tsx: main's file at `1341c06b7` byte for byte, with the two
  proof rows appended; logs/redfirst/): the on-purpose row times out as it must (106 ms). The row after it is RED in
  1 ms, `expected '' to contain 'Welcome.'`, the cascade's own signature.
- **At the fix:** 44/44, the row after 9 ms, with no MaxListeners, overlapping-act or unhandled warnings.
- **The witness**, both harnesses at `--testTimeout=600`, so the file's own cold first row times out as under that
  verify (logs/witness/):
  - the old harness reads 41 of 44 red: row 1 (666 ms) and the AO-5 row (602 ms) time out, and every other row is empty
    in 0–5 ms. That is item 81's verify, reproduced on demand.
  - The fix reads ONE red, row 1's own timeout (606 ms), and the other 43 rows are green.
- **Row 1 alone ×5** (logs/row1/): 1333, 1191, 1090, 1029, 1347 ms, every run green.
- **Rebased** onto `d9e5eb119` (merge-tree rehearsed: tree `6258e8abd`, no lane file in the onto-range; patch-ids

- **`pnpm verify`** at `8828601ed` (logs/verify/verify.log): EXIT 101 (21:49:40–21:57:27Z; load 8.7 armed, 125 at its end).
  Every stage before the Rust tests passed, and the TS test target too ("Successfully ran target test for 27 projects"):

**What.** TS-8 is the ladder's upstream rung (thinking doc §10): T9, T10 and T11 shipped together as truffle 0.7.24
(sidecar protocol 11, the lead's EL8 `af3f3078f`). The EL8 moved only the pins, so VibeField's use of them is this

    and `clientLogUpload`; `MeshFailure` "logging_required"; `MeshRetireResult.signedOut`;
  - the link: `UserLinkState` "logs_required", a state rather than a reason (the tolerant-reader law);
    `UserLinkStatus`'s `tailscaleVersion`, `needsSignature` and `sendLogs`; `TailscaleLink.sendLogs`, kept in
    link.json and never in an env var; `UserLinkBeginParams.sendLogs`;
  - a door, `user.link.logs {send}` (settings.manage, local);
  - two fixtures parsed on both sides, `mesh-self-identity.locked` and `mesh-not-up-details.logs-required`.
- **field-native:**
  - The builder's `client_log_upload` is false unless asked (D15). It is the BUILT value beside the gate, so a changed
    opt-in builds the node again.
  - The status hook hears truffle's new events:
    - `LoggingRequired` names `logging_required`, and takes a running node down as `SidecarExited` does;
    - `NeedsSignature` and `Signed` set Tailnet Lock's hold, and the unit's words say it;
    - `BackendStateChanged` with NeedsLogin reads as signed out, and Running as up again.
  - At the install, the version and the hold are read from the node.
  - TS-1's 15 s tick is RETIRED: the pin is exact 0.7.24, so no older sidecar is in the build, and truffle delivers
    the backend event for every sidecar.
  - `retire()` calls `Node::logout()` first. truffle bounds it at 12 s (LOGOUT_TIMEOUT) and stops the node either way,
    and `native.mesh.retire` answers `signedOut`.
- **fieldd (the link service):**
  - The floor is asked with link.json's `sendLogs`, or the capture's.
  - `logging_required` → `logs_required`, live and after a floor restart. `begin({sendLogs})` begins a refused
    capture again, and refuses a standing link, naming its act. `cancel()` ends a refused capture.
  - `logs(send)` keeps the opt-in in link.json and builds the node again. Its door is audited.
  - `unlink()` gives the retire 20 s: the mgmt default (10 s) would give up before truffle's 12 s bound, which
    contains the sidecar's own 10 s. Its audit records `signedOut`.
- **field-app:** the tolerant reader knows `logs_required`, and draws the offline face ("This Mac only", §11's menu
  word) until TS-8b gives it its own.
- **Not in it:** the faces and their words (TS-8b: DESIGN.md §8/§9 are drafted on `ts/8-surface`, and "Connected,
  not yet trusted" goes to James with its photograph), and T8's hostname prefix (TS-8c, after its probe).

**Found:**
- **D15's default reaches every stub sidecar.** truffle probes an opted-out node's sidecar protocol first, and refuses
  one below 11. The stand-ins for "a sidecar" answer `tsnet:version` at protocol 11: mesh_unit's two, and
  mgmt_server's TS-1 wire stand-in, which the light pass did not run and the first verify's alone `test:rust` caught.
  The UA-P-4 rows, whose old protocol is their point, ask for uploads, so the login gate is still what refuses them.
- **truffle can drop a `LoggingRequired` at a start.** It aborts the status forwarder with a failed build, so the
  failure branch also reads the refusal from truffle's start error. A typed refusal is a candidate petition, in
  focus-session's queue after T8.
- **field-app keeps its own list of the link's words**, so a contract word it does not list is derived from the facts.
  Without `logs_required` in it, a standing record kept down for its logs would have read as linked. The light pass's
  field-app typecheck caught it.
- **A node that starts unsigned hears Tailnet Lock's hold before its install**, so the install's words said plain Up.
  The install now chooses its words from the hold (`up_words`).

## FN — item 83: the ledger's refresh row takes its first `as_of` from an attempt that returned — the row's read raced, the ledger is right (2026-10-27; `f0b5342ac`, lane `fix/item83-ledger-as-of`; VF-PM's ruling 23:34Z)

**What happened:** TS-8b's alone `pnpm test:rust` (23:28:09–23:28:38Z) went red once on field-native's
`services::terminal::tests::the_ledger_refreshes_the_machine_total_while_this_floors_total_stands_still`
(terminal.rs:4626, FN's row of `f601f7ff0`, 2026-10-19), "and every refresh that lands is an answer: as_of moved". The
row passed 30/30 alone after that, and the field-native tree was TS-8a's, which TS-8b does not touch.

**The cause is the row's read, not the ledger's stamp order** (d0's read, unproven, was that the pressure is set
inside the attempt and `as_of` stamped when it returns. The code does it the other way round):
- One ledger attempt is two flocks: `publish` writes this floor's total, then `machine_total` reads the machine's back
  (admission.rs:284, :291).
- `LedgerPump::observe` seeds `as_of` with the attempt's `begun` before the file work, stamps the same `begun` when the
  attempt returns (:3203), and only then sets the pressure (:3217).
- The row waited for the file to show 1 and took `first = slot.as_of()` with `.expect("the publish landed")`. That was
  the misread: the file shows the publish while the attempt is still inside, so `first` could be attempt 1's seed.
- When the other pair's `try_reserve` took the flock before attempt 1's read-back, attempt 1 answered PtyExhausted
  itself and stamped `begun_1`, the same value as `first`. The assert went red, and the refresh the row claims to prove
  never ran.

**The product is right.** `as_of` is "the moment the ledger's last returned attempt began". Attempt 1 began before the
reservation and its answer included it, so `begun_1` is the honest stamp. Because the stamp comes before the pressure
write, a reader who sees PtyExhausted sees the stamp of the attempt that read it. The ledger thread is the pressure's
only writer, and the sampler's late judge (:2697) reads `as_of` alone. Moving the stamp after the apply would not
touch this red either: both values are `begun_1`.

**The fix** (`f0b5342ac`, test-only, the row alone, +12/−1):
- After the file shows 1, the row waits for `as_of` to move past the seed, then reads `first` and asserts Up.
- A stamped value's read-back came before the row read it, so it came before the reservation. The PtyExhausted answer
  therefore comes from a later attempt.
- :4626 stays a hard assert (not an `eventually`), so the refresh claim stays tested. The Up assert now reads a real
  answer, where before it held because the pressure starts None.
- Siblings read and left as they are: the flock row and IL-D6's held-flock row wait for `as_of().is_some()` and mean
  the seed; `a_ledger_that_fails_at_once_is_never_late` drives `observe` synchronously.

## AO — item 84: the History pane says "last used" against the clock it is given — the Setup Assistant's pane forwards `now`, so the suite's "today" no longer expires at midnight (2026-10-28; `68296443f`, lane `fix/item84-history-clock`; VF-PM's ruling 02:41Z)

**What happened:** CI's verify on the pushed `0ec11879e` (run 40605216364, the verify job 23:53Z–00:26Z) failed ONE
row, field-app `test/history-consent.test.tsx:202`, "the History pane (AO-3) › opens with every switch on, says the
time and where it stays, and brings the complete set in", on "expected … to contain '6.2 GB · last used today'".
Every other row was green (field-app 2756/2757; fieldd 2575 with 11 skipped). This is not a lottery row, so CI was not
rerun: a rerun would be green or red by the clock and hide the cause.

**The cause is a fixed date read against the wall clock** (the class of 2026-10-03's TL status-history row):
- The suite dates its census fixtures from a fixed `NOW = new Date("2026-10-27T12:00:00")`: claude-code's newest file
  at NOW, codex's a day before. Its `lastUsedWords` unit rows pass NOW.
- The pane row mounts `HistoryWizardPane`, which took no `now`, so `HistoryConsentPane` said "last used" against its
  default, `Date.now()`.
- "today" was therefore true on 2026-10-27 local time alone: green on CI's runs before midnight UTC, red on the first
  after it (00:17Z). On a Mac in PDT it reds from 07:00Z on 10-28.

**The gap was the controller's door, not the view.** `HistoryConsentPane` already takes `now` (default `Date.now()`),
and the design-system catalog already hands the body `FIXTURE_HISTORY_NOW`. `HistoryWizardPane`, the pane of the Setup
Assistant and of Finish setting up, had no way to pass one.

**The fix** (`68296443f`, 3 files, +12/−2):
- `HistoryWizardPane` takes an optional `now` and forwards it, with the pane's own clock when none is given. Production
  is unchanged: SetupSheet and the onboarding HistoryPane pass none.
- `HistoryConsentPane`'s `now` is typed `number | undefined`, so a forwarded absence reaches its default
  (exactOptionalPropertyTypes).
- The suite's `mountPane` passes `now: NOW`. Its fixtures stay dated from NOW, never from the wall clock.

**The known sibling, left as it is** (VF-PM 02:41Z: not worth a change): `NewAgentPast`'s host renders with
`now={Date.now()}`, and `new-agent-past.test.tsx` dates one fixture `Date.now()` for "last used today". Both read the
wall clock, so that row can red only on a run that crosses local midnight between building the fixture and the
render. The class is the same; the window is milliseconds wide.

**Validation** (this Mac's SSD lane `/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/item84`, guard, nice 19; VF-PM's GRANT 02:41Z):

    past the fixture's: RED, 8 of 9, the row at :202 on "expected … to contain '6.2 GB · last used today'". That is
    CI's red on demand.
  - Main's files with a lane-only fake Date (`toFake: ["Date"]`) at NOW + a day: RED, the same row, the same words.
  - The fix with the same fake Date: green, 9 of 9.
  - The fix as committed: green, 9 of 9, under each of UTC (CI's), America/Los_Angeles (this Mac's),
    Pacific/Kiritimati (+14) and Pacific/Pago_Pago (−11).
  - The tree was restored from HEAD after each run, and was clean.

## FN — item 85: a route move between the routes subscription's reading and its forwarder's first poll reaches fieldd; the design-system page's budget is measured on CI's runner (2026-10-28; `7eda2ee38`, `b60e80398`, lane `fix/item85-routes-baseline`; VF-PM's rulings 18:22Z and 18:33Z)

**What happened:** CI's verify on the pushed `e3a00a07f` (run 40728506315) went red on its two attempts, on two
different rows, each green on the other attempt and on this Mac:
- **Attempt 1** (17:23Z): field-app `test/design-system.test.tsx` › "shows the launcher of a pane born under a
  profile…", "Hook timed out in 60000ms" in the beforeEach that renders the whole `<DesignSystemPage />`.
- **Attempt 2** (18:08Z): fieldd `test/agent-session.test.ts` › MF-1f/MF-1g "resume hands the pane over…", at its
  setup's 30 s wait, "the floor's terminal endpoints reaching the daemon did not hold within 30000 ms". Item 68's
  evidence at the deadline read "fieldd's link: connected; routes heard at revision 1, 0 cell(s)". The floor's own log
  had both cells serving at +219 ms, 4 ms after the mgmt client authenticated, and nothing moved for 30 s.

VF-PM made both item 85. They are two causes: a field-native race and a thin budget.

**The race, since TM-r13 `8e9cfbb82` (2026-09-14), in `native.lifecycle.terminal.routes.subscribe`
(`mgmt/mod.rs`):**
- The handler read the current snapshot for its result (`state.terminal_routes.borrow()`, the revision-1
  announcement, no cells). It then spawned `spawn_routes_forwarder` with a clone of the state's receiver.
- At its first poll the forwarder's task marked whatever the channel held THEN as seen (`rx.borrow_and_update()`,
  added so the stream's first delta would not repeat the result).
- When the cells came up between the result's read and that poll, revision 2 was marked seen and never sent.
  TC-D15's "a missed delta is repaired by the next one" did not hold, because a floor whose cells are up has no next
  one.

**The fix** (`7eda2ee38`, `mgmt/mod.rs` only, +131/−53):
- The handler marks the baseline in the SAME read that builds the result (`borrow_and_update` on its clone), and hands
  that receiver to the forwarder, which no longer marks anything.
- T-M2's dedupe stands: the result's own snapshot is still never repeated. A move after the read wakes the forwarder
  however late its task first runs.
- The row: `a_route_move_before_the_forwarder_first_runs_is_delivered_once`. It drives the window on a current-thread
  runtime, where a spawned task runs only at the next await. The result reads revision 1, revision 2 lands before the
  forwarder runs, and the reader must hear revision 2, once. T-M2's row's two helpers are hoisted to the module for it,
  unchanged.
- **The siblings, noted and left unchanged → ITEM 86** ("health/observed subscribe: subscribe-then-read on one
  receiver", planned). `native.lifecycle.health.subscribe` and `.observed.subscribe` read the Sender's value, then
  `subscribe()`, so a send from another thread between those two statements is lost the same way. That window has no
  await in it, so no current-thread row can drive it, and neither changes blind (VF-PM 18:22Z). Each handler carries a
  dated note naming the closing shape: the routes handler's, one receiver read once with `borrow_and_update`.
- **Item 63, likely, not proven.** Item 63's red (the nightly's AR-6-0 row, 2026-10-26) was the same 30 s setup wait
  for `daemon.native.terminalEndpoints`, and its twin in agent-gateway-floor.ts reddened the same way twice on this
  Mac. Its floor's log was deleted with the row's temp root, so whether it was this race cannot be shown.

**The budget.** DK-11's 60 s (2026-10-05) was "the worst render measured about twice its time", measured on this Mac.
CI's runner is the slower host:
- Attempt 1's runner was slow all through. field-app's test task took 773 s (161–488 s in the eight green runs before
  it) and fieldd's 1349 s (682–1042 s); this file took 415 s (61–197 s).
- Nothing in the design-system sources or this test changed in `c903853a1..e3a00a07f`.
- **Measured** (each row is vitest's own time: render, body and unmount, since its runner starts the clock before
  beforeEach):
  - CI, nine green runs of verify (10-27/28, the eight before plus attempt 2): 4.6–47.6 s a row.
  - CI, attempt 1: 22–84 s a row, and one render past 60 s. Rows of 76 s and 84 s passed there, because the hook and
    the body each have their own budget.
  - This Mac, the file alone ×3 at the lane's tip (nice 19, load 15–18, 18:24:53–18:26:10Z): 1.5–2.8 s a row, 24 of
    24 passed.
  - DK-11's 10-05 envelope, alone: a 1.3–1.7 s render and a body of at most 0.9 s. **The page did not grow**: the
    catalog's sources grew 2% by lines (19,617 → 20,003) since 10-05.
- **The line** (`b60e80398`, the test only, +6/−1): `PAGE_BUDGET_MS = 120_000`, twice the 60 s that render passed.
  It still bounds the hook, the body and the unmount separately, so a render that hangs still fails. DK-11's claim is

- Not taken (VF-PM 18:33Z): one render per file is a test-isolation change. If the row reds again at 120 s, that

**Validation** (this Mac's SSD lane `/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/item85`, guard, nice 19; VF-PM's GRANT 18:22Z, the mark
18:33Z):

## AL-9b — one chord table in main: a held ⌘Q, ⌃⌘F or ⌃⌘A acts once and its repeats reach no page or menu, a non-Latin layout's chord names the physical key's letter, and ⌃⌘A joins ⌘Q and ⌃⌘F in one listener (2026-10-29; `cc37d2d8e`, lane `al/chords-2`; James's "do the follow ups"; VF-PM's GO)

**Why:** James asked for a review of AL-9 (`933d2fba3`) on 2026-10-27, then for its follow-ups on 10-29. The review
found two gaps that could bring AL-9's symptom back, and two cleanups:
- **Repeats passed through.** `windowChordOf` returned null for an auto-repeat, so a held chord's repeats reached the
  page and the menu. ghosttea's workspace keydown (`Workspace.js:632`) does not skip repeats. A held ⌘Q over a pane
  therefore ran the deck's `quit` hook and put the terminals away behind the quit box. A held ⌃⌘F reached the menu's
  `togglefullscreen` and flipped it back. A held ⌃⌘A (SNAP-3's chord, the same rule) reached the canvas's select-all.
- **The letter came from `key` alone.** ghosttea's matcher also reads the physical key (`unicodeCandidates`,
  ghostty-triggers.js), and macOS's key equivalents fall back to the Latin letter on a non-Latin layout. A layout
  that reports ⌘ and the Q key as its own letter (Russian "й") would leave ⌘Q to the pane, AL-9's bug again.
- `WindowChordInput` was a field-for-field copy of `ScreenshotChordInput`, with two `before-input-event` listeners per
  product window.
- `ProductChord`'s `matches?` and `takenBy?` were coupled by a rule that only a test row held.

**What landed** (electron-shell · field-app):
- `window-chords.ts` is the one table: ⌃⌘A (SNAP-3; Alt+A off the Mac, SNAP-D3), ⌘Q and ⌃⌘F (AL-9; darwin only).
  - `installWindowChords(target, { quit, screenshot? })`. The screenshot act is absent where no capture can run (no
    helper, Studio's window), and ⌃⌘A is then left to the page and the menu, as before.
  - `screenshot-chord.ts` and its test are gone, and their rows are in window-chords.test.ts. main's index.ts installs
    one listener.
- A matched chord's repeats are swallowed and act on nothing; the act runs once, on the first press. A keyUp is still
  not swallowed.
- `chordLetterOf` decides the letter:
  - the key's own letter when it is a Latin letter;
  - the physical key's (`KeyQ` → q) only when the key's character is not ASCII;
  - an ASCII key the layout sends (Dvorak's `'` on the Q key) is the layout's own and names no chord, as macOS's menus
    do.
- `ProductChord = PageChord | ShellChord`: a page chord has its matcher, a shell chord has none, and the compiler holds
  the rule. The runtime row that held it is retired.
- GodviewDeck's `quit` hook comment now reads true: ⌘Q never reaches it on the Mac, held or not; off the Mac Ghostty's
  `ctrl+shift+q` does.

**Not in it** (AL-9c candidates for James's word, on VF-PM's board):
- a person's own Ghostty `quit` chord quitting the app (a page→main door);
- the deck's no-op `toggleFullscreen` (the same door);
- Settings' words off the Mac;
- the deck's last-pane count (the upstream "last pane closed" hook).

**What a test reaches, and what only a hand does:**
- Tests:
  - the predicate: each chord, each modifier mix, keyUp, repeats named, the Russian and Dvorak layouts, off the Mac;
  - the installer: each act once; the repeats swallowed and inert for all three; ⌃⌘A left alone with no capture;
    every other key untouched.
- By hand only: whether macOS delivers a chord to `before-input-event`, and what Electron's `key` reads on a Russian
  input source. ROADMAP §5's witnesses gain AL-9b's two rows beside AL-9's ten: a held ⌘Q over a focused pane, and
  ⌘Q under a Russian input source.

**Rows:** window-chords.test.ts 13 (was AL-9's 7 plus screenshot-chord's 5); product-chords.test.tsx (the coupling row
retired).

**Gates** (lane al2, nice 19, the guard before each step; VF-PM's slot from 01:07Z):
- The light pass (01:07:35–01:08:40Z, load 9→17) EXIT 0:
  - typecheck electron-shell and field-app; biome; check:walls;
  - preflight, with 2 WARN, both main's: the lane's unused puppeteer checkout, and R23's acp candidate;
  - window-chords 13/13; product-chords, terminal-keyboard-model and godview-deck 103/103.

**What.** TS-4 is the ladder's rung for asking again (thinking doc §10, D7; §14 for its marks). Someone who said Not
now said it before they had a reason, so the offer returns only where a connected device would do the job. The plan
(`lanes/ts3/drafts/ts4-plan.md`, a code read on `3e6c941a8`) split D7's places in two:

    a place's own `retired` for good; its own 30 days after a saying; any other place's saying spends the day; an

## AL — the shell lease's rows settle every lease's writes before their root goes: "only the LAST holder's close" raced its own temp root's removal (2026-10-29; `2422bdf5c`, lane `fix/shell-lease-enotempty`; VF-PM's word 03:08Z and 03:13Z)

**What happened:** `shell-lease.test.ts` "only the LAST holder's close vacates it; a second holder keeps it held"
failed with ENOTEMPTY on its own mkdtemp root at the afterEach `rmSync` (:26). This is a 4 ms row.
- **Witnesses:**
  - CI run 40807651886, attempt 1, on the pushed `77322a501`: 2590 passed and this one failed. Nothing pushed touches
    the lease.
  - Earlier: QW1 stack B's verify at load 236, green alone (VF-PM 10-28 09:39Z, the Fixer queue's "the shell lease's
    cleanup race").

**The cause, read:**
- `ShellLease.closed()` (fieldd `src/shell-lease.ts`), for the last holder, chains the record's write onto `writes`
  and returns at once. The write is a mkdir of `fieldd/`, a temp file opened, written and fsynced, then
  `durableRename` onto `LAYOUT.SHELL_EXIT`.
- Every other row that vacates the lease awaits `flush()`. This one ends right after its second close, so its
  write was still in flight when the cleanup's recursive `rmSync` listed the root. The directory or temp file the
  write made after that listing left the root not empty.

**The fix** (`2422bdf5c`, the test only):
- The `lease()` helper pushes `value.flush()` onto the cleanup list after `tempRoot()`'s `rmSync`. The list runs in
  reverse, so every lease's writes settle before its root is removed. That includes a later row that ends without a
  flush.
- `flush()` never rejects: its chain catches and logs. Nothing tolerates the error and nothing retries.
- The daemon rows were already covered, since the daemon's stop awaits the lease's flush (`daemon.ts`:6913).

**Validation** (this Mac's SSD lane `/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/item87`, guard, nice 19; VF-PM's GO 03:13Z and 03:16Z):
- **The file alone** at `2422bdf5c` (03:14:11–16Z, load 11.1): 15/15 passed. The row passed in 11 ms.
- **`pnpm verify`, verbatim**, at `2422bdf5c` on `77322a501` (03:17:50–03:27:39Z; armed at a 1-min load of 17.4
  after PORTALS' drain; the 5-min load was 128 at the end): **EXIT 0**.
  - The test target: "Successfully ran target test for 27 projects". fieldd 2,591 passed (11 skipped), with
    `shell-lease.test.ts` 15/15; field-app 2,788 passed.
  - `pnpm test:rust`: 31 suites, 493 passed, 0 failed. gen:check clean.
- Records: `/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/records/shell-lease/`.

## FN — item 87: a run's exit is published before its workspace cleanup, and a resume during the cleanup waits a bound then says finalizing (2026-10-29; `8d56b2bd8`, lane `fix/item87-exit-cleanup`; VF-PM's rulings 02:16Z, 02:50Z, 02:58Z and 03:13Z)

**What happened:** `agent-session.test.ts`'s MF-1f/MF-1g rows interrupt a scripted run (`endedRun`) and wait 15 s for
`continuation.exited`. That wait timed out twice, and each time the log stopped at `fieldd.agents.interrupted`:
- item 85's MF-1f run 2 (10-28 18:24Z, load 18);
- item 89's verify run 1 (10-29 01:55Z, load ~215).

**The witnesses** (records `logs/witness`, `logs/witness2`, VF-PM's GO 02:35Z and 02:43Z):
- `endedRun`'s steps ran ×30 on one warm floor, then ×30 on a fresh floor per pass (routes rev 3, 2 cells, the lost
  shape). 60 of 60 exited, at loads 13.8 and 14.4.
- The interrupt answered in 10–40 ms. fieldd's `onSessionExited` heard the pane 5–27 ms after it, and the row read
  exited 112–194 ms after it.
- So on a quiet floor the ^C, the PTY and the floor's `session-exited` all work. The ~110 ms between heard and
  exited is `closeRun`.

**The read:**
- `closeRun` awaited puppeteer's `handleProcessExit` before it stamped the record, held the exited row, logged
  `session_exited` and published.
- puppeteer-runtime 0.3.0's `closeManaged` (`runtime.ts:1941` at `d0aa1224e`) does its synchronous part first: it
  dispatches `process:exited` and marks the run terminal. Then it awaits, with no bound:
  - the controller's dispose;
  - the terminal claim;
  - `finalizeWorkspace`. Its git calls, `diff`, `rev-parse`, `status` and the rest, are each
    `execFile("git", …)` with no timeout (`packages/workspaces/src/git.ts:23-24`).
- On this Mac `git` is `/usr/bin/git`, the xcrun shim: 12.3 ms a call against 4.8 ms for the CLT binary. That is the
  ~110 ms, and it puts no rosettad ingest on the path. A loaded host can hold those forks far longer.

**Red-first** (records `logs/row-A-2b01c8144`, `logs/row-B-dac1c5bac`, `logs/diag`; VF-PM's GO 02:58Z and 03:02Z):
- **Scaffold A** (main's runtime): a row puts a `git` that sleeps on PATH after `joinedRow` and before the interrupt.
  RED in 7630 ms: no exited within 5 s, and the log ends `+2517 fieldd.agents.interrupted`. This is the lost shape
  exactly.
- **Scaffold B** (the honest state): `fieldd.agents.exit_heard` at the exit handler's entry, and
  `fieldd.agents.exit_cleanup_slow` while a cleanup is still pending past `AGENT_EXIT.CLEANUP_WARN_MS` (2 s). RED in
  7678 ms at the same assertion. Its log ends `+2532 interrupted · +2533 exit_heard reason="signaled" · +4533
  exit_cleanup_slow`: **C3**.
- **The diagnostic** (lane-only, at B): the in-process `onSessionExited` heard the pane at +7 ms. `exit_heard` came
  at +7, `exit_cleanup_slow` at +2007, and `session_exited` at +5071, just after the row killed the stalled git.
  fieldd hears the exit at once, and the close is held exactly as long as the cleanup.

**The fix** (`8d56b2bd8`, the lane's A+B+C+D squashed, rebased onto `db12d0939` as an identical patch):
- `closeRun` starts `handleProcessExit` and publishes the exit fact without waiting for the cleanup.
- The cleanup's promise is kept in `exitCleanups`, keyed by run. A paneless run's cleanup still gates a resume.
- The row reads `resumable: false` until the cleanup ends, because the old run's lease covers the final git
  observation (`runtime.ts:1875`). The cleanup's end publishes.
- `agent.resume` waits for the cleanup at most `AGENT_EXIT.RESUME_CLEANUP_WAIT_MS` (5 s; `registries.ts`, contracts
  first). Then it refuses PRECONDITION_FAILED, retryable, `{runtimeRunId, state: "finalizing"}`.
- The AR-D25 persona sweep runs at the cleanup's end.
- `closeRun`'s callers still await the cleanup.
- **Rows:**
  - the stall row: exited at once, not resumable, heard, warned;
  - the resume row: waits, `finalizing`, then goes through once the stall ends;
  - MF-1f's held-pane row polls for `resumable`.
  - floorEvidence names `pendingMs`.
- **Unchanged:** `runContinuing` skips exiting entries, so a resume of the same conversation through another record
  is not held by the old cleanup.

**Upstream:** PU-G (drafted, not filed; records `PU-G-puppeteer-bounded-exit-finalization.md`) asks for three things:
- a bound on each workspace git call (`GIT_TIMEOUT`);
- a bound on the exit's finalization as a whole, or a split close;
- an observable release of the lease.
It moves to `draft/petitions/` in the next draft queue. The workaround retires when PU-G lands in an EL8.

## TS-4b — the approval line on the claims strip (TS-D20 = A, TS-D20b = A): "It waited 14m for you." as a long approval clears, behind the limit moment (2026-10-29; `257af5f6f`, lane `ts/4-asking-again`)

**What.** TS-4b is TS-4's second packet: D20's line after an approval that waited more than ten minutes, the
`approval-wait` place of TS-4a's ledger. D20 (ruled A 01:01:59.983Z) put it "on Godview's agent row". TS-4b's code
read found that row is puppeteer's: the views draw it through `MonitorViewHost`, and the views SDK lends its host no
place on a row. The place went back to James as TS-D20b (02:38Z, `rule-ts-d20b-host`). He ruled it, D19 and D21 at
03:57:49Z, typed in TS's session: "ok, go with your lean". VF-PM recorded them on the board as his.
- **The watch** (`account/approval-wait.ts`):
  - `ApprovalWaits.observe(rows)` remembers each approval (`wait.kind: "permission"`) that an agent of this Mac's is
    blocked on. It answers the ones that cleared after more than ten minutes, timed by the backend's own clocks (the
    wait's `since`, then the next state's `statusSince`, or a new wait's own start).
  - A wait it never saw waiting says nothing, so a launch is never the moment. A run that ended while it waited, or a
    row that left, says nothing. The longest is first.
  - `approvalWaitOpen` is the nudge's gate: this Mac in the ordinary unconnected state, the switch read and on, and
    TS-4a's `connectAskOpen(ledger, "approval-wait", now)`. `approvalWaitStands` keeps the line until its row moves
    or leaves.
- **The row** (`godview/ApprovalWaitMoment.tsx`, `ApprovalWaitCard` controller-free), in the limit moment's chrome:
  - the agent's own mark (`AgentIcon`, as the views draw an agent) and its project;
  - "It waited 14m for you." (1h 12m past the hour);
  - "Your phone can show and answer requests like this one." in the muted ink;
  - **Connect your devices** (`open-connect`) and × (Not now, which writes nothing more and leaves by the retract's
    fade, 180 ms; none under Reduce Motion).
  - Its controller says it once per window, written `connect-ask:approval-wait` asked before it shows. A refused
    write keeps the window's quiet.
- **The strip says one moment, the limit moment first** (`godview/ClaimsStripMoment.tsx`, the overlay's `moment`):
  - the limit moment tells it whether it shows (`onShown`, a layout effect, before paint);
  - while it shows, the approval line is `held`: a wait that clears then is not said, and a line already said stands
    aside until the strip is free;
  - the monitor lends the moment its unfiltered rows (`MonitorMomentRowsContext`, beside the account facts), so the
    moment opens no feed of its own.
- **TS-D19 = A needs no code.** TS-4a's rows (the status item's, the ghost rows) never read the switch; the away
  notice and the approval line do.
- **Catalog:** Godview's "The approval line" specimen, the shipping card over the shipping watch's fixture (its agent

  - James's three rulings as a dated sub-bullet: the switch stops the nudges and not the rows; the line sits on the
    claims strip; Publish's choice of where to open is deferred until a Publish offers one;
  - an as-built sub-bullet.

## WP8 — item 113: the packaged-resources guard reads the test's own disk, never the host's installed app (2026-10-29; `218dc3d9e`, lane `fix/item113-resources-readers`; VF-PM's slot 18:04Z)

**What happened:** TS-6's verify on the Mac mini went red at 17:59:53Z on one row, with everything else green:
`packages/electron-shell/test/resources.test.ts` "never silently falls back to a development path when packaged". It
blocked every mini run, so it was the queue's first landing.

**The cause:**
- The row called `assertPackagedResources(pkg)` with no readers, so the defaults (`headOf`, `textOf` in
  `src/main/resources.ts`) read the HOST's `/Applications/VibeField.app/Contents/Resources`.
- Where no VibeField is installed (James's Mac), nothing was there and the row threw, as it claims. On the mini, where
  it is installed, fieldd and field-native were there for its architecture, the assertion accepted, and the row's
  `toThrow` failed.
- The row's premise, "nothing on disk at those paths", was the host's installation rather than the test's.

**The fix, test only** (one file, +18/−1):
- The row injects `nodeArch`, `readHead` and `readText`, in the neighbours' shape. Nothing is at the packaged paths,
  and a whole development tree is under REPO (heads and texts present), so a search into the checkout would find one.
- It asserts the refusal it means: a `ResourceError` with `fieldd-bundle-missing` at `pkg.fielddCommand`, rather than
  any ResourceError.
- Read and unchanged: the development-layout row (`assertPackagedResources(dev)`, no readers) touches no disk, because
  `resources.ts:378` returns before any read when `!resources.packaged`. Were that early return to regress, the
  defaults would read `/Users/dev/…` paths no host has, and the row would go red on every host.

**Validation:**
- James's Mac (no installed app), each row alone at nice 19: biome on the file, the electron-shell typecheck, and the
  resources suite 30/30, all exit 0.
- The control, since this Mac cannot show the red: the row's readers mutated to report present binaries and a valid
  identity at every path. The assertion then runs the neighbours' checks through (rosettad, the capture pair, the
  trust anchor) and accepts, so exactly 1 of 30 went red, this row, for "expected a ResourceError". The mutation was
  restored and sha-checked.
- The mini, the red-first host (the row as on main red there at 17:59:53Z): run 0 at `218dc3d9e`, `pnpm verify` exit 0
  at 18:15:04Z through the Rust tests and gen:check, the resources suite 30 passed with the installed app present (the
  mini's log :1351, read by VF-PM).

**Landed:** main fast-forwarded `e23fa8a1f` → `218dc3d9e` at 18:17:43Z on VF-PM's GO (18:17Z), after the four checks;
the porcelain empty after. Not pushed (James's click).

**Lesson:** a test that claims "nothing on disk" injects its disk. A default reader makes the host's installation the
premise, and the row passes or fails by machine.

- Records: `/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/records/item113/`.

## TS-6 — the sync question at the first new field (TS-D13): a new link keeps the fields made before it on this Mac, and New field asks once in the explorer (2026-10-29; `14c74f980`, the merge of main `218dc3d9e` (item 113) into `26b331dbc` on `93916c1c6` and `a58d96a4f`, lane `ts/6-sync-question`)

**What.** D13 moved the sync question out of the Setup Assistant to the first new project after connecting. Taking it out
of setup alone would have synced every field made before the link the moment the link landed, under the default
posture (`automatic`). So TS-6 is two halves: fieldd keeps those fields on this Mac when a sign-in lands, and the head
asks the question when New field is next pressed.
- **The keep** (fieldd):
  - `LinkService`'s `beforeLinked` is awaited at a NEW link only (no login held), after the capture is verified and
    before link.json is written and the linked remount seeds the library. A linked boot, a renewal (expired → linked)
    and a re-verify never run it. A failure is logged and never refuses the link.
  - `oweSyncQuestion` (`sync-question.ts`) owes `sync-question` in the setup ledger first (`SetupLedgerStore.owe`,
    only where no row stands), then sets every field with no answer of its own (`syncIntent` undefined) to `local`
    through the catalog's own `setSyncIntent`. A field sent or kept already is left alone, and so is a system
    document. A refusal on one field is logged and the others are still kept. Nothing is kept once the question is
    answered, and an unreadable newer row stops it.
  - **Contracts:** `owed` joins `SETUP_MOMENT_STATES`. A window's `setup.moment` takes `SetupMomentAnswer` (retired |
    asked), so `owed` is fieldd's alone (PRECONDITION_FAILED). `SYNC_QUESTION_MOMENT`, and the EL9 golden
    `setup-ledger-sync-question.valid.json` (the kit mirrors no setup fixture, so there are no Swift copies). AO's
    lead read the seam first.
- **The question** (field-app):
  - `account/sync-question.ts`: `syncQuestionOwed` (the ledger says `owed`, never a guess), `earlierFields` (the
    fields staying on this Mac), and `useSyncQuestion`, the door ChromeLayer hands to Head. Head itself runs without a
    provider in its tests and the catalog, and there New field never asks.
  - `frame/Head.tsx`: New field asks while the question is owed. The answer runs in order: the fields added are sent
    through the manager, then the posture is set and the moment retired, then the field is made. A posture that does
    not land keeps the question and makes nothing. Cancel makes nothing and leaves it owed. Closing the explorer, or an
    answer from elsewhere, closes it.
  - `frame/SyncQuestionView.tsx` is controller-free, behind HeadView's new `question` prop, with the tiles `hidden`
    beneath it. One `account/PostureCards.tsx` serves both places: the question and Settings → Devices' New projects.
  - **Setup's posture pane is retired** (`panes/PosturePane.tsx`, `views/posture.tsx`, the catalog's frame 07). A
    linked user goes from the name to Setting up, and Connect goes to Setting up either way.
  - **Catalog:** the head's plate "The sync question" (Design System → Chrome → the head), the shipping HeadView on
    fixture props.
- **DESIGN.md** §8, at its source: the bullet "The sync question" (between Settings → Devices and Asking again), and one
  dated line in the explorer's New field paragraph.
- **The rulings:**
  - VF-PM 05:13Z, derived from D13, with James told and free to overrule: a Mac whose link was captured before TS-6
    keeps what it syncs and is never asked;
  - James on VF-PM's board, `ts6-sync-question-words` 05:37:09Z, "all four as drafted" (the title, the voice, the
    list's label, the acts Cancel and New field);
  - and `ts6-sync-question-noun` 05:37:06Z, "projects (the cards word)", the sheet's voice throughout. New field is the
    head's act and stays.

**Found:**
- **Retiring the pane alone would have been a privacy regression.** Every field made before the link had no intent of
  its own and followed the `automatic` default, so connecting would have carried it away unasked. The keep has to run
  before the linked remount seeds the library (`daemon.ts`'s linked change), so it hangs on the capture, not on a
  ledger read later.
- **"New link" is "no login held".** The first guard (`state !== "linked"`) would have run on a renewal (expired →
  linked) and kept fields a person had already been asked about.
- **A field made while owed by a path other than New field** (a paste, a template, a plugin's create) follows the
  posture until the question is answered. Owed on TS's list.
- **biome's stdin route** (VF-PM 08:07Z, from the iOS lane): `ts6-light.sh` now checks that every non-ASCII character a
  modified file held at the base is still there. The one deliberate removal is named: the retired specimen's arrow.

**Validation.**
- **The lane:** the edits in `/Volumes/SamsungRed/lanes/ts6` (worktree off `e23fa8a1f`, which was still main's head, so
  there was no rebase). The runs were in ts3's run lane, detached at each sha (its own target `rust/ts3`, rosetta-pin
  and mille-pin at the lock's pins), at nice 19 under the guard.
- **Red first** (`ts6-light.sh red`, 08:29:34–08:30:06Z) at `a58d96a4f`: fieldd's `sync-question.integration` file 1
  failed and 4 passed, the keep row alone.
- **The light pass** (`ts6-light.sh green`): the first run at `4b51c069e` (08:30:06–08:31:50Z) was red on two rows of the

## AL-8a — item 94: a crash's count that does not come in time says why — the floor names each owed cell's pump (2026-10-29; `148f2dff0`, in the stack's merge `0b4cb2ff0`)

**What happened:** TS-4b's second verify (load ~216) read AL-8a-4's record of a crash as `{sessions: null}`. The floor
had held the hello's ack for its whole bounded wait (`FRESH_COUNT_WAIT`, 2 s, AL-8a's ruling of 2026-10-27) and sent
unknown, AL-8a's honest answer. But it logged nothing, so the null could not say whether the bound met a slow floor or
a cell that never heard the ask.

**The fix:**
- field-native `orphan.rs`: `fresh_count` takes what it counts for (`CountFor`: a departure with the record's `at`, or
  the bound's confirming read). At its deadline it logs `field_native.lifecycle.manager_count_unknown {count_for,
  at_ms, waited_ms, why, cells}`. `why` is one word: `slow` when every owed cell was mid-work, `unheard` when a cell
  sat idle from before the moment without hearing the ask, `dialing` when a cell was being dialed.
- `terminal.rs`: each cell's stamp records when its pump last heard an ask (`heard`) and last went idle (`settled`).
  `InventoryStamp::not_fresh` classifies a cell as reconciling, tick_late, dialing or unheard.
- The bound is unchanged at 2 s, and no contract changes: the record still says `sessions: null`.
- fieldd's kill matrix: AL-8a-4 and AL-8a-2 hold the law through `expectCountedOrSlow`. `sessions` is 1, or null WITH
  the floor's own `manager_count_unknown` for this departure saying `slow`. A 0, a bare null and an `unheard` null are
  red.

**Red-first** by mutation, restored byte-identical (`records/item94/plan.md`): M1 (the ask arm holds the pump 4 s)
reddens the old rows on a null while the new rows read `slow`; M3 (M1 without the give-up line) is red on a bare null;
M2 (the record says `Some(0)`) is red under both; MC (an idle cell classified `tick_late`) reddens the two
`terminal.rs` rows.

## FN — item 86: a health or observed send between a subscription's reading and its baseline reaches fieldd — the receiver is taken first (2026-10-29; `bca8aa778`, in the stack's merge `0b4cb2ff0`)

**The cause:**
- `native.lifecycle.health.subscribe` and `.observed.subscribe` (`mgmt/mod.rs`) read the Sender's value for the
  result, sent it, then handed the forwarder `subscribe()`, which marks seen whatever the channel holds by then. A
  send from another worker thread in between was never forwarded. That window is microseconds, unless a loaded host
  preempts the thread.
- Both streams are state transfer, so the next send or a reconnect repaired it. Until then fieldd held the old
  terminal inventory, or missed a mesh node-up subscribed while the units come up (item 85's timing). Named at item 85
  (`7eda2ee38`) and left for its own item.

**The fix,** in the shape the file already had three times (routes since item 85, `freeway.state`,
`diagnostics::subscribe`): one helper, `subscription_reading(&mut rx)`, reads the receiver the forwarder will hold
with `borrow_and_update` before the result is sent. Health and observed take the receiver first; `freeway.state` goes
through it with no change. The two "Noted 2026-10-28" comments are dated corrections at their source.

**The row:** `a_send_after_a_subscriptions_reading_is_still_owed_to_its_forwarder`, a plain `#[test]`. Its Probe
value's `Serialize` sends the next value between the reading and the forwarder's hold. Red-first by mutation (I86, the
old order): `has_changed` is false, red; restored, green.

## GV — item 90: the GV-D1 swarm row solves the 600 steps it names — its loop counts the world's steps, not the frames (2026-10-29; `8a1d08d03`, in the stack's merge `0b4cb2ff0`)

**The finding (item 89):** the row's settle, 600 frames of `now += 1000 / 30`, solved 599 steps.

**The cause:**
- It is the world's own accumulator. `SwarmPhysics.advance` (puppeteer-views 0.3.0, `world.js:327–347`) adds the
  clamped delta and subtracts a rounded `stepMs` per step, so it loses the epsilon itself.
- Simulated alone (`records/item90/acc90.mjs`): main's sum solves 599, and so does a time counted from the frame
  number. So item 89's named remedy, "counting frames instead of summing time", would not have worked. Item 89's entry
  carries a dated correction at its source, in this commit.
- It is not a product fault: a live driver hands continuous time, and the epsilon is caught up the next frame.

**The fix, test only:** `settleCrowd` advances until the world has solved 600 steps (601 frames) and returns `solved`.
The row asserts 600 for both settles; the crowd's assertions and the 15 s budget are unchanged.

**Red-first** (I90): main's `frame < 600` loop under the new assertions is red at 599; restored, green. Deterministic:
float arithmetic, no clock.

## B4 — item 96, its first half: the launch rows play FieldView whole — a board is ready on the desk's present, never on the 2.5 s fallback (2026-10-29; `8d5254747`, in the stack's merge `0b4cb2ff0`)

**What reddened:** `doc-manager.test.ts`'s first-run row ran 2.9–4.8 s in nine full verifies and crossed vitest's 5 s
default twice: the EL8's r2 at 5257 ms, and TS-4b's verify4b-1 at load 663.

**The cause:** `contentApplied` → `presentStage` → `waitForCanvasPresentation` waits for `canvasPresented` or
`CANVAS_PRESENT_TIMEOUT_MS` (2500). The harness played `contentApplied` alone, so every wait for ready sat out the
fallback: one apply ≈ 3 s, three ≈ 8–9.5 s. The product calls `canvasPresented` one frame after the arrival framing
(`use-workspace-session.ts:493`), so this was harness time, not a product item.

**The fix:** `presented(manager, generation)` plays both reports, and `applyPending` and the remount row use it. The
refused board's row keeps `contentApplied` alone. The first-run row says ready arrives in the present's own turn,
never on the timer.

**Red-first** (I96, the helper without `canvasPresented`): red ("loading"); restored, green. Timed alone, the fix
against main's file: first run 313 against 2825 ms, the field-report flow 712 against 8216, the whole file 14 s
against 74 s.

**Its own half, queued:** the parts alone ×N and on CI; which of the 13 bare `30_000` rows keep a named constant; and
the one row still past a second ("a window whose OWN board another window holds", 1667 ms).

## DK-18 — item 93: the launcher's census reads the whole process table once — every later look asks one pid at a time; the launcher rows get their named budget (2026-10-29; `d50b972dd`, in the stack's merge `0b4cb2ff0`)

**What reddened:** `smoke-profile.test.ts`'s launcher rows overran vitest's 5 s default in loaded verifies. The LEFT
row (:114) went red four times since 10-20 (5126–9144 ms, the last at `8d5254747`, load ~400), and the profile row
(:189) once (6432 ms at `ec7899a4f`).

**The cause:**
- The census (`apps/desktop/packaging/smoke-daemons.mjs`) read the WHOLE table twice per look: once with every
  environment (`ps -axww -E`) and once plain. Every re-look was a whole look, so the LEFT row made four or more whole
  reads.
- Measured (10-29 08:05Z, 1244 processes): the `-E` table 152 ms, the plain one 92 ms, `-p <one pid>` 3–4 ms. A `-p`
  naming two or more pids takes 204–216 ms, because macOS reads the whole table again.

**The fix:**
- The first look reads the `-E` table ONCE to find the run by its mark and names each found pid by its own command
  line. Every re-look asks `ps -ww -E -o … -p <pid>` per known pid.
- The mark guard is kept: a pid counts only while its environment carries the run's mark. `ps`'s exit 1 for its one
  pid reads as gone.
- The LEFT row makes one whole read where it made four. `runProcesses` is unchanged for its callers.

**The budget:** `LAUNCHER_ROW_BUDGET_MS` = 15 s for the three rows (item 85's and 89's shape). It is more than 1.6
times the worst any row took in 121 logged runs since 10-20; the LEFT row's median was 2201 ms, its p90 3568, with
four reds up to 9144.

**Red-first, a count:** `tooling/dev-runner/test/smoke-daemons-census.test.mjs` counts the reads through an injected
`ps`. With main's census both rows fail: "the whole table was read 4 times" against 1, and 4 against 0.

**Kept out, its own item:** electron-shell's twin `stopRunDaemons` (`src/testing/smoke-daemons.ts`), which reads the
whole table twice per 100 ms poll.

## AR — item 92: the fake rosettad's late words come from a helper already running, and the rows they trail run under bounds wide of its wake (2026-10-29; `7af99678b`, in the stack's merge `0b4cb2ff0`)

**The reds:** item 87's verify at `8d56b2bd8` and TS-4a's, where "an older binary whose words trail its exit is
TERMINAL at once" spawned the binary three times; and the stack's rerun at `ec7899a4f` (load 362), where the crash row
read "its stderr still open after 1000 ms".

**The cause is the fake, not the supervisor:** `sayThenExit` under `FAKE_ROSETTAD_LATE_STDERR_MS` spawned a `node -e`
at the exit, so a node boot rode the trail. Past `STDERR_DRAIN_MS` the supervisor rightly composes a crash.

**The fix:**
- A `/bin/sh` helper (`LATE_SH`; Windows keeps a node on the same protocol, `LATE_NODE`) says it is running before the
  fake exits, takes the exit as its stdin's EOF, and writes the words after.
- `LATE_DRAIN` (`STDERR_DRAIN_MS` 5 s, `STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` 6 s) is named by the three trailing-words rows. The
  product's bounds are unchanged.
- The fake's comment carries a dated correction: the 07:41Z rerun falsified "exactly the delay the rows name".

**Red-first found the second bound.** M92 holds the helper's wake 1.5 s. At today's bounds it is red 3/3. With the
drain raised alone it is still red 3/3, on "did not become ready in time", the startup bound. With `LATE_DRAIN` it is
green 3/3; as committed, green, the file 32/32.

## AR-6 — item 101: item 87's stall rows wait for the interrupted exit on the heard exit's own budget, its witness beside it (2026-10-29; `a2cf1b76a`, in the stack's merge `0b4cb2ff0`)

**The reds,** both at TS-6 on James's Mac: its verify at `26b331dbc`, and its rerun inside his quiet window, where the
load still went 18 → 471. The two stalled-cleanup rows ran out "the exited row … did not hold within 5000 ms" (6666
and 6134 ms), last reading `persisted: true, resumable: false`.

**The read:** it is the same interrupt-to-exited WAIT as AR-6-0's (`INTERRUPTED_EXIT_MS`, 15 s), so one exit had three
budgets. What the rows prove (item 87) is that the exit is published before the cleanup ends, and the cleanup cannot
end inside the row: the git sleeps `STALLED_GIT_MS` (30 s, now named). The 5 s was a guess at the heard exit's speed,
never the property's bound.

**The change, test only:** both waits take `INTERRUPTED_EXIT_MS` and `exitWitness(box, pane)`. The `exit_heard` check
stays, so a backstopped `unknown` never passes as a heard exit.

**Measured:** across 15 verify logs, the two rows ran 6240–11716 and 2852–6724 ms over 30 row-runs, one red each.
Alone ×3 at load 37–44, all green.

## FG-2 — the returning tear: a returning boot's splash stands its floor, its words go, and the field tears open onto the desk as it settles in; every boot is handed over before it is interactive (FG-D9 A, FG-D10 B, FG-D11 A, FG-L6) (2026-10-29; `07618ca61`, lane `fg/build`, in `fg/land`'s merge `ffe9d9b40`)

**What.**
- **The machine** (`boot/machine.ts`): once the desk is frame-stable, EVERY boot holds at `handing-over` until its
  first face hands it over (`revealDesk`). So `interactive` still means revealed, and AO-D2's `revealHeld` retires.
  - A hand-over given early is kept.
  - The release exists before the patch that notifies.
  - Before the hold comes the floor: the splash stands 700ms from `start()` (the website's `SPLASH.again`). A hidden
    window skips it.
- **BootRoot is the one decider.** A returning boot's splash opens by the TEAR where the field is live, motion is
  allowed and the window is seen. Otherwise it opens by the base reveal's FADE, at once.
  - The choice is made once and never cancelled by a later render.
  - The Setup Assistant hands over at its own last beat (FG-5 brings it to the tear).
  - A switch's arrival hands over at once.
- **The tear**, in order:
  - The words go first (240ms, the website's `wordsOut`), taking the ground's colour with them under the live canvas.
  - Then `FieldHandle.tear(dark)` (`FieldLayer`'s `handleRef`) reveals the website's look: `TEAR = { duration: 1900,
    markFade: .24, rim: .5, tear: .3 }`, with the daylight `[1, .955, .87]` by day and no ink by night.
  - It is bounded at 2.9 s, and a failed reveal settles at once.
  - Once open, the door is destroyed at once. Not open, the field leaves with the ground's fade (the website's
    `.is-fading`).
- **The desk** stays at `.99` under the splash, as before. At the tear's words it goes, unseen, to `.985` and
  `brightness(1.16)`, then settles with the tear (1900ms island, 1500ms `ease-out`) and is still as the tear resolves.
  The fade, the first run and the switch keep the base reveal byte for byte.
- **The smokes** (`electron-shell/src/testing/smoke.ts`): `bootRevealed` waits for `vf:renderer:interactive` after
  DESK_READY in the twelve places that press or shoot (below).
- **DESIGN.md** §8 "The reveal" gains its as-built paragraph.

**Found:**
- **The smokes pressed on the splash.** VF-PM's condition had every smoke's boot wait read before the commit.
  - Every smoke's boot is a returning one.
  - Against FG-1, a tearing boot's `interactive` comes later by the floor's excess (0–700ms) plus about 2.14 s, and
    by at most 3.84 s at the bound. A fading boot's comes later by the floor's excess alone.
  - CANVAS_READY and DESK_READY are said before the reveal, so no marker wait moved. But DESK_READY is said beneath
    the splash.
  - smoke:canvas pressed inside the new window in three places: first-load's TIDY and DOWN-GONE (`select()`, about
    1–2 s after a reload's DESK_READY); PT-1's pegboard after the retry row's reload; and the two peer openers
    (DESK_READY + 800ms).
  - The fix is the harness's, at the cause: wait for the reveal law's own mark, bounded at 30 s with the marks seen in
    its diagnosis, never a sleep.
  - The per-smoke reading is in the commit body. smoke:plugin-restart reads only doors and counters. The GPU-less
    smokes and no-webgpu take the fade. The godview smokes' first act after a boot is a key, which the splash never
    held. studio, update and profile wait on DOM presence or on main.
- `mount.tsx` is the machine's only host and BootRoot its only face. So no path waits at `handing-over` for a
  hand-over nobody gives.

**What.** AP-D3 (the phone's face) was built on 2026-09-23 as a lean, "the face dealt once per login from the first
self desktop's user ULID until `user.me` (IOS-8f)", and ruled at it on 2026-10-28 (the housekeeping page, Q14).
IOS-8f builds its end state. VF-PM took its seven leans on 2026-10-29 at 07:26Z. Eight commits on `e23fa8a1f`, 26
files, +1154 −15:
- **(a) `44d649776`: the face deal, pinned on every plane.** `packages/contracts/fixtures/face-deal.vector.json` holds
  the 48 faces in order, five hashes, six deals and three rosters, generated from the TypeScript and checked back.
  Contracts' `user-face.test.ts` and the kit's `FaceDealVectorTests` read it. A `check:ios-fixtures` row holds the
  kit's copy byte-identical (`FieldDesignTests` gains `resources: [.copy("Fixtures")]`).
- **(b) `94c59122f`: contracts' `user.me`.** A product method: scope `workspace.read` (the roster's), idempotent,
  local. Its result is `UserMeResult {userId, name?, face, dealt}`, with two goldens (a written coin with a name; the
  deal with none) and the TS-only `USER_ME` UNAVAILABLE {service: "user", state: "no-user"}. `pnpm gen` regenerates
  nothing, because `users.ts` is TS-only.
- **(c) `35cb5e360`: fieldd answers from its own user row.** `user-me.ts` reads `users.json` at each ask from
  `config.vibefieldRoot` and answers the row as Electron main's roster shows it (`effectiveFaces`). With no row, file
  or root, it answers the phone's own deal, `dealFace(userId, [])`, with no name. An unreadable file is warned, never
  thrown; no user is an honest UNAVAILABLE. It is registered beside `device.list`.
- **(d) `933a22c82`: the kit reads it.** A tolerant `UserMeResult` in `ProductShapes.swift`, tested over the
  contracts' own goldens (mirrored by a `check:ios-fixtures` row).
- **(e) `3c68ed542`: the phone asks its home.** `FieldLink.askHomeForPerson()` asks the HOME once per connection,
  beside the catalog ask and never of an owner door, and the answer rides the home's row (`FieldDesktop.person`).
  NOT_FOUND (a desktop older than the door) and UNAVAILABLE leave the deal standing; a retryable failure is asked
  again on the sweep's clock.
- **(f) `b9de1bd47`: the corner wears it.** `AccountFaceStore.adopt` lets the home's answer replace a deal or an
  earlier home's word, and keeps the name per login, forgotten at sign-out. A nameless answer keeps the name, an
  unknown frame is a sticker (UA-D17), and a deal still never moves a kept face. The deal is now only the fallback
  until a home answers.
- **`0e004bafe`, the pre-compile review's two:** a bare ⚠ that biome's stdin had turned into "!" in
  `user-face.test.ts` is a ⚠ again, now written as an escape, and fieldd's face is copied to its wire type
  (TS2322). **`d3f566322`:** `USER_ME` moves below `PROJECT_DOORS`, whose doc block it had taken.

**Found:**

  > **Correction (2026-10-31, at the draft queue's read):** the fact stands, but "it never lints" was found on FG-2's
  > drafts (2026-10-29 12:40Z), not by IOS-8f, which found the U+26A0 rewrite alone (`0e004bafe`).

**What.** B2 is the first batch the window shows. Its order is LC-30's, so no commit names a page that does not
exist yet.
- **AU-3a (`571d81079`): a desktop says which VibeField it runs.**
  - contracts: `DeviceSlice` and `DeviceInfo` gain an optional, tolerant `appVersion` (`.optional().catch(undefined)`,
    the VERSION_CHARS bound). An older peer says none, and a malformed one drops alone, never the slice (LC-20).
    `appVersionOfBuildId` reads WP12 D10's `<appVersion>+<commit7>`; a dev build id names none.
  - fieldd: `selfSlice()` publishes it, the roster row carries it, and `narrowDeviceSlice` copies it (without that,
    intake strips every peer's). `emitRoster`'s change signature includes it, so a desktop that updates in place
    reaches an open page.
  - `compareDotted` and `compareSemver` move from decide.ts into contracts' `update-policy.ts` as
    `compareDottedVersions` and `compareReleaseVersions`, with no alias (X24).
  - New fixtures `device-slice.app-version.json` and `device-info.app-version.json`. The iOS-mirrored goldens are
    untouched, so the kit owes no copy, and gen does not run.
- **AU-3 (`0706b1b76`): Settings → Updates** (AU-D8).
  - The card leaves General for a page of its own, first in Support (Updates · Diagnostics · Advanced), wearing
    `reset`. Its nav row wears a 6 px cyan mark while an install waits, with words for assistive tech.
  - The head: "VibeField", the exact version in mono with Copy, and the channel's word.

    off) · Download anyway (skipped). Download goes through AU-1's door, and a refusal says main's words or a composed

## AU B3 — the menus, the move and the quit: the app menu's About, Settings… ⌘, and its update item, and the status item's update image (AU-4); Move to Applications through the quit gate (AU-7); a signal skips the quit gate in every build, a fault older than AU (AU-5a); and a person's quit installs a staged update after the gate's stop (AU-5) (AU-D9, AU-D12; AU-G3, AU-G8, AU-G9, AU-G14) (2026-10-30; `20783c656`, the merge of main `1de84540b` into `a4688b7c9` on `cbd6e15e5` on `2cfaa1f96` on `7b2cd0db6`, lane `au/b3`)

**What.** The order is LC-27's: install on quit is born with the read-only and pending-move guards beneath it.
- **AU-4 (`7b2cd0db6`): the menus say it too** (AU-D12).
  - The status item: `updateMenuEntry` is the one update item both menus wear (AU-L4). A found update that was not
    skipped, with automatic updates off, reads "Download Update" (no ellipsis: it asks nothing, LC-41) and downloads
    that version through AU-1's door. Check for Updates… keeps its ellipsis for now (LC-52, the lead's call; whether to
    drop it is open for James).
  - Its image: `trayImageKind` gains `update` for a staged update with an apply wired. Attention keeps one meaning, a
    degraded service or a failed check, and outranks it. A staged update with no apply wears the base image (it wore
    attention).
  - The art: four images (`fieldUpdateTemplate.png` and `@2x`, `field-update.ico`, `field-linux-update.png`) generated
    from `tray-master.svg` by `generate-icons.mjs`: the mark with one plain dot, no bang. The lead generated them in
    B3's slot at 12:03:40Z, looked at them at 16 px on a light and a dark bar (LC-32), and folded them into AU-4;
    `b3-slot.log` checks that the committed bytes are the ones looked at. No image of the look is kept.
  - The app menu (darwin) is spelled out: About · Settings… ⌘, · the update item · Services · Hide, Hide Others, Show
    All · Quit. Settings… registers ⌘,, but the page answers it first in its capture phase (GT-D21), so the chord keeps
    one owner, and the item's click reveals Settings, never toggles. The update item wears the status item's entry.
    About names the version and the commit (`commitOfBuildId`). The Windows and Linux menus are unchanged.
  - No ⌘, smoke row (LC-28): `sendInputEvent` enters below AppKit's key-equivalent dispatch, so a synthesized ⌘, never
    reaches a menu item. ⌘, through the menu is an owed eyeball.
- **AU-7 (`2cfaa1f96`): Move to Applications** (AU-G8).
  - contracts: `UpdateView.location` (`applications` · `elsewhere` · `read-only`; optional, absent off macOS, and a
    location it does not know is a wire error),
    `UpdateMoveResult`, and `IPC_CHANNELS.updateMoveToApplications`, the ninth update door; four EL9 fixtures.
  - main: `updates/location.ts` classifies once per process (App Translocation, then `isInApplicationsFolder`, then
    the parent's W_OK). A read-only copy checks only when a person asks, downloads nothing, and refuses a staged
    Restart as `location` before the census, so it no longer ends sessions for nothing before Squirrel refuses.
  - The move goes through the quit gate (`quitThen`): `app.moveToApplicationsFolder` runs only after the durable close
    and a COMPLETE stop, and an existing copy in Applications goes to the Trash. An incomplete or failed stop, a quit
    with no gate, or a mover that refuses or throws relaunches in place, logged `desktop.update.move_failed` (LC-25).
    `QuitGate.stop()` now answers `{kind: done, complete, ended}` or `{kind: aborted}`.
  - The window: the Me row's R5 ("Move to Applications…", "Can't update from here") only for read-only; the page's
    read-only state in the attention ink, with the move as its primary; "elsewhere" is one quiet line with the move as a
    secondary act.
- **AU-5a (`cbd6e15e5`): a signal skips the quit gate in every build. The fault is older than AU.**
  - LC-26's read (2026-10-29 09:18:57Z, a bare Electron 43.1.1 with no handler of ours, `lanes/au/lc26/`): Electron's
    own POSIX handler turns SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP each into an ordinary `app.quit()` (before-quit → will-quit →
    quit). AL-4's handler ran only under `MODE === "dev"`, so in production a signal met the census gate as ⌘Q would and
    could stop the pairs, against ESR §7.3 as amended.
  - AU-5a moves `dev-signals.ts` to `signal-quit.ts`: a mode-free `installSignalQuit`, installed beside the lifecycle in
    every build, with SIGHUP added.
  - Folded in from B3's quit-seam review (`quitForSignal`, LC-50): a signal that lands while the gate's box is up is
    not the person's quit, whatever the box answers, and stops nothing. During the stop's re-ask box, a signal still
    quits on its Cancel, while "Quit and end N sessions" finishes the stop already under way. Before, the box swallowed
    the signal's quit: Cancel left `restarting` set for the session, with the handler's own latch already tripped, so
    every later SIGINT or SIGTERM was ignored (the handler caught only those two) and the person's next ⌘Q skipped the
    gate and stopped nothing; and "Quit and end N sessions" stopped the pairs under a signal. Dev had this since AL-4.
  - AL's own LANDED entry ("Which quits skip the gate") now carries both faults as a dated correction; their design
    source, `thinking-app-lifecycle.md` AL-F11 and §5.7, was corrected on 2026-10-29 (dev-local `1d91b1bbd`).
- **AU-5 (`a4688b7c9`): install on quit** (AU-D9, AU-G3).
  - One step between the gate's stop and the native quit (`installThenQuit`): after a COMPLETE stop of a quit that is
    still the person's, `installOnQuit` stages the update (`apply.stage`, bounded at 30 s), with no relaunch and no
    `quitAndInstall`. `autoInstallOnAppQuit` stays forced off.
  - It is skipped, logged `desktop.update.quit_install_skipped {why}`, on a signal, an update's armed quit, the OS
    ending the session (AL-D6) and an incomplete stop. A waiting move runs in its place (LC-25). A second ⌘Q or a signal
    during the stage is absorbed: one stop, one install.
  - One hold list, in order: busy, not staged, no apply built, `location`, then the silent holds (disabled, declined,
    confirmation-required, LC-24). Then a fresh policy read bounded at 3 s, and the levers.
  - The quit box's last line, "The Oct 28 nightly installs as you quit." (LC-36), shows only for a person's quit whose
    census box shows, and never while a move pends.
  - A policy hold at the quit is said by the next launch's OUTCOME row (`QUIT_HELD`, LC-14), with no new enum value.
    field-app's not-applied words lead "The last quit didn't install …" for a quit.
  - `smoke:update` gains a sixth run, quit, which is OPT-IN (`--runs quit`, LC-29). desk-gates row 30 says so.

**Found while building** (the record's §11.2, §11.4–§11.6):
- The two faults AU-5a corrects (above).
- A queued quit leaked between tests (B3's light pass, run 2; the harness's fault, not the product's). The lifecycle
  queues its quits (`setImmediate(() => app.quit())`), and every rig in `lifecycle.test.ts` shares one mocked
  `app.quit`. Vitest's step between tests yields no macrotask, so a quit still queued fired into the next test's rig,
  past its `mockReset`. The fix is the harness's: `drain()` in the quit-gate block's `afterEach` and before each
  mid-test `electron.reset()`. The rule: drain the queue the code under test feeds before a shared mock is reset.
- biome's `noThenProperty` refuses a `then` key even in a fixture, so the smoke's step key is `next`. A long signature
  wraps as the formatter prints it.
- The commit bodies are stale in two ways. AU-4's still says "GENERATOR ONLY: no PNG/ICO bytes are in this commit" and
  that `icons:check` stays red until they are; the images were folded into AU-4 before its light pass, and run 11's

## FG-3a — the Setup Assistant stands in one glass on the field: 880 × 640, fitted as one picture, its material in layers, its steps along its top from TS-6's order alone (FG-L2, FG-L3, FG-D3 A, FG-D22 A, FG-D23 A, FG-D26, FG-D27) (2026-10-30; `e012d1f50`, lane `fg/build`, in the mini's mint `5cc2d1108` over main `12a9a4e4b`)

**What.** FG-3 split at VF-PM's word (13:17Z): 3a is the glass's DOM; 3b, the field drawing it (FG-D24), follows.
- **The glass** (`boot/onboarding/wizard-ui.tsx` + `.css`) is 880 × 640 on every step.
  - It is centred on its ground and scaled as one picture by `glassFit` = min(1, (w − 96)/880, (h − 96)/640), never
    reflowed.
  - Its material is four layers under its contents: shadow, frost, grain and edge.
  - On the field it wears `--vf-wizard-edge`, `--vf-wizard-edge-light`, `--vf-shadow-wizard-field` and the grain.
    The tokens are in `tokens.css`, from DESIGN.md §5.
  - It forms where the splash stood: `--vf-glass-frost` 0 → 1 and `--vf-glass-rise` .985 → 1, 560ms island,
    registered with `@property`. Under reduced motion it is the frost alone, 280ms.
  - Nothing that holds the frost sets opacity, filter or mask (a backdrop root), and a test row holds that.
- **The steps** (FG-D22 A, FG-D23 A) have ONE source, TS-6's `order.ts`.
  - `STEP_OF` maps each pane to its step or none, total by `satisfies Record<Pane, …>`.
  - `stepsOf(variant)` walks `nextPane`, and `topOf(variant)` is the one "top".
  - The band: You · Agents · Profiles · History · Devices · Setting up, done/now/next, `aria-current="step"`. It is
    absent on the welcomes and the chooser, fades in with You (240ms), and fills as you arrive (480ms island).
- **The frame** (FG-L3) is 96/160/40, 560 wide. A pane centres in it, scrolling downward only, until FG-4 lays its
  head, body and foot.
- **Finish setting up's sheet is unchanged** (FG-D26, VF-PM's lean): one size prop on the shell, `glass` | `sheet`.
  The sheet's is today's exact geometry, never fitted, with no band.

## PT-S1 fix — item 119: the pegboard's rows are the lay's lines, not the hangs' tops; a hook and a shelf on one line read as one row, so → and the listbox agree again (2026-10-31; `88bf4605d`, lane `portals/item119-rows` on `bef070265`, in the mini's mint `265325d09` over main `eb3a562ac`; VF-PM's GO 2026-10-30 23:30Z)

**What.**
- The board's specimens (`field/desk/pegboard/pegboard-model.ts`, `boardSpecimens(laid, order, drawer, scroll)`) are
  drawn in the lay's own order: core's `trayHung`, which reads `TrayContent.order`, the types `layTray` placed line by
  line. That is the order ← → walk (ICE's `tray.focus`). A type the lay does not name is left out.
- A specimen's row is the lay's line, numbered from 0. The kernel writes no line into the world, so it is read back
  from that order: a line starts wherever a hang's x falls back, since `layTray` starts each line at the margin.
  `rowStep` (↑ ↓) is unchanged.
- `Pegboard.tsx`'s `drawnSpecimens` passes `trayHung(engine.world)`. `laidOf` is unchanged: the specimens' sibling order
  is not the lay's, since a re-lay appends new ones.
- smoke:canvas's KEYS expectation is untouched (`smoke-pegboard.ts`: → lands on `first.options[1]`).

**Found.**
- **The cause was field-app's.** PT-S1 exposed it and did not make it.
  - `boardSpecimens` keyed a row on the hang's exact top (`row: s.hang.y`) and sorted the listbox's options by it.
  - ICE hangs a line's specimens with their tops together only "as near as their holes allow".
  - PT-S1's phone is the first shelf on line 0. ICE 0.16.0 lays it beside the comment pad's hook, at y 132.52 against
    the hook's 130: 2.52 px apart, so the board read two rows.
  - The listbox went [pad, note, …, phone] while → walked pad → phone. That is run 12's "→ moved the focus to
    vibefield.simulator, not the next specimen desk.note".
- **Found and fixed with it, predating PT-S1 on that desk:** line 1 of `pegboard.test.tsx`'s desk, which has no phone.
  It was measured on `bef070265`'s code with an uncommitted log.
  - main's rows were the pad, the note, the photo, the notebook and the calendar at 130; the minimat and the board at
    450; and the browser pane, a shelf laid first on line 1, alone at 471.42 and listed last.
  - So ↓ from the pad (centre 120) skipped the browser pane right below it (centre 180) and went to the minimat
    (centre 460).
  - With the fix, ↓ lands on the browser pane, row 1. It is the same cause, with one fix.
- **The ring reads back at the CSSOM's grain.** That ↓ row's `expect(ringRect()).toEqual(ringOnFocus())` then went red
  by 3.7e-8 px.
  - A width serializes at six decimals: "213.44498px" for the browser pane's 213.444979…, where the minimat's was a
    round 217px.
  - The four ring checks now share `expectRingOnFocus()`: each edge `toBeCloseTo(…, 5)`, and null where ICE has no
    focus.
  - VF-PM ruled it the unit's float grain, not a wider slack on a judged motion (23:45Z).

**Validation.**

  own `layTray` (1120 px at `DRAWER.pitch` 40).
  - It was green on its precondition: both hangs valid, both on line 0.
  - It was red on the row: "expected 2 to be 1". Log: `lanes/pts/logs/probe119-keys-bef070265.log`.
